review_text: Excellent farm to table food, I was here for a sampler menu and had honeydew carpaccio, fried oysters with watermelon, seared trout, and a desert. To top it all off it was a wonderful day and I sat outside. If I am back on Philly I will definitely come back here again. I am really glad that I happened upon this place.

Oh my gosh their nachos. I've had basically nothing but beef fajita nachos, and that's completely okay with me. They deliver quickly, and it's DELICIOUS. My displacement from Texas is relieved by Taqueria Diana.
Friggin fantastic macarons! Woww!  Worth the price and hype of it all ! Check this place out. Totally worth it!  The vanilla macaron is my favorite. Melts in your mouth ! Fantastic!

This place USED to be awesome - then they changed management & ownership, and have really gone downhill. We have ordered catering for our business numerous times, and everyone at the office complained that the sandwiches weren't that great. So then I went a few more times individually and ordered a few diff things - the chicken cheesesteak is so gross I ended up throwing it all in the garbage! The next time I ordered an Italian sub, and how can you really mess up an Italian sub? Well, they managed to and it had literally NO flavor! I think they changed their orders for meats or something because they taste like garbage! I finally stopped going there as I was wasting almost $9-10 on a SUB, which is outrageously overpriced. Such a shame as they used to be phenomenal...
One of my favorite izakaya in midtown. Nice food and atmosphere. Helpful service is a plus :)

Had lunch there. Was offered a community table and declined due to the fact that those seats didn't have seatbacks. There is lots of bread here, so if you're into the Paleo thing, not a lot of options.  I ordered a salad and asked them to add turkey meat to it, which they obliged. Everything is made fresh, behind the counter in plain view. My salad had awesome dressing in it- maybe blu cheese based. Also, the most phenomenal bacon bits ever. Service was good. Nice job.
Love this place, so much food!!!!

I've ordered from these guys plenty of times. The food and delivery service is great. Lots of options too in their menu. I remember ordering a lamb platter once from here and when I got to eating my lamb, I started to think about that kid's show, "Lambchop," or whatever it is and I started feeling bad? Weirdest experience ever, but I thought that I'd mention that (time for the creepy stares at me now). Anyways, the food here is great. Check them out if you like healthy food that tastes great.

Service was very slow, not sure the waiter was ever a waiter before. Sat waiting for cream for my coffee for 10 minutes. Asked what was on my dessert, waiter did not know. He said sugar but it was a nut rolled in sugar. Food was good - not fab! Presentation of food on plate could of been nicer. For the price $$$$ could of been a step above.

Great staff, great food.  I visit Philly frequently (used to live in the Fairmount neighborhood), and this is really the best Mexican I've had in Philly.  On Saturday I ordered their version of shrimp and grits -- grilled shrimp on tequila-spiked grits.  That dish is perfection.

My first time and I am a convert! Hands down beats some others in the neighborhood. Clean, bright, sleek, inviting room for a quick meal.  Menu boards are a bit confusing but the staff are beyond helpful and friendly. The choices are numerous and the food is soooo fresh. I constructed my own salad bowl and was delighted with the subtle flavorings of the chickpeas, beets and Israeli/Moroccan salad. The falafel is yummy and crisp but not oily. I will definitely be back and pass the word about Abaleh. Next time I will try the juices.

First Post, I am being pro-active against the saying that people are more likely to post a bad review than a good one and giving some of my favorite establishments a nod. Grew up in Windsor since the age of 5, my grandfather and father before me swear by this place, and so do I. I am what you would call, a human ninja turtle. My favorite food is pizza, I can polish off a large pie from anywhere I have been single-handedly. It's freakish, I only weigh about 170. I eat Pizza EVERYWHERE I go, I have been to Italy, Greece, Chicago, all the boroughs of New York. The only pizzas to rival Wilson for me were Lou Malnati's in Chicago, the ORIGINAL Frank Pepe in New Haven (The expansions are lackluster), and a spot that had no name I could see in Rome (It was close to the Vatican). I would call it an even tie between Frank Pepe's since if you aren't a fan of thin NY style pizza Pepe won't be amazing for you. Me, personally, I love ALL pizza. To anyone who complains about the health factor of a pizza, seriously? If you are such a carb counter then a place called "Wilson Pizza Palace" should be off of your radar. The pies are bursting with flavor, and they are very generous with toppings. Their grinders are enormous and best if eaten on the spot. Their other food I have not explored, the Pizza / Grinders are just too darn good. But some friends tell me everything they make is good. I know the family that owns the place, they are good people and keep everything very fresh and very clean. Do not be fooled by the janky appearance of the building, it is just a piece of Windsor history.
Highly recommended. Delicious food and great atmosphere! If you are a meat lover try lamb lula kebab. It is excellent!
Authentic and fresh- amazing variety and a Options. Every dish is full of flavor and service is outstanding. I would recommend bringing your favorite bottle of wine and enjoying the experience.
I haven't had popovers since I left the UWS 15 years ago!! Great service and excellent food. This is the area's best option right now, and one of the best new restaurants to open.

I had very high hopes for this restaurant due to the previous reviews but the service was very slow and a little bit unfriendly. My family and I ordered lamb and chicken pita bread wraps. The waiter was quick to serve us our water but it came with no ice and although we didn't have to wait long for our meal, the lamb wraps were lacking content in terms of meat and taste. The best part of this meal was the free check in offer which was a rice pudding with cinnamon on top. It was pretty damn good. The chicken wrap that my stepmom had was also better than the lamb. But, shouldn't all the wraps be equally as good? Service was slow in terms of getting our bill and free dessert. I don't know whether I like this place or not but for now I say...meh

The guys behind the counter are really nice. And the burgers are awesome we got The Up Side and the Truffle Burger were cooked perfect. This is a you have to stop. Not quite a must stop but close. Next time your in Philly or live here just try it. In my top 5 places for a great burger.

A SUPER beautiful dining experience, not to mention yummy :) The restaurant has an awesome air to it - comfortable, artsy, and natural. We sat inside (though the outside dining garden looked very cute) and I loved all of the detail from the various walls, the cool tables, the pretty plates, and really cool restroom. Split a Spanish cheese plate- delish!, and then had the scallops and swordfish for dinner (my Mom and I). Both were bursting with new flavors and cooked to perfection. A real treat, from start to finish, with great service as well! Totally recommend this yummy restaurant!
The greatest.

I visited this restaurant when my husband and I were on our way to Newark Airport.  This restaurant was a pleasant surprise.  We found it online and decided to try it.  The staff (she may be the owner) was very friendly.  We felt like we were friends instantly.  The sushi and sashimi we ordered were very fresh. We will definitely visit again.

My friends and I visited during the official grand opening on 7/11/14. From what we were told, they had a soft opening a few weeks back.  The restaurant has a totally different look and vibe from the other Ethos Meze location. From the onset you notice the warm wood with touches of color, there is a long warmly lit bar with a single TV overhead. The bar area has high top tables while the back dining area has tables/wall benches which really help for groups. The restaurant has a back garden where you can notice fresh herbs growing. Not sure what the plan is for the area, but it feels totally natural when paired with the rest of the ambiance of the restaurant. The whole restaurant feels like home, like you are visiting a friends home for a great meal. We enjoyed a few small plates and absolutely everything was top notch. We started with the assorted spreads served with Pita bread, Babghanoush, hummus, & tzatziki. The babghanoush was great you could see the bits of fresh eggplant, the hummus also very good with a touch of smokiness, the tzatziki as absolutely fresh and delicious. The Saganaki - Greek Kefalograviera Cheese was lit at our table with Ouzo. It was soft, warm and yummy. Perfect to spread on the pita bread The grilled stuffed calamari, grilled octopus and lamb were all great small plates at well. Spying at the other tables all the food looked amazing and I'll be back for sure to try everything else out. The only thing lacking was the dessert, although delicious the creme brûlée seemed out of place at a greek restaurant. This place is great, definitely a great addition to the neighborhood. Perfect place for grabbing some small plates before heading out, or even as a night cap before turning in. Can't wait to visit again and try the larger plates.

I'm visiting New York from Cleveland and my friend really wanted to visit a "secret restaurant" (as she put it.) Me along for the ride was looking to experience everything I can, so I was certainly on board. After walking by the restaurant nearly twice, we did find the "secret door" my friend was so craving for and found ourselves inside. We were greeted immediately. We had a party of three and the place was jam packed with people! The hostess suggested we sit at the kitchen bar, which we did. The atmosphere was beautiful, despite being crowded. An open kitchen with the cooks using so much detail I couldn't wait to try it! The menu looks amazing! My mouth was watering from reading all the descriptions. The service was super slow, and I'm pretty sure half way through our meal we ended up with a different server, but they were Friendly. The menu was extremely over priced for the portion sizes. I had the lamb shank for $17 dollars which was roughly the size of an ice cream scoop. Despite the size, it was amazingly flavorful, along with my friends ice cream scooped sized quinoa. Other then those two items, everything else was severely disappointing. My $11 dollar burratta salad lacked any kind of flavor or pizzaz and my friend complained of the hanger steak being extremely salty. Our dessert was average. On a positive note they do have a wonderful, decently priced wine list! Out the door after drinks, food, taxes, and tip we spent about $110 dollars and left still hungry!  And I never got that wow! factor, like 'wow! New York has some Great restaurants!' Now as I mentioned earlier I am from Cleveland, and if you have never been to Cleveland or don't know much about it, it has a HUGE food scene. I wanted this place to blow me and my taste buds away so that I'd be craving to come back, but it Left me still hungry, and extremely disappointed
delicious pizza! no doubt, one of the best in NYC. friendly staff, reasonable price. highly recommended!
Gristle and grease. Fries, steak and water $17. Just plain bad food at tourist trap prices. The city has so much more to offer.

We heard good things about A's, and tried it on a late July Sunday afternoon. Got a quiet table in the back and had an interesting conversation with the neighboring table (frequent visitors). Drinks were a little pricey, but quite good sized. Had the arugala salad, calamari and one order of veal Adriana for two seniors- almost too much food. It was all delicious and the wait staff was attentive and engaging. Overall, a very nice experience and one we look forward to repeating.

Charming spot..Great Ambience..Delicious Food..Had the Ravioli Formaggio which was good however the Tiramisu won my heart- easily the most heavenly Tiramisu i have ever had!! To top it off - Real affordably priced..A must-go spot!

Loved this place! We tried to go to Tom's but the line was out the door and sunshine co was right across the street.  We stopped in after a long bike ride, I had the kale salad (surprisingly flavorful for such a simple salad) and my boyfriend had the brussel sprout hash which was out of this world! The place is adorable and our waitress was beyond friendly.  The service was great, we had our food in no time considering how busy they were

The low rating on this page are well-earned.  Service is very confusing.  Food is just plain awful.  Generic and bland, has zero taste of "Asian" cuisine.  The pork egg rolls are gross - greasy and do not really even taste like egg rolls.  The Hot Thai steak was  the lowest quality meat with weird flavored sauce that just did not seem to go well together.  The brown rice was dry and did not seem fresh.  The wonton's also tasted different/bad.  I love l almost any type of Asian cuisine (Japanese, Thai, Chinese you name it) but this is just not cutting it.  Most of the menu ideas just seem - like food combinations that don't work.

I must say, the tastiest gyro I've tasted in a long time!! A++... Found this place on a search for gyro as I was really craving some.. Made the right choice! Babaganoush was on point and food was delicious.. Wish I could try everything on the menu.. Only wish service was a tad bit quicker but well worth the wait!
Only thing to say is it is the best chicken-over-rice I had.

We ordered sushi for take out and I have to say the sushi was awful. The place itself is not very nice either and it smelled very bad, I think they just had some renovations done. The only reason we ordered there was because of an recommendation but that will be the first and last time. The only reason I give two stars is because the lady in there was so nice but that's it.

This is the second time I've been to this restaurant.  The farm-to-table concept is great but the menu choices seemed very oridnary.  I was there about three months prior and the menu hadn't changed since my last visit. I ordered the special (tilefish, $26) and it was OK but utterly forgettable.  My dining companions ate chicken breast and flank steak which they enjoyed but seemed like very traditional ingredients. The atmosphere is quite lovely except that the upholstered chairs were stained as was the carpet.  The interior looks neglected which suggests they're not doing well.

Super yummy place to get an awesome soup on a dreary day.  Service was a bit spotty and the language barrier with the server was a tad bit of an issue, but all in all great stuff.  Definitely a spot that fits the bill when looking for some real Japanese options.

Best pho in Jersey City. They use fresh noodles which makes a huge difference in the quality of the pho. They also make some mean shakes (am a fan of the avocado shake myself). Sure, it's not a fine dining experience but it's a great hole in the wall Vietnamese place if you're picky about your Vietnamese food. Miles above any other Vietnamese place in Jersey City. Totally with the trek. Spring rolls are crispy and hot. Flavors are good. Bun bo hue is decent - I can only compare to my mother-in-law's bun bo hue which is out of this world. This is also pretty decent!
where I always visit on the first day of my business trip to NYC. after having long fright, BCD soondubu help me to get some energy. prefer extra spicy. staffs are nice and welcoming.

Stopped in for lunch during the middle of the week and the restaurant fairly empty. The service was attentive but their was a co worker at that bar as well and that took up most of my servers attention. The Revolution margarita was great! Tortilla chips were great! Caso Funidito, however was awful. The beef tacos were good and flavorful, however the rice had clearly been sitting under a heat lamp for quiet some time as it was not only dry but crunchy throughout. I had to add sour cream to the rice to eat it. The flan was good but the portion size was tiny. I would return but that is mostly due to the limited options of hispanic food. As someone that grew up on hispanic and Mediterranean food Revolution Cantina was "ok".
Just OK place. Nothing memorable. Didn't think the restaurant week price was a great deal for the average price of a dish in this restaurant.

This place was not bad - the service was definitely struggling (there were only three other tables and we had to chase the waitress down). But, they did let me order off the lunch menu when it was clearly dinner time. The food was not terrible, the ribs were not the best. The wings and nachos were good I would definitely recommend them!! The mashed potatoes were excellent!  And the burgers were OK. Overall, the place was meh.

Best Japanese in the neighborhood. Not quite authentic (there's hardly any in this area) but the food is very tasty and the price is decent. i usually get beef negimaki or chicken katsu bento box, it comes with miso soup, salad, california roll,  gyoza and tempura. I can easily eat one order for two, sometimes three, meals.

Umm...yes, yes, yes and more yes. We first ran into the owners of Emily when they co-opened Brooklyn Central in Park Slope. A few months of weekly (and sometimes daily) attendance followed, but we fell off the BC wagon during Hurricane Sandy (work was a bit hectic). Much to our sadness, when we returned, we discovered the owners had parted ways, and while we loved the food, much of what we enjoyed about BC was the atmosphere created by Emily as manager/hostess. Happily, the party's just moved a little uptown! Emily continues to serve most excellent pizza, and the cocktails aren't too shabby either! After our triumphal reunion with this fabulous food, we vowed to bring a group of friends with us...and we did! I'm happy to say they were all very pleased, too, and we are planning more trips to Emily. I could go through the list of pizzas and tell you about each one, but what a waste. If you've read this far, you hardly need to hear me go on even more. What I will say is that my partner and I have had, between us, 4 pizzas and our friends had 3 others, and no one said anything beyond variations of "yum" or "I want more."

Give these guys a TON of credit - walked in 90 minutes after they opened their doors for the first time ever and they already got their act together! Amazing service, food and a great vibe. What a welcome addition to Wayne. This is gonna be the new hot spot for sure. Meatballs were EXCELLENT and pizza was well cooked with delicious toppings. Waitress was bubbly and management was really on top of it all. Pleeeeease stay great! Hooked already.

GREAT new restaurant in Cobble Hill! Great outside and inside decor - Cool gatstropub restaurant vibe with an amazing craft beer selection. Good place for everything- a date, meeting friends, even a family dinner (i was there with my hubby and baby). The owner, manager, hostess, and waitress were extremely warm and accommodated my pouty 15month old. They came over to make sure everything was okay multiple times-not in an annoying way; just a "is everything cool and can we do anything more for u way". We shared the pork belly and sweet corn fritters as an appetizer. Comes with a mango(?) jalepeno same that is not hot at all.  Weird sounding combo but very yummy. A perfect guy appetizer for your hungry date (who happened to be my husband , in this case!) . He had the chicken and waffle and liked it a lot. A little different from your typical soul food menu item- a bit crispier and maybe need some powdered sugar (?) for presentation. But still good.   I had the ugly duckling burger-needed the ketchup for a sauce addition. But was cooked to my medium well perfection and yummy. The chips were a hit with my son. Handmade thin potato chips with sea salt with sliced pickles on the side. Overall, a great addition to the neighborhood. Will definitely come back and have already recommended to fellow Brooklynite foodies.

The food is amazing, but if I were you I would only order from here! Was with my 4 friends for the first time there to sit down and eat(normally I order) and service was not good, 2 ladies served us, we got different drinks then we orders, they forgot one drink, we were still eating the appetizers and got already our main mean and then was cold before we could start! There is only one really cute waiter, that was super nice. Making the  sign with his hands! So nice right ! But that was all! It is cheap, and so good the food! But if you go there.. Make sure you say you want the main meal after the appetizers!!!

Went here for the first time after reading some good reviews The burger was good not to big just right but the Peanut butter shake was outrageous I would say probably the best so far I would DEFENITELY be coming back almost forgot the fried pickles very very good
Beautiful Gem in Brooklyn, Long established but recently has stepped it up to another level. The decor is inviting food is amazing, classic french but  throws many surprises.  Will be back.

Decent pizza, AWFUL service. My friends and I had to wait for more than 30 minutes to be seated... beside the fact that there were at least 10 available tables (without reservation)! Hostess and waiters literally ignored us when we got there, and they didn't explain why we had to wait so long. Beside a friendly and professional barman, the service was very disappointing. I hope they will improve.

Very friendly atmosphere. Attentive wait staff as well. The chef just asked if i enjoyed my meal which i did. I ordered the turkey burger with fries combo meal. Fries My  were hand cut and not in chip shape as others mentioned guess i they listened  to the other yelp review. My  friend and I inquired about this place last night and since i was getting my car repaired around the corner, i stopped by. My only complaint would be the bun. It was kinda crumbly and fell apart a little as i ate. I dont like that. No other complaints though.

One of my favorite restaurants in new haven. Located at the top of the omni hotel, the view is spectacular. I visited for dinner on a Tuesday night and it was fairly slow so we were seated right away. The waitress was lovely very warm and laid back. I had a filet.. Like buttah. Used a restaurant.com gift certificate which helped with the bill. The waitress welcomed it without fuss; she told us it's been great for attracting new diners. Parking is convenient down in the hotel garage. Overall, excellent food at a premium price.

This is my first yelp review, been using it for a year or so to always find a pretty good meal so I figured it's time to chip in.  I have been to hinge cafe 3 times now, the first two times for lunch and now yesterday for breakfast, and it has been great every time.  For breakfast I went with the Super Spicy Burrito, eggs, chorizo sausage, pa blank peppers, corn (and I went with no black beans), and I ordered a sesame seed bagel, which, after the burrito came out, I knew I wasn't gonna need.  It was excellent, though I wouldn't call it super spicy, it had it's punch.  Burrito was perfectly put together, big enough to need a fork and knife but held together very well.  Side of salsa and sour cream made for a fantastic breakfast.  Wife had the challah French toast Bananas Foster, and I will be getting it the next time we go for breakfast.  It was like a candy breakfast, just delicious.   Had the pulled pork sandwich for lunch previously, and although it could be on a stronger roll then the ciabatta, which didn't hold up well, I just pulled out my fork and finished it up that way.  Moist pork, nice taste to it, with some cheese, spinach, and roasted peppers.  Definitely worth a shot, and the French fries were excellent Will definitely be back many times, so many more interesting menu items to choose from.  And the price seems about right for the quality of food

Definitely  my favorite Indian restaurant. its pretty consistent and has a good selection of vegetarian and non veg options. I especially love their dosas and kathi rolls . Sambhar and sauces are delicious and have great samosas . Their mango lassi was awsome , would definitely visit again .

My boyfriend and I popped in here to enjoy a late lunch on a Friday afternoon while meandering around SOHO. At first glance we weren't too sure about this place as there was only one table sat. Since it was a chilly weekend, we chose to eat indoors next to the windowed doors. I ordered minestrone soup with the Insalata Mista, and my boyfriend ordered the Napolitano pizza. Both were really large and I don't recommend unless you split one or the other with another person. The waiters were a little slow after we mentioned we were in a little hurry. But I can give them the benefit of the doubt here as it was not busy. I would go back dinner if ever given the chance as it seems to have good menu items.

Noooooooo!!!!!! I'm holding a MAJOR grudge!! Only three stars because the old place was worth a five star review! So upset they closed and moved.... Planned to meet my sister here (as we always have over the past few years as a go to place). I ended up being early and very confused because I had no clue they closed and moved and reopened in a few months time. I know, I know, if I like this place so much how did I not know they closed up? I haven't been around since the winter and needed my fix only to be devastated!  Anyway, the new place was..well..new. I sat at the bar waiting for my sister and I was asking the bartender what the hell happened. She told me they had to close because the building got sold or something. They lost a lot of their bartenders/staff because of the move. This is the WORST part!!!! Nooooooooooooo. Where is that awesome Irish bartender with the long hair that always remembered you???? He looked like a sexy Jesus! Where the hell did he go??? Seriously, if you know, message me because he was one of the reasons we (my sister and I) loved this place so much. The food is the same, thank god because the food was always great!  To be honest I probably won't be back, I'll be searching for my bartender friend. On a side note, I saw him about a year ago near the west 4th subway stop and he waved and asked how I was doing. He knew exactly who I was, that's how great this place was. Oh well, my search continues for a comfortable pub with dim lighting, good food/beer and a one of a kind bartender!!!
Delivered in under half an hour!  Huge wraps - chicken fajita was awesome, possibly more accurately classified as a burrito.  I asked for no raw onions and they got it right!
Was craving some delicious Chinese food and this spot did not disappoint me. Delicious
the broth man, the broth

You have to be patient, because you will wait for your food quite a long time. But once the food is there, you know it was worth waiting for! And the atmosphere of the place is unique and the ladies who cook the food absolutely lovely!!! Thank you, we had great time and we definitely will be back.

I came here for a quick lunch during the work day and the buffet set up was perfect.  I also got a side of steamed pork dumplings which were super tasty.  The food is reasonable priced and definitely authentic.  I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a quick and tasty Korean lunch fix.

Recently went to Sunday brunch here with a large large group.  OUr server was excellent and very attentive for such a large crowd, food was delicious and there was a great atmosphere.  He was also very patient with us, which I appreciated a lot.  Looking forward to taking my group back there again sometime soon.

My quest for the best cheesesteak is officially over now. This place here is hell!! The meat they put on your cheesesteak is outrageous!! I needed a fork to help me eat it. The flavor was there and everything is on point. I've found out something. North Philly and South Philly has a different variation. South Philly is on the cheez whiz kick and North Philly isn't on that as they like to give you the choice of real cheese on your sandwich. I'll head back over here before I leave to go back home. After eating this, I don't even want anybody else's cheesesteak, REAL TALK!!! This is MY SPOT now!!!

I had one of my favorite meals in NYC! This was so surprising but perfect for Chelsea! The atmosphere is very intimate and relaxing. Perfect for a date night. All the food looked gorgeous but the zucchini appetizer is a must!  I also had scallops perfected. What a great experience. So glad we came.
Excellent food!! My husband and I came after reading reviews from fellow yelpers. Everything is clearly made fresh at the restaurant and the portions are very large. Worth the money!

I have been going there for years but have not been there in awhile.  The last time we went the food was cold.  I suggested to my husband to try again.  Food was alright except they forgot to put two items on my burger.  The waitress did correct it.  I asked for mustard and they brought me a brand new bottle that had never been opened.  The problem after I already put it on my burger and ate half of my burger I looked at the mustard and the expiration date was 02-03-2012!!!  The place really looks dirty, sure has gone down.  Will not be going back

I absolutely love this place. First off, I adore the decor. It's clean, modern-looking and not your average Chinese restaurant. The staff is very friendly and they have the best customer service! I'm obsessed with the VEGAN general tso's (although I no longer have a meatless diet). Everything is fresh, light on the oil, but most of all TASTY. I also thoroughly enjoyed the chocolate fortune cookies! I'd never had one before this place. Please keep up the good work!

This is a perfect Sunday morning brunch spot! Though.. I must say that the Lobster BLT that they have for lunch on weekdays is also very very good. In all honesty though, how often do you find a French-African restaurant snugged in a quiet yet vibrant and chic area of Manhattan - right by Union Square, but not too far east as Alphabet City? After enjoying your Lobster Benedict and White Sangria for Sunday brunch (both of which are amaaazing!), you can take a stroll in the area, walk towards Union Square (potential shopping on 5th ave) or choose to go uptown towards Madison Square Park or walk down towards East Village. OR if you have weekend grocery plans to stock up your supplies for the week, you can always stop by Trader Joe's for food and wine after your meal. The place is not big, but definitely a comforting place to sit and catch up with old friends! They also have a "Check in and get free dessert" offer that you can use via yelp so you really get the most out of your experience!

Service, foods and the price was A +++ I love that they have small hidden backyard And It's BYOB!! Jambalaya and truffle burger was so good. One star off for the cash only thing. Everything else was perfect!

Went here for the boyfriend's birthday dinner on a recommendation from a friend. The layout is cozy and though we were originally put in a high traffic spot, our server moved us to a more private table by request. We got guacamole and mole sauce along with our salsa and chips to start out. The chips tasted a little stale and the guac was just average but I really enjoyed the salsa and the mole sauce was some of the best I've ever had: creamy and sweet! For entrees I got the vegetarian enchiladas and my boyfriend got enchiladas in mole sauce. I am vegetarian and he has a gluten allergy: the menu was accommodating for both dietary restrictions and our server was helpful. My vegetarian enchiladas were fine and the green sauce they came in was delicious. The enchiladas in mole sauce were to die for! We also got two margaritas that were tasty, generous, and very authentic. This spot is expensive, $46 for two of us without dessert, but a good dining experience. Great service and good food but not fantastic enough for the the price.
Just had lunch here for the first time. Amazing sandwiches, great prices, friendly staff and fun atmosphere. All around great experience. Can't wait to come back!

I'm disappointed. Nice atmosphere, and much anticipation waiting for this spot to open. Unfortunately, the $17 Porgy was a letdown. Small portion, definitely needed a side to accompany the tiny fish on my plate - That, and it was a really unattractive cut of meat with a bloody vein at it's center. Then, there was the schnitzel. I mean, gravy or a nice jam would be the appropriate accompaniment, but instead - you get the 'claw.' I'm all for a bit of theatre with my dinner - but not when it replaces basic attention to dinner flavor detail. I don't like to hate, but this was not a great experience. That said, the service was AWESOME and so was the wine. I think there is still hope...but the kinks need attention.

Great rolls. I tried the Achari Paneer and Chicken Tikka roll. The best part about the roll was that the chicken and paneer were drenched with flavor. Whatever the Chef did to imbue the flavors deep within - it's commendable. Would love to go back to this place when I visit NY next.

I love el Rey this food here is very tasty.  The drinks are very good too. The food here keeps you coming back and great atmosphere. El Rey is very authentic Mexican food this is my 4 time coming here and every time is very memorable. The service here is really fast.
I like this place. Laid back atmosphere, good cocktails and the food is good too. It's my first time here and I will come back.

Had brunch reservations for my cousin's birthday. I was really looking forward to coming here. The food was delicious as I expected, but if you're looking for mom's traditional home cooking, then you're better off going home to visit mom. We enjoyed our experience and the staff was super friendly and knowledgeable. I would definitely recommend coming here to experience what they have to offer!

I went to the Risotteria because of its gluten free options. I bought the black and white gluten free cookie and the orio cake.I was surprised the food was tightly packaged, probably to make sure it doesn't come in contact with other products. The cake was quite dry but works well with a glass of milk. I would not recommend it if you are looking for a gluten free pastery place but it's good enough for a quick snack in soho.

I've had bagels from here for 30 years.  Parking is horrible and the place has gone way down.  Must be the new owners.   The bagels in the afternoon seem leftover from the morning.  I'm very disappointed. There is a great bagel place in wallington.  Long drive since I living in west orange but worth it. The employees not so nice. Cream cheese prices are very expensive.

I have come here multiple times and am finally sharing my view on this place. Yesterday I got the Kobe beef buns and Spicy Miso Ramen. Stunning. Thankfully it seems that people who queue up at Ippudo don't know about this place!! Keep up the good work.

One of many places that offers great breakfast meals! Always served hot and fresh. Morning is often crowded but that's a given considering how great this place is. Service is fast which is really good for me. I really like this place.
Best ice coffee!  Great cheeses too!  Love the salads.  great of lunch!  The deli past closes at 7!

The owner is the kindest man I have ever met! He genuinely cares about his customers and their experience. I recommend this place to everyone. The food is fresh and amazing and everything is so flavorful. You feel at home in this place and relaxed. I could hang out here all day and sip the fresh juices!! This is the kind of hardworking, caring man that deserves equally awesome customers. Also really good hummus. This is definitely a type of business and hardworking man that a community needs!

I have been hearing great things about this place. I was finally able to try it today. I hade the thanksgiving balls and they were great! The blind pig has an amazing beer selection. If in season try the watermelon wheat. I was able to talk with the owner she was great! This place will be on my list every time I come to philly!! Keep it up.

Great spot for a quick bite during lunch break.  Conveniently located at 19th and Market.  I had the chicken salad wrap and the tomato soup.  Tasty and inexpensive!  I heard they have great smoothies as well.  I will definitely be back to try one of those!

Disappointed. This is one high rated restaurant. I was expecting a home run. I came all the way from Brooklyn. Both dishes we had were one dimensional. With the drunken noodles our taste buds could not detect any salt or sugar. I asked for it spicy. It had a mild heat to it. Drunken noodles is suppose to be spicy, sweet, salty & full of Thai basil. That's what we love about it. How can they forget the basics. Hardly no basil at all. The noodles were stuck together. I like my food not greasy but you need a little oil to keep the noodles from sticking together. The other dish we ordered was tofu & mixed vegetables fried with red curry. The mixed vegetables were bamboo shoots that tasted like the can it came in & those very seedy green Indian eggplants. It also had a few shreds of red pepper. I should of asked what they mean by mixed vegetables. all the sauce had going for it was heat. What is so wonderful about Thai food is the multi dimensions of flavor. Not this time. The restaurant was only about 20% full. The chef was out to lunch. Asleep at the wheel. Not mentally there. With all these good reviews maybe I caught a bad night. Maybe the usual chef was out sick. Maybe they are not as good as they used to be. We wont be trucking down here from Brooklyn again. DaFooflum

Went to Tortuga's for lunch today as I was craving tamales.  Had high hopes based on reviews of this place and was thoroughly disappointed.  Blindfold me and this place tastes exactly like the old Chi Chi's or Casa Lupita on rte 1. First off, I walked in not knowing I had to wait to be seated and then the waitress told me to wait before sitting.  Ok.  I watched her clean several tables before she said ready.  She was the only one there serving and bussing the entire restaurant. Looked over menu and decided to order the chicken dhile relleno and beef tamale.  The food came out pretty quick and piping hot.  Now this is where it went down hill. A proper chile relleno should be stuffed with chicken or beef with cheese stuffed in a pepper that has been deep fried in a batter that is crispy.  What I got was a soggy sponge with unmelted cheese as the first layer followed by a pepper then topped off with a mound of shredded chicken topped off with way too much cheese.  It essentially was a Mexican lasagna.  Over this lasagna was a salty sauce all over the plate with a side of rice and refried beans. Every good Mexican restaurant when serving a proper relleno always has sauce on the bottom of the plate with the crispy relleno on top, so you get proper texture.  A nice dollop of sour cream/guac would have added a nice touch too. Onto the tamale.  Why not serve it in it's corn wrapper? What I got was a mashed potato like masa with shredded beef below and topped with that damn salty ass sauce again. If you are going to call yourself authentic Mexican cuisine and charge 17 for a tamale and chile relleno combo, at least make it authentic and proper. This place IMHO sucked!

I LOVE THIS PLACE SO SO SO MUCH!!! We came in from out of town and the Waldorf recommended this place. Me and my boyfriend went to check it out and it was a super long wait but the handsome and charming doorman (who is the uncle of the owner) made us feel like we were the most important people in there. He made jokes and made sure we found a comfortable place to wait. He even bought us a bit of champagne while we waited. The meal was exceptional. The spinach dip and meatballs may be the BEST we ever had and the wine list was incredible. I can't wait to come back here but until then I will be telling all my good friends to come and ask for Uncle Mike. hahahaha.
Amazing food for a great price! It's the perfect place to meet friends to grab drinks and tapas! Friendly staff!

I ordered food for take out so I don't judge or make any review service here. I ordered dandan noodles and others (can't remember). Dandan noodle was soooo good. Little spicy and moisture, which make tasty. Chinese food is not one of my favorite but I can eat dandan noodles multiple times. Dandan noodle is highly recommended when you visit Philly  (if you can't eat spicy food, just don't try it, busters).

Beyond overrated. Went for brunch last Sunday, but got there at 3:33pm and the brunch menu ends at 3:30 so could only order from the "in between" menu. The food is average and the service is AWFUL. We waited 20 minutes for our drinks. So did the table next to us. When the customer at the table next to us asked where her coffee was the waitress cut her off and in a patronizing tone said "they're making it honey, they're making it." She'd ordered a coffee when she sat down and had already been served her entree before getting her coffee. The mussels are interesting, but not outstanding like they claim. The hostess was so rude and pretended there was a 25 min wait for a table when there were clearly at least 6 tables open or opening up outside then after we stood for five minutes she sat us at the table that she initially insisted we couldn't sit at. This place sucks.

Stopped by for lunch and had a seriously good and seriously inexpensive combination plate as part of their lunch menu. Pad Thai, Ginger Chicken, spring rolls plus a Thai desert for $7.95. Seriously good, large portion to the point that I took some home with me.  When I asked for a container to take the Ginger Chicken they asked me if I would like some rice with it? I said yes and asked for brown rice which they added to my doggie bag AT NO CHARGE. Definitely would recommend this for food, price, atmosphere, convenience. Enjoy.
Great food, nice environment and very friendly family owners who serve and bartend. I'm happy to have this lovely gem in the neighborhood. I'll become a regular.

New to yelp so catching up on reviewing one of my favorite restaurants in the city.  Amazing food, beer selection, happy hour and especially late night happy hour! Best place to go for a cheat meal -- burgers, maple fried chicken, pot pie, and homemade choco-tacos! Great late night happy hour stop -- cheap amazing eats like soft pretzels, deviled eggs, pork bruschetta, and oysters!

Came here for Sunday late-night happy hour with a group of friends. Half off margarita pitchers, half off tostadas and $3 nachos. Food was pretty good if not lacking a little bit of flavor. Margaritas were weak and sort of tasted like Mike's hard lemonade and/or Jose Cuervo margarita mix, but at $15 for a large pitcher I can't complain that much. Just means they're overpriced to begin with. Our waiter was awesome and friendly.

I've been wanting to try this place for a while. There are lots of seafood restaurants in/around Hartford, but the Chowder Pot seemed like one of the best. I had the stuffed shrimp. It was delicious, but I wouldn't say it was amazingly good. If I was in the mood for seafood I would probably try another restuarant before coming here again, but I also wouldn't be opposed to eating here again.

I love this place! Halcyon is probably one of the most beautiful restaurants and bars in the area. They have great staff, the bartenders are pro's and the servers are very attentive and knowledgeable about their menu. They have a great raw bar selection and they even do happy hour raw bar during the week. Its a great after work spot. Try their tuna tartare and crab cake, to die for. Also great tacos. Filet mignon and Cod ( if they are not super busy they will mix up the tacos for you)  Halcyon is the closest thing to a great city restaurant but in the suburbs. its a great date spot, or just a night out with family & friends. also, if they have the coconut cream pie, you MUST order it.

Enjoy your meal with Cool place, Cool service & Cool price. The food was delicious and seem like you have dinner in Thailand. Both of Boss, Khun Tom& Khun Ann are very nice, They take care every clients by themselves.....it's Great !!!Have a worth dinning today.

Went for a date night because we wanted to try something different and everything was great. The only thing we would change about our dining experience is getting an appetizer, not because it was bad, but because we were too full! We loved our meals (which were a recommendation of the bartender) and wanted to fully enjoy them. All drinks we had were awesome; sangria, mojitos, and an after dinner drink the bartender whipped up :) Fruit empanadas were the perfect ending to this meal. Will definitely go back again. make reservations because it is a small place :)

Let me start by saying that I completely admire the concept behind this place. Healthy food. Eating right. Affordable prices. I get it. However, for me, the flavor was a bit underwhelming. The food wasn't bad. It was good.... It just wasn't  great. It seemed like a layer of flavor was missing... maybe more seasoning is needed. I don't know. I've only eaten here once and had the Sicilian Breakfast. I'll come back and try something else. Maybe it will change my mind.

A local classic and absolute staple in the Clifton/Montclair area!  Best "square" slice around - prepared with the sauce on top and cheese underneath.  The first thing you taste is the tangy sauce - crust is great as well.  Why not 5 stars? Depending on who is making the pizza quality can sometimes be inconsistent.

Less is not more.  I ordered a noodle only drunken noodle and as you can see By my photo I literally have not even half a container for almost $11.  I also ordered a Thai iced tea which was not sweet enough.  I used to come here all the time when it was the puket cafe and even the lunch specials weren't so small.  Just disappointing, the drunken noodles weren't as good either.

Every time we are in town this is a must stop for the family. The baby lobster tails the spice shrimp, the beer tower, oysters, and clams. This place has a lot of TVs to watch your favorite sports. Perfect for hang out and eating and watching your favorite team. Great for families when we were there the last time they had trivia night. It was pretty cool. This is a must stop.

Found this jem today. It's self seat, booth or stools, at a counter facing the cook/kitchen. The waitress was friendly and brought large cold waters immediately upon us being seated. Their menu is long but organized which made decision making easy. I ordered the French toast with home fries and a coffee. Home fries came with option peppers and onions. I only ordered onions. My coffee came quickly and was larger and hotter than expected. The food shortly after. My French toast tasted like Christmas. The home fries buttery, crisp, and seasoned with onions. Price was more than reasonable for product. Definitely returning.
They were packed and their service was actually pretty good. If you need a quick slice or a decent cheesesteak, this is not a bad option.

I love this spot! It is a great Spring/Summer spot to sit outside and eat. Their crab habanero dip is to die for but it hasn't been on the menu (which is why I only gave it four stars. Put the dip back on the menu and they will get five stars). Great environment though! Also, kid friendly!!

Great service and great food. I've been here several times, food is always consistent. Their pork belly buns,melts in your mouth. Their green papaya salad is refreshing.  Duck ramen and seafood ramen is tasty.

The food is yummy but it was better with the previous chef. Very crowded after 6pm on weeknights with the business school crowd but after 8pm ish it settles down. The duck fries and clam pizza are classic greats.

I had the best meal at Calle Ocho tonight.  I am in from out of town and went to Calle Ocho because I read that they had some gluten free options.  I ordered the grilled steak but didn't realize that "carabas" is blue cheese and attempted to scrape it off when my dinner arrived. The bartender and manager quickly arrived and insisted on replacing the meal despite the fact that it was my fault.. When my meal arrived it was one of the best meals I have had in a long time, The food, manager and bartender made this a great meal. I hear that they have a great brunch including bottomless sangria. I definitely will have to check out.

Finding good fried chicken in NYC is difficult. Some of the most highly rated options I've tried were no better than the Publix Supermarket deli chicken (although their chicken is great). The fried chicken here was delicious. They incorporate sweet tea & lemon with a light breading and tender juicy chicken. It makes for a deadly combo. The menu is very inventive with new takes on old southern favorites. We tried a few different items and enjoyed each of them. I also recommend taking a look at the cocktail list. The drinks are well crafted and offer great flavor without being overpowering.
Pretty good. No complaints. I enjoyed the fries a lot. My sandwich was good but nothing to write home about. The service was also good.
i am a lover of sweet and this resturaunt met my needs.i went there a few days ago.they have a good variety of sweets.

Food was really good. Absolutely the worst service I have ever experienced. This service was so bad that I almost knocked a table over and left but my diner came out (before my appetizers) so that stopped me from leaving. When the apps finally came out, they forgot one taco out of two. While we waited for 45 min until we got food... Our waitress didn't come to let us know anything. We sat in the dark util we had to open our mouths. I will order out from here... But refuse to ever sit and eat.

I just love it here.  I've been a few times and I'm never, ever disappointed.  Maybe it's because I feel like I'm dining instead of just eating out in another loud, trendy, resto of the moment.   The decor is modern and minimal but doesn't feel cold...rather very cozy and intimate.   Service is always outstanding...very knowledgeable, attentive and you don't ever feel rushed.  The food has always been scrumptious.  I think I'm one of the few that doesn't feel the need to get the monkey bread, but the lardo spread is pretty yummy.  The pastas are insane (in a good way, of course)...the scallops and suckling pig are incredible. Extensive wine list and some pretty inventive cocktails, too. Save room for dessert...whatever is chocolate on the menu, just order it! When I want a special night out, Piora is one of the first places that comes to mind.  Always love coming back here.

Where have you been all my life!! I can't believe I've lived in Jersey all my life and have not tried this place. That relish is a crack sauce topping for the for dog combined with mustard and a side of the mouthwatering chili. I don't normally like chili, but this one is the one! If you love hot dogs you must try rutts hut. It is the holy grail of hot dogs.
I would come here for the atmosphere. Food is good, it's very well worth eating at. I kind of felt that my pasta (custom made, I like plain pasta with herbs) was sort of watery.
the almond croissant is super delicious.

Very disappointed with this place the fact that they weigh the meat should indicate something, my husband had the 1/2 pound pork belly which was more fat than meat and I had the 1/2 pound brisket, taste wise it was pretty good but the portions are to small for the price. The fact that you go to the counter and order your own food and they have paper plates and you seat yourself they could do a little better on the servings. In our opinion not worth it and won't be going back.

I HAD a reservation for 6 people and wanted to increase it to 7 people.. I received a comment of they needed to "ask" if that was possible.. for 1 person?!?!? then I was instructed that I needed to change my dining time to 45 min later to accommodate 1 extra person.. just 1... I canceled the reservation.. asked to speak with the manager, that never got on the phone.. I will NEVER dine there.. and will deter all who suggest it..

Tried a range of tapas... Pan Tumaca, Churrasco Arriero, Croquetas De Jamon, Empanadillas De Carne, Pimientos De Piquillo Rellenos.... they were ok, but nothing that I'm craving to have again. Red wine sangria was ok, not awesome.

Made reservations for 2:30 just in case. Waited at bar with a pitcher of red sangria until the whole party arrived. Ordered Matador Combo & Mixto Cebiche. More than enough for 4 but we enjoyed it all... Along with more sangria. Staff is helpful and kind enough to even charge my phone for me. Cheers!

I will be typing about the Big Ass Biscuit with Gravy from the Khyber Pass pub. I really like the biscuit because it is really is huge so if you are really hungry go there. The biscuit is firm but not that hard. The gravy though is the best part of this dish. There are little pieces of meat inside the gravy so after I finish the main part that is a biscuit  I get my spoon and just eat the gravy off my spoon. So if you are in Old City you should go to the Khyber Pass and eat a Big Ass Biscuit with Gravy! Looking for more awesome food Agent G.

Where shall I start...my boyfriend and I have been here a couple times before and have left beyond satisfied in the past. Tonight was just ridiculous to us. We waited about 30 minutes to be seated which is completely understandable for a Friday night. It is BYOB therefore we did (a bottle of wine), our server seemed to be offended by us having a personal bottle of hard lq and after that everything went downhill. The table next to us were seated after us and he proceeded to take their order before us. He stopped by their table to ask how everything was going, never once stopping by our table. He flew past our table a few times which is also understandable considering the huge crowd that takes over this restaurant almost every night. We finally get his attention to bring the check over and he does the math & just throws the check on the table. My boyfriend always whips out his phone to calculate 20% gratuity, but this guy didn't even deserve pocket change. Never in my life have I experienced such terrible service. Yeah the food is great but there are plenty other restaurants that provide the full package..great food AND great service.

I came here once earlier this year late night.. our bartender was very friendly , down to earth and just overall pleasant. It was laid back and casual. I must say I had way too much to drink and at $25 a shot.. I should of known better .. lol
Great food, great service!  Had the filet at a birthday dinner here.  Best BYOB in Fairmount

We asked the waiter what the most popular dishes were and we ordered most of what he recommended, as they sounded good (sheep's milk ricotta, kale salad, gnocchi, and stuffed meatballs). Also got a bottle of their lower-end bubbly, a Casa del Mar cava for $50. The ricotta was good, but honestly, something that you could easily do at home if you were willing to grill some good bread with olive oil. Same for the gnocchi -- a good dish, but a skilled cook could probably pull something similar off at home. Now, the kale salad was great -- creative, well prepared, and really flavorful. I would not recommend the meatballs, though. I was literally tasting them hours after we ate. They're heavy and a little much. You can do better in the Italian Market, both for the meatball and the sauce that came with it. The caramel budino was delicious. It was easily the best part of the meal. The kicker was that I liked the bottle of cava and so went home to order some. I got it for $10.99 at one of my favorite wine shops that ships. You could alternately special-order it from the state stores for $13. I wouldn't think too much about a 3x markup. However, a 4x or nearly 5x markup is insulting. In the end: OK food in a rustic-chic setting, and wine that is obnoxiously priced even if well selected. I might order the budino to take out but I won't go back. There are too many other good places with better food in Philly.

Excellent pizza, was walking by and the recession special caught my eye, but the yelp reviews drew me in; the service and ultimately execution knocked it out of the park. The first time was just the recession special, an amazing deal at 5 and change for two slices and a fountain soda. What sealed it was ordering delivery had two large pies one plain and one pepperoni and the quoted delivery time was 30-45, however the pizza was here between 20-30 minutes. At the end of the day, the brick oven taste is the lasting memory but the attention to detail leaves you wanting more. As for the taste, I'm one for a million toppings on my pizza and i still prefer the plain.

I do love Vegan Tree. This place is a cute and comfortable place to eat at. I love that it's on South Street and I just wish it was closer to me. The cheesy bread is beyond good. I could just eat that alone but I've also had the vegan cheese steak and I loved that, too. I've had other dishes and all I have to say is the food is great and the employees are lovely. I really have to make my way over there some time soon. Try them.

We walked in, the place was not crowded for a Friday night. I ordered a Mediterranean Mule and it came in a copper mug, which reminded me of the copper cup my mom gave me back in 1991. I was 10... Life was good back then, simple some may say. My mom gave me the copper cup to put pencils and crayons as homework started to come in at a frequent rate. I loved that copper cup more than I loved my sky blue crayon, which later, sadly, dissappeared after using it too much...
Great price and quality for a noodle place! Beef cake and spicy beef noodle soup are must have.

Hands down one of the best meals in the city. The food is creatively crafted and truly memorable. My must-have favorites are the edamame dumplings and wasabi crusted filet. This is my favorite place for that special romantic date.
Great bread for bruschettas, and I had a decent composed duck salad. But $7 for 2oz of cheese makes it a little pricey in order to have a decent cheese plate. More a wine bar than an eatery.
Awesome food!! The flavors are awesome and the food does justice to the fresh farm vegetables . Great choices for vegetarians and the vegan option is also great!

Housesitting in Kensington, and the owners recommended I see Joe when I need a sandwich as big as my head. It's my last day here, and I'm annoyed with myself for not having gone earlier. (Although my waistline is probably grateful.) Ordered the balsamic chicken sandwich with fancypants cheese and avocado. Except they were out of avocado. I was going to make another selection when Joe suggested he put fresh pesto in place of the avocado. So be it. Sandwich indeed came out as big as my head. It's delicious. The bread is so good, the chicken is tender and yummy. The pesto tastes great. I planned to eat half and save the other half for later, but later equals 20 minutes after I finished the first half. I'm pathetic. And happily full.

Been here a couple times for sips and for entrees.  Food is alright, can't complain but I can't compliment it either.  Sub par asian dishes, mostly chinese although they consider themselves fusion.  Most the cocktails are fruity and lack any real attempt at broadening their signature cocktails list to appeal to those who don't need an apple bees type sugary drink.  Decor is nice, casual crowd except for the cheap booze fiends on sips.  Avoid that cheap wasted crowd.

Absolutely wonderful place. Great food, ambiance, amazing customer service. Came on a Saturday night with a large group,made a reservation and they called me ahead of time to let me know they wouldn't be able to seat us immediately as the last party was running late which was such a nice courtesy. When we arrived, the host offered us drinks on the house because of their delay. food was unique and tasty- favorites at our table were kale and shrimp salad and the squid ink pasta.  Unique decor and nice vibe. Definitely recommend!!

We were in from out of town and I wanted Korean food. My friends did not so this was a compromise. Though the Korean menu was small; I did get the bi bim bop with squid  which was great. My friends also enjoyed their meals.  I wish we would of BYOB'd and it would of been great. I recommend this place for a nice date night. Bring the wine.
I can only speak for the donuts which are both square and glorious. If you're in New Haven and you go to Dunkin Donuts, shame on you.

Lobster Joint is located in a new commercial area with street parking available. Light up lobster sign with lead you through the gateway. Picnic style tables with a few pub tables available. Open french doors make for a nice breeze during the summer. Menu written on a chalkboard style board above their register. Noise level was normal, was able to have a conversation without yelling. Staff was helpful in answering questions on the menu and making accurate recommendations. Beers on tap and bottled as well as wine available. After you order they hand you a number and you choose your seat. Moderate prices for lobster as $17 for each dish. Excellent food for a great value. The New England Lobster roll was warm and flavorful. Fries that came with it were seasoned appropriately with what may have been old bay.  Lobster tasted fresh with an even balance between their herb mayo and lobster. The Lobster Mac'n'Cheese was hearty and filling. There were nice chunks of lobster. Top layer was nicely crusted with a creamy center. Definitely a meal to share as the cheese was overwhelming halfway through.

One thing that you should get if you've got a big party is the whole lechon. Something that some friends always get for the holidays. The changes I've seen in the past years is the price of the bread being a little higher than it's competition. I'd still go here for fresh PanDeSal.

A few weeks late writing this, but here goes: Came here for dinner w/ reservation their first week and loved our entire experience.  It was a rainy evening and the staff members were trying to figure out a way to keep the floors dry but they remained friendly, attentive and enthusiastic throughout - wonderful service.   Their fried chicken is fantastic (Tabasco honey is great with it).  Also ordered grits (delicious), mac and cheese, cheddar cheese waffles, a sandwich (which I don't see on their menu anymore) and split a sundae/cookie for dessert.  The space is decorated nicely and on the small side, but it looked like they managed to fit a lot of people in there.  Looking at their updated menu, a few things have changed, so I can't wait to come back and try the rest of their food!

Such a great place with fantastic service, food, and ambiance.  A friend and I sat at the bar in front of the open kitchen and the chefs were fun, chatty and happy to describe what they were making and check in on us to see how we were enjoying our food.  Our server was so friendly, made some really great suggestions, and seemed like he had everything under control despite the packed house.  We started off with biscuits and the peach caprese.  The biscuits were good and the peach caprese was interesting, but seemed like a very small serving.  We then had the chicken and waffle sandwich with a side of waffle fries which were both amazing and very filling. Loved it, super charming and great service.
This place has great happy hour deals!! Everyone that works here is super nice. The Mexican revolver cocktail is on point.

Came at 730 on a Friday, nervous at first with how few customers were in, but the nerves didn't last long!  Had the lettuce wrap app which was great!  Wife had the steak tips, I had the mahi mahi (and some steak tips), both were absolutely fantastic, and would get again, although based on the reaction of the customer next to us, I may be getting the samosas next time, she couldn't stop talking about it. Drinks were very well made, had a Manhattan and a beer, my wife had a couple martinis, not too strong, but definitely not weak, perfectly done! Desert was great, had the Creme Brûlée and wife had the cheesecake. Not sure why this place isn't packed on a nightly basis, it really is that good!  Definitely coming back for more.  Only knock is that the live music tonight night have been a bit on the loud side, other then that, nothing to complain about at all.  If you're in the area, stop by, you won't be sorry!

Holy Jesus the noodles are so good. Good alternative to beef noodle soup for all the Taiwanese people who are feeling homesick. Hidden little hole in the wall but judging based on the crowd, the locals know.
Ordered the lamb chops and lamb shish kabob both were amazing! Staff was fast and friendly and the food was great. Its definitely my new go to spot for Turkish food! :)

Cool place - great cocktails. Excellent steak, spicy/sweet desserts  - and very well trained wait-staff. Had a group of 8 and everyone seemed happy. The owner/manager stopped by for a chat which gives the place a good friendly vibe.

Came in with a group of friends on Friday night and it was PACKED. Thank god we made a reservation so we didn't have to wait too long. We were seated in a nice booth that had 6 individual pots and a BBQ grill, so it was perfect. The girls in the front were super nice, even gave us some watermelon juice while we waited. The waiters did a great job getting us what we needed as well. Definitely will be back again!

Had lunch here today. Such a disappointment. I had the ravioli and broccoli rabe. The ravioli was so so, albeit homemade. The flavor wasn't bold. Not worth the price. The rabe was too al dente. The gelato was good, however. Espresso machine was broken. Everyone talks about this restaurant.
Super food! Best falafel in Brooklyn. Excellent value for their meal deals too, staff are consistently friendly and cheerful. Everyone should come try this place out!
The peach iced tea is amazing. Brunch until 4 on weekdays. Maple bacon (with the syrup on the bacon drool drool). Cozy, airy fun setting in great location. Excellent service.

Ordered the pie with Mozza cheese, also one with spinach, pepperoni, and cheese, and a third that was the casino with the clams. The clam pizza was horrible. Too briney and just not tasty. The other two pizzas were tasty and we ordered pick up...two hours in advance...so our wait wasn't long at all. Personally if I had to pick a pizza place to eat at I would rather eat Bar or Modern in the New Haven area.

Probably my favorite happy hour spot. Private parking lot for easy parking, just get in early enough. Appetizers such as the maple chicken wings make my mouth water as I yelp this review at 7:30 am. Very accessible from the train. What a bar they have! If they don't have what you drink you must be from another planet! They even brew their very own beer! It's hard for me to even say this but this Irish pub makes a fresh homemade pizza VERY well. A must have. Outdoor benches are a great hangout for you and a couple friends! Enjoy!

Had the Mexican (vs. American) soft tacos with my fiancé and we absolutely loved them- I had the cows tongue/steak combo and he had steak. Definitely enjoyed the cows tongue more myself but everything tasted fresh and authentic. The salsa and chips they give you are great too! Definitely going back.
Best burritos in Burlington for sure. Beats the popular chains in quality, and comparable on price.

This new addition to the Manhattan dining scene has brought all the freshness and zest of southern Italy to West 8th Street in the Village. The brothers Giuseppe and Mario Pesce use only the most authentic ingredients--mozzarella, mortadella, prosciutto--in their sandwiches, plus a choice of fresh breads. The dolce--like cannoli and cornettos--are baked daily. Pass on the chains and get on over to taste Italy as it was meant to be.

OMG!  Hubby and I were looking for a quick lunch on the way to Ikea and found this via Yelp. My only regret is that we don't live closer but from now on all of our trips to New Haven will include a stop to Jordan's to see Cory and Tiffany.  The chili mac dog supreme was excellent and the Jordan burger, with the surprise of a sweet glaze was also a winner. LOVED the toasty, buttery bun on both the dog and the burger...a wonderful thouch. The showstopper of our visit however, was the beans....and I don't even like beans!  Will be dreaming of beans tonight...

Went and checked this place out last night and I definitely approve. I liked it right away just because of the ambiance but, luckily, the food's good too! We started with the calamari and then had the spaghetti with shrimp and zucchini and the olive and sun dried tomato raviolis. All three were delicious. The portions aren't huge so definitely try out at least two of the appetizers or salads in addition to your meal.

This is a beautiful space - bright, airy, and spare, with a nice garden.  The service was good and the presentation beautiful.  They have an extensive wine list, although there are no local or American wines on it.  The ingredients are fresh.  However, for the price point - four glasses of wine, two appetizers and two entrees was $120 - the food should be better.  The Ensalada De Remolacha was tasty, but the way it was prepared and presented made it hard to eat without being messy.  The blue cheese flavor was lacking from the potato whip in the Paletitas De Pollo - it was just starchy.  My rack of lamb was good, especially the mint sauce, but it was a bit too fatty and the "farmstead cheese and green apple gremolata" was frankly tasteless.  A pleasant dining experience but there are much better restaurants in Park Slope.
Spectacular food. Wonderful service. A great place for a special dinner. Be sure to make reservations.

This place is so good! I'm from NYC and have tried almost all of the famous bbq places,  but this little spot in CT we just happened to stumble upon while driving past was such a pleasant surprise. We had the full size beef brisket over fries with sweet and tangy sauce. Amazing! Incredibly tender and oh so flavorful. It was so good we ordered the pulled pork over Mac and Cheese to go. Wham bam seconds please m'am! Damn good. The customer service is excellent and the decor is simple but clean. If you happen to be on the neighborhood,  do your stomach a favor and stop by this joint.
Quick service and great pasta! What more can you ask for?! Highly recommended for date nights

The waiters were not attentive and I had to ask for something I needed more than 3times and still didn't get it ! The food arrived pretty late and the hostess at the entrance was a little rude .As with the other reviews I strongly agree to make a reservation ! The pro was that the food was yum! Get the mahi mahi entree :)

The pizza is GREAT! And the service is BETTER! We ate a cheese pizza I can say every part of the pizza was on point. The crust,the pie, and the toppings were all fresh! Next time I come to Brooklyn this is the place that will have my business!
Been there a few times and have yet to be disappointed! Best sandwiches around, and the service is great! Really friendly nice people working there

So So So So GOOD!!! I am a lemon squeezer especially when it's put on my plate ... couldn't bring myself to change anything it was so good!! I am 100% coming back for more!! Had Shakshuka (which is poached eggs in a tomato sauce) and the sample platter with amazing grape leaves and the tzatiki was real not liquidy. Everything was great!
The Salmon burger was amazing, opted for greens instead of the bun and added feta cheese.
The pancakes are pretty good.
Got the Pope Francis sandwich.. Sooo good! The mozzarella was fresh along with the prosciutto. The staff are super friendly and it's an overall cute atmosphere(:

the corn is amazing . Something I had never tried before and didn't expect to taste so great. Fish tacos are great too as are the margaritas. Would be great if they could sell singular tacos instead of having to buy the whole plate with rice and beans. Also the staff aren't the friendliest hence the 4 stars.

Found this great, local BYOB place a few blocks from where we live. We are vegetarian and there are plenty of options to keep us satisfied. The spicy agetofu and grilled rice cakes with sweet and sour sauce were phenomenal. We also had a sweet potato tempura roll, bibimbap roll, and an avocado, cream cheese, jalapeño tempura roll. The food was fantastic. The spicy Korean sauce s well as all other sauces are all homemade and to die for. The service was top notch and the staff are very helpful and courteous. It has simple, yet elegant decor and has the feel of a mom and pop type restaurant. Not overly commercialized and even during its busiest time, the service was great. Will be coming back here again and again!

I was in Astoria with an associate last week on business ,and went to Trattoria l'incontro,. The restaurant is  just, let's  say, "enchanting"..  The high ceilings, huge dining room , decorative moldings, and impeccably dressed waiters who cater to your every whim and timely dim the lights and replace with lit candles ,create an even more  soothing ,relaxing atmosphere.  Our intention was to have  a quick cup of  coffee , for a half hour between appointments. But , being spell bound ,we ended up staying almost  2 hours enjoying the atmosphere. We ordered the Ricotta cheesecake  and cappuccinos.   The cheesecake was a  combination of orange and lemon citrus perfectly blended giving it a  light creamy texture  from Ricotta ,or as the chef would pronounce  RIGOTTA , it was simply perfect. My friend also  had  this delicious  stuffed ravioli with 3 different cheeses ",intoxicating "were his words.. What we also found incredible was that the chef  Rocco , was in the dining room ,greeting  his guests, most of them , by name .  It made you feel so welcome.  Hope to be visiting Astoria again soon, leave plenty of time ,for Trattoria l'incontro to enjoy everything , taking it all in ,, from appetizer to dessert.
For the price you can't beat this place. Always a local hippy working, and always consistent, for $7, it's better than grabbing a slice of pizza

My husband and I tried to visit El Matador a couple of months ago based on a couple of recommendations from his boss. We arrived during normal business hours but the doors were locked even though there were people visibly inside. The only responses to us at the door were stares... Still... We decided to go back last night because we were craving authentic Mexican tacos. We ordered the sopes to share in addition to our tacos (chicken and steak). The sopes were good, but more explanation on the variety that is available would've been nice when I asked about them -- a guy at the next table had some that were different and looked even better than ours.  The tacos were very dry and had little flavor, but there was no salt on our table to help boost what flavor there was. The green and red sauces were good but still couldn't make the tacos moist enough to enjoy. Apparently there are other things to order than what is on the "to go" menu we were given to order from (that was just a plain paper menu with much wear and tear). My husband's boss said he'd had some very good soup and there were empty tables holding semi-empty dishes with beans, rice, etc. Neither was on the menu nor offered to us -- if either were part of the "special," They weren't mentioned. The man serving us was very brief and didn't explain anything even when asked, but two other customers who came in speaking Spanish were treated very nicely. Probably won't return. Total bill was over $30 for not a lot of primarily bland, dry food.
Some of the best brunch food I've had in awhile. Big portions, great price and very friendly waiters. Will definitely return. Only downside was that they didn't accept credit cards and was cash only

The drinks!!! Oh man the drinks!!! I usually am not a drinker but if I drink I do it right... not once did I have to ask for my drinks to be stronger they were perfect, delicious! ... The food was good too, I don't do spicy and asked if my food was going to be spicy was told no, but it was... still good but had to trade with the bf his fish tacos were tasty :) desert was nice too.
Best soup dumpling in NY in my 4yrs here and great pancakes!!

Yuuuummm!  I had the sweet potato tacos.  The tacos were really simple and the ingredients were really fresh, especially the guacamole.  The atmosphere was really great -- lots of outdoor and indoor seating.

Chose to do dinner here based on Yelp reviews; was definitely pleased! Made a reservation, but the two floors don't seem to talk to each other, so they weren't sure where I was supposed to be. Outside of that, the place had good atmosphere, friendly staff, and was next to the Book of Mormon play. Though we didn't take advantage of it, they offer pre-order intermission drinks. My dining partner and I shared a pitcher of Brooklyn Lager; a nice amber that wasn't too hoppy, and had smooth flavor. We got a basket of bread cubes, seed to be a focaccia, dipped lightly in olive oil with a dash of rosemary. Good, albeit a little dry. I had the Spaghetti Alla Bolognese; thick noodle spaghetti, with a good helping of sauce. It came as is, no sides. Presentation was traditional, but clean. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and it was very filling, so be prepared to hold back if you have any antipasti or dessert to follow. My dining partner had Chicken Picatta. They really liked it. It came with some steamed garden vegetables, and crusted potato cubes. For a person who usually doesn't like vegetable, they ate them all! I tried their dish as well, and while the sauce was a little thicker and the chicken a little more breaded than I'm used to with my Picatta, I definitely liked. It lacked capers was the only thing of note. Overall, I would say it was a great dining experience! It's definitely $15~20, which is a little high if you're used to Dallas prices, but definitely well worth it! I would recommend, so long as it isn't busy.
New York strip was cooked perfectly.  Yukon mash potatoes was delicious.  Awesome service.  Definitely highly recommended!

The white clam pie is absolutely the best non-tomato pizza I have ever had, and within the top 3 pizzas I have had (Regina in Boston and John's in NYC).  The clams are FRESH, not canned, at least as far as I could tell.   And a special shoutout to SUSAN, a server who is a true pleasure - she adds to the seriously good vibe at Pepe's.
Great food, flavors are subtly magnificent and the care of preparation shows in the food. Service was top notch, not a beat missed. Will be back

I love this restaurant!  Great food and charming atmosphere.  The brunch menu is amazing.  The Nutella French Toast is sinfully delicious.  I also love the Sake Bloody Mary's (they are very spicy).  We have always had great service too!  If you go to weekend brunch be prepared to wait an hour or so.

So while I give Taim credit for their creative 'falafel balls', I despise being asked if I'd like some "Israeli salad" with it.
