Wow wow wow, best place in town was very lucky to get in as we didn't have a reservation and luckily enough some crazy people didn't show, straight away service was amazing we knew our cheeses but was schooled by our server, everything was amazing, we were all eating off each other's plates great time, just don't forget to pay your parking they wait for your car to expire as we set a time for exact and not a min before
Consistent and delicious. You can't go to Princeton and not eat here.

We had about 30  minutes to get in and out and they have no problem graciously and  quietly moving the courses through the time we had. The pasta with shrimp, although small shrimp. had a delicious kick to it - the squash dish was perfect, adding green olives for a salty addition - the melon/proscuitto was very nice - bibb salad was fine - fried cauliflower with a hint of lemon was a scrumptious side!

Have always ordered pizza for pickup since I live locally and after recently always will, was with another couple for a long evening it was early around 1015pm when I tried to get a pie after a few drinks when your little hissy fit host, wanted to charge me my wife and the couple we were with $6 a head for a cover for some metal band in the back, that's $24 before I even order a pie !!!!!?I told him repeatedly I'm just here for pizza, I asked him how can I get to eat without paying a cover charge, instead of solving the problem and handing me a menu while I stood behind to front door red-faced he replied you can call in, yes he is right but what the hell type of service is this !?!? After  exchanging some words he started flicking his fingers towards a server who I'm guessing was busy working for her to go fetch a menu, it was then I walked out the door, can't stand laziness, this would never happen at pepes lucky you have good pizza

I fondly call this place the "Capital of Hippie Food".  Meals here are inextricably linked to a long chain of Vermont-special memories.  One of the owners used to make delicious little tofu cubes at the Onion River Co-op about 15 years ago. He's still making those lovely tofu squares you will find them at Stone Soup. You never know what you are going to find on the hot bar, because they change the menu every day to take advantage of what's fresh, good or just inspired.  I've found every dish to be delicious and as a vegetarian who loves dairy, it's great to see options for all eaters. Had an amazing plate yesterday with cheesy millet, a vegan casserole a creamy tofu stew and that great old standby, steamed kale.  The toppings are all there - brewers yeast, local hot sauce, braggs amino acids, gomasio, etc.  The Ceylon Tea/Lemonade blend added a nice slightly sweet drink treat to the meal. You might not find any of these dishes here - but whatever you do have, it's likely to be well prepared, well seasoned and good for you. I'm not a huge fan of eating healthy for the sake of eating healthy.  Flavor and a nod to the sense of the pleasure of eating are equally (if not more) important. Yes, it's a bit pricey  - but anyone who shops healthy in a decent market should understand that freshness and quality don't come cheaply.  If you're looking for a cheap meal, go to Olive Garden.  If you want quality, freshness, bright flavors and food that nourishes you, head on over to Stone Soup. Stone Soup is a unique treasure that should be visited by anyone who appreciates good home cooked food in a casual setting.  I'm happy it's still around. And lastly, THANKS to you guys for hanging in there all these years and still producing food you can be proud of and the Burlington community can continue to enjoy.

I've only been to Cafeteria twice, and the first time was 5 years ago, however I remembered it being a good experience. I was disappointed to see that the polenta fries were not on the menu, however all I had to do was ask the waiter and he excitedly said I could order a side. They were amazing, and if you don't get the steak that they accompany, ask for a side order! The Wedge Salad was good, but a heavy start to my Mac and Cheese. They have 3 types and then a sampler of all 3. Yum. I regret that I forgot to take pictures until dessert came, but I guess I was too wrapped up in my cheese. I stated aloud "red velvet yodels" and the waiter heard and became so excited that he sat down and described them! His description really sold them, and they did not disappoint. Red velvet cake with cream cheese frosting rolled up and dunked in chocolate that hardened, served with a SIDE of vanilla milkshake! Well done. Beyond. All of the servers were great and it truly is affordable. It's said to be open 24/7, but it doesn't give the vibe of a late night messy haunt, so I assume a nice crowd comes in and keeps it classy.

The restaurant staff is courteous the food is less than average. Simply an overhyped place..certainly not worthy of the stars or the hype..look around in the immediate vicinity you will find much better restaurants ..Avoid this !!
As always, Roia was delicious. My favorite dish of the night was the Carpaccio di Funghi (Mushrooms!) and the pannacotta with cherry compote. Great wine recommendation!
I would love to bring my mother here
Friendly and prompt service. The food was nothing short of fantastic and full of flavor. It's a hopping joint that would also be great for some evening drinks.

My girlfriend and I went to Tuome on opening night last night for our anniversary. I had flowers with me and the staff was very accommodating, offering to store them in a cool spot in the back. The decor is rustic with much of the paneling, fixtures, and decorations coming from old Philadelphia factories (our server was kind enough to educate us on the wall of wool spools behind us). Tuome's ambiance is not dissimilar to a West Village wine bar: candle-lit, chock-full of well-heeled 30-something couples, and long on exposed brick and reclaimed wood. Perhaps in ironic acknowledgement that it is very squarely in grungy hipster territory and far from Greenwich's angular cobblestone streets and $10mm lofts, Tuome's playlist ran the gamut of 80's high school dance classics - from Asia's 'Heat of the Moment' to Abba's Dancing Queen. Somehow it worked marvelously. The wine list is well-considered with relatively affordable selections and a token rose for girls' night groups that couldn't get a reservation in Midtown. In our own irony, we ordered beer ($7, from a short, but remarkably well-curated selection) and the Mexican Coca Cola ($4). The chef's amuse was delightful - a well-balanced, subtle offering of pickled vegetables with an Asian touch. Restaurants that resemble any relation to the bygone fusion era are always at risk of producing flavors that conjure memories of some panko-breaded slider with teriyaki dipping sauce gone awry. Luckily Tuome avoids this gracefully. The ginger-scallion sauce is just right. Our next dishes - watermelon with farro and chrysanthemum ($12) and chicken liver with milk toast, sunflower seeds, and local maple syrup ($13) are marvelous. They embody the inventive yet harmonious combination of familiar flavors in crisp, bright, unique preparations that is the greatest hallmark of modern cooking. After a long lull (a bizarre pause to an otherwise good tempo of service), we received our mains: scallops with carrot puree and maitake ($25) and beef short-rib with sweet potato puree and grilled shishito peppers ($28). Diners have long come to expect a standard of perfect or near-perfect protein preparation and Chen does not disappoint here. The beautiful sear on the scallops does not come at the expense of its smooth, tender flesh. Likewise, the braised short-rib maintains its form long enough to stand upright on the plate but absolutely melts in your mouth. Chen tends toward the sweeter end of flavors on the proteins but this is a minor shortcoming and easy to forgive. Where Chen excels is his obsessive attention to texture - our side of snap peas ($8) was crisp yet tender with peanuts for additional crunch, and the sweet lotus root chips perched atop the delicate scallops provide the perfect contrast. We were disappointed to learn that dessert was not on the menu for the evening, but after such a wonderful first experience, we'll surely be back for more.

The restaurant is quaint and dark and perfect for a date although the place was empty besides one other table and they placed us right next to them so we asked to be moved. The dumplings were delicious but my Pad Thai was a bit soggy. I like for the noodle to be soft but not like it would be inside a soup. I wanted to try something new but I think I'll stick to Circles for now.
Best soup dumplings I've had in awhile!

My first choice for a buffet is Dosa Grill, that's mostly because of the quality of the food they offer. You get to pick your own variety of dosa which comes free with ever buffet. Based the food taste I assume that they always use quality ingredients. Their wife variety of Vegetarian food would be preferred choice for many veggie folks. Next best thing about this place is their staffs are very friendly and helpful. They also maintain this place very clean. During week end they buffet is costs you few extra bucks but it's ok as that's when they add few extra dishes as well. Leaving the buffet aside their dishes during dinner is also superior, specially their gongura dosa is very awesome, you got to try it once
Loved the food here. It is definitely pricey for the portion they serve but worth it.

Went to Tavern on Jane last night with my sons, husband and a work colleague.  We love coming to the city for work, and it was a rare treat to have my family along. Big disappointment, which was such a shame considering all the good reviews and all of the truly great places to eat in the city.  First, it's a bar, just a bar. And sort of a smelly, not so clean bar.   It's way loud, though the music was good.   The food was so completely average.  The service got progressively worse as our waitress must have clocked out and didn't tell us and then we weren't really paid attention to.  And the bill for 5 of us was over $300 - no bottles of wine or anything fancy.  Probably 5 wine/cocktails total, couple of burgers and 3 entrees. 1 dessert.  But all so very average.   Only exciting thing about the night was the big drug bust right outside.   I wanted a cozy, Village place with brick walls and candles...had brick and candles, I guess. Not sure what everyone is so excited about.
The nicest wait staff around. Risotto to die for. Only wish they'd been around when my office was around the corner. I'd have taken a time share on a table. Love this place!!!!

2.5 Stars purely for the service and atmosphere. The staff and atmosphere gave me confidence that the whole dining experience was going to be good, but sadly the food was a huge let down. Escargot were extremely bland and of questionable freshness. No flavors, not even salt, was able to be infused into the meat. French onion soup was executed really poorly. All but 1/2 ounce of liquid had been reduced down to just a salty slurry. The flavors hinted at the potential, but alas it was a failure. Cote de Boeuf was not good. It was overcooked by at least two degrees of doneness, which should have been apparent when they sliced it for us. The flavors itself weren't very inspiring either, just loaded with crushed peppercorns. For $120, it should at least be mediocre. I certainly would not trust them with guests I am entertaining, but I might give them another shot down the road. Hope it was just an off night.

This is a great new little spot on Astoria Blvd.  Its really a pure takeout spot.  Food was very very good and very fresh.  They made the dumplings in front of me.  They have several sauces they use, all were delicious.  Had the chicken empanada, playeros, and pork dumplings.  We will definitely be back again soon.
I love this place. Everything is delicious and the atmosphere is comfortable. I would go back again and again.

I love the food! For appetizer we ate oysters! Bread:)steak is amazing! Lobster is great! Creamy spinach! Mash potato! Lava cake! Raspberry sorbet and vanilla ice cream with cappuccino!! Yammi! And I really like French rose wine from Angelina Jolie! Now it's my favourite!

Delicious from start to finish! Had dinner there last night and I am really impressed! First off, our server was fantastic and attentive.  He suggested many dishes for us to try and he was not kidding about how good they are.  We had the 1  burrata salad, which was so refreshing 2. Red Snapper ceviche, WOW! must have, the chef brought it out to us himself and told us it's his best creation thus far 3. Octopus Angry tacos, so tasty, 4. Shrimp Angry tacos, good, but if you like octopus, I'd go with those, 5. Grilled skirt steak, tender and tasty, and the cheese fritters are sinfully good 6. Pork Shoulder Rigatoni, Oh em gee, it's all I want to eat ever again, forever! The general manager then brought out some desserts to make up for our long wait for a table which was so nice and thoughtful of him! Standouts were the melba donuts and the napoleon, YUM!! Everything was delicious, the long wait was totally worth it, service was impeccable, and I'll definitely be back.

Nico is literally attached to NJPAC, making it THE dining choice before a show there. Or one would think. On the upside, the food was very good and the staff was pleasant. The service was awful, and if you scroll thru these reviews, you'll see this complaint often. We sat for 20 minutes before anyone came to take an order. The food arrived quickly - actually, too quickly - with the server trying to take away our half finished appetizers to make room for the entrees. Awkward. Entree was thoroughly enjoyable. Then, we sat. And sat. And sat. No one came to offer a drink, dessert, the check, anything. Had to flag down a bus boy to find our server. 20 minutes later, offered our expensive cocktails TO GO because it was showtime. Fail.

First thing you will notice is how cozy this place is. It's wonderful.  The ambience is like you step away from the busy street and be absorbed in the music they set up.  Think soft jazz or soft trance. Every table has a little candle, and flowers and is welcoming.   The waiter we had was a darling, he was very attentive in helping us select drinks, food and recommendations.  Unlike some waiters I have had in other places,  he was doing things at the right pace.   The food!   Gosh,  that day I was hungry and ordered so much.  Gua bao to start with though a little pricy is refreshing, and filling for one large person.  I'd say get two lol.  The dumplings were crispy through out. And had very good stuffed pork. And my entree the avocado bibop was freaking good. I added some eggs and meat and it is worth it.  I hope to go back again soon,  every  entrees you get will be stamped on a card where you can get a  free one.  I hope to claim it soon. Yay.
Been coming here for over 20 years.  Same owners, consistent quality, best fast Chinese food I have ever had.  Super fast, clean and great food.
Not that good...much better Italian in the city.  Staff was a disgrace.. Food subpar, only plus byob.

The best roast pork in the city, and arguably the best cheese steak.  I'd be much heavier if the place was open late.  Can't comment on anything else they make as the two aforementioned options are so good that I haven't been tempted to try anything else.

Decided to give this restaurant another try after a year of staying away after a "bad" experience.  Was close and relative up for visit.  Ordered the lo mien noodles, chix fingers, veg fried rice and veg egg rolls, all to share.  GREASY, GREASY, GREASY.  Lo mien noodles very slimy and oily tasting with hardly ANY VEGGIES.  Chix fingers and veg egg rolls still greasy even after blotting.  Veg fried rice bland tasting with not many veggies.  What is wrong with them?  Do they need a new cook?  Not consistent in their product.  I hope they read these comments and IMPROVE as nice family run  but sad to say, think this is the last time I will try them....

Great for authentic sushi lovers. The flavors are all immersed in the fish. For anyone who likes to dip their sushi in soy sauce think again. The waitress told us "NO NO not good idea"!!!! The place is very simple yet has an elegant style at the same time. We had a small sake bottle and the omakse and it was almost $200 for two. Not your typical japanese dinner but great for special occasions.

I'm sorry, Kim, but you have let me down.  This restaurant is a testament to the fact the yelp star rating alone is no guarantee of a good experience.  Perhaps the quality of sushi is the redeeming factor, and I can attest that my Jorge roll with eel was indeed very spicy and generally delectable; but I must, nevertheless, address the otherwise imperfect experience. Having maneuvered my car into the incredibly cramped and poorly laid-out parking lot in the back, we made a few circles around the building to find the entrance (it's located next to the parking area).  The hand-written paper sign on the door indicated what the waitress confirmed upon entry: the restaurant is closed at 3, and everyone must evacuate the premises in 30 minutes.  It was 2:30. Can we stay a bit longer?  No, unfortunately. The restaurant's cramped and uninspiring interior made me feel uneasy.  Perhaps we shouldn't have been seated?  After rushing through the food, we left.  Small restaurants can be cozy, but I did not get this feeling at Kim's.  At least the sushi seemed relatively fresh and tasty.

I had been interested in visiting this place since I first read about them opening.  The draw for me is the pinball, which is difficult to find these days.  I'm happy to report that they more than met my expectations.  As for the games, a good assortment, fairly priced, and arranged so that you have enough room to play. The ambiance was a good (and unique) combination of bar, arcade, and casual dining restaurant.  Initially I thought I would just check out the pinball, but decided to get a bite to eat too.  I had their white bean chile with corn bread, which was very good.  I wouldn't mind seeing some kind of veggie burger on the menu, as well as a fish option (sandwich or fish and chips) but, as it is, the menu is creative and fresh.   So, if you have a yen for pinball or other classic arcade games, or a beer and some quality food, I'd check them out.
I'm originally from Szechuan, this is only place I can taste a little my hometown favor in NJ&PA area.

I honestly don't know how this restaurant gets such rave reviews.  Me and my girls took a taxi from the Bronx to Brooklyn to try this restaurant after reading all of the glowing reviews on Yelp.  This atmosphere is fantastic and the waiters are courteous and helpful. The bathrooms are clean. But IMO the food is just all right.  Reading the reviews my mouth watered and I couldn't wait to try the pecan encrusted pork chops with sweet potatoes and collards.  Pork chops were just o.k. - thin and kind of dry.  Sweet potatoes were good but then again it's hard to mess up a sweet potato. Collards were good.  My sister had a salmon burger with fries. Fries were excellent; salmon burger was just o.k. My other sister had baked or steamed salmon.  She said it was dry.  Someone else said the macaroni was definitely on point. I had some kind of shrimp spring roll as an appetizer that DID NOT have any shrimp in it!!! The drinks were weak - too much ice, not enough liquor. The first few sips were o.k. and then it was like drinking koolaid.  Not only that, it took about 45 minutes for our food to come.  Maybe I should have had the chicken and waffles that everyone raves about instead
Can't go wrong with this place. Works for brunch, dinner, and dates. Highly recommend the bi bim bap.

This pizza is so yummy!  They have an arugula pizza that makes you feel like pizza is a healthy choice. Its great for date night and a group of friends. I really love this place.  Try what ever speciality pizza they have when you go, you can't go wrong. I have found interesting flavors on pizza that I never thought would work.
Magic food, we went there in a large Group and everyone was really happy with their meals.
This is my spot for a cheese steak big good and affordable ps ..go early the spot is in THE HOOD
The best coffee I try one of the barista s creations Call the 59 under the bridge The most delicious ice coffee ever

I really love this place! It has great ambiance and the food is very good not to mention the selection of wines! I had the lobster club for brunch with some mimosas . Great for a gathering and romantic date as well. They are also having a Cocorico Wine and Appetizer launch party on Wednesday 8/20!  See the tip!
This place is really good! One of the best cheesesteak  I've ever had. ( I personally think their 100x better than Pats and Genos) small  and very friendly environment. Highly recommended.

Their meat is perfectly seasoned. The wait time isn't long. You'd most likely have to order two rolls, as one roll isn't really that filling. However the staff has a small issue with waste management. If you owned a restaurant, how would you want your staff to handle the garbage? A. During downtime when there are less people in the restaurant. B. Through the back door in the alley (if this is possible) C. During dinner time, persistently shove two carts of garbage through the line of a dozen people waiting to order/waiting for their order, and nudge a baby carriage along the way. ...They chose C.

One of the best veggie ramens in the city.  I wish they had more than one option for vegetarians, but I've never been disappointed with what arrives.  The noodles are always well prepared and the broth is flavorful without being too salty.
Good place for some tapas and wine. I remember this place wow'ing me a bit more my first time around years ago. It's still a great pit stop while in Soho.

Absolutely fresh and delicious! Back in LP for a bit and I've headed to i Sushi three times in ten days. Added bonus: the owners are friendly and thoughtful. Will return...need to order the daily specials...

This place is great if not slightly too expensive. To eat, we had the adobada, pollo and asada tacos and we threw in an extra asada tostada just to try it. The tostada was great and we liked that adobada the best. In addition to this we got a little cup of the spicy salsa which is genuinely spicy but honestly worth the pain. If you are looking for something to accompany the food I suggest the horchata and the jamaica.

My coworker and I were on extended business travel and we were looking for a place near our job site that was going to offer us the ability to sit down for a while.  We had a moment and fast food was not going to be for dinner.  While the area on Roosevelt does not have many options,  after driving back and forth between major intersections we opted for this restaurant.   As we pulled in the overall decor out side is not striking as very nice.  We walked in the front door and were shocked as we stepped into a bar. I immediately thought uhoh this is not the place that I intended. Pretty quickly we realize that the regular dining room area is in the back.  We made our way back to a table and was seated.  Now we're cooking!  White table cloth, comfortable surroundings in a Tuscan style themed dining room. We were immediately served our drinks of ice tea and water and given fresh bread rolls. We both decided to have the special which was the Prime Rib with a house salad, yellow rice and boiled cabbage. The special price was listed as $14.00, which we both agree is a pretty good deal. As hungry meat eaters we were now content to relax and enjoy our salad as we waited for our main entrée. When our server brought our plates I actually laughed out loud as the dinner plates were bigger than I have ever seen. I think they were actually supposed to be platters? I wish I had a tape measure but I swear it had to be at least 30 inches across. My buddy immediately challenged the waiter and asked if what we ordered was Prime Rib, as it had bones in it. Our server assured us both that indeed it was Prime Rib. As our server left we both looked at each other and we really didn't understand why the plate looked like a bony fatty grisly price of meat.  I told my buddy that at least they got the cow part right,  he said it could be horse? I replied that it is likely cow but it didn't even come with Au Jus or horseradish. After attempting to saw through this very very tough piece of meat I decided I had enough asked for the waiter again. My friend continued to eat his as his was cooked less than mine even though we ordered it exactly the same way.  The waiter got very frustrated and states that we ordered the prime rib even though I had pulled a picture of what it was supposed to look like on my phone.  He left for the kitchen and came back with a raw chunk and confidently reaffirmed that we ordered the prime rib. After a few rounds and going back and forth between us we came to realize that it is "grilled prime rib" as per the main menu but the special menu hadn't specified grilled. Overall the waiter removed mine from my ticket as I couldn't eat it. I will give three stars as he did end up taking the meal off the check but overall the entire experience was poor. I ended up stopping for a sub sandwich for my "dinner".  I won't be going back.
Been here 3 times.  My favorite is the beef tendon soup (1103) The pork cutlet is good, but the broth is very neutral.

Their tacos are amazing -- best fish taco I've ever had. Great atmosphere, great service -- the fact that they're a little off the beaten path is a plus, because if they weren't they'd be insanely crowded.

We showed up with ten people in our party , four adults and six teenage boys and EVERYONE enjoyed the food.  As a group we ordered a variety of items and we loved it all!  The owner was very nice and the restaurant was nice, cozy, and clean.  I highly recommend this place to my friends and family.  Next time we are in Newark we will definitely be back.
Good dumplings.
The food is good. The service and noise level annoying. You're better off ordering at their to-go window.

This place has really good food quality and is a short distance walk from my house. The staff is really fun to talk to and everyone is nice. The queso burrito is really good. It's very expensive but the food makes up for it. The tables are clean and everyone takes this job seriously. Overall a pretty good restaurant.

My coworkers and I were so excited to try this place out because the reviews looked good and we were starving. 1. We were told it would be 5 minutes to get a table after being ignored for 10 minutes. There were 3 two-tops and 1 four-top tables open. Then, we waited for 40 minutes, not 5 to be re-acknowledged. After being re-acknowledged, we were seated after 10 minutes. 2. I swear we were skipped twice as they do not take names for a waiting list. This one group of 5 said they came 1 hour prior to us but didn't give a name and as soon as they arrived back, they were sat immediately. They were friends with the host. Where was the waiting list???? 3. After sitting, we were then told cash only. Why the hell wouldn't you disclaim that when greeting is for a table first? Or at least have a sign? We were so upset and disappointed in their service and attitude. 4. It's BYOB. I wish I could speak on their food but if their food is anything like their service and host, I bet it's awful. Unfortunately, I wanted to give this place no stars but you have to at least give one even though they are unworthy of one. Advice for the host working 8/13: Firstly, greet your customers and tell them you'll be right with them. Don't ignore people no matter how busy you are. Secondly, let your customers know it's cash only. Lastly, make and take a name for the waiting list.

Great atmosphere to have dinner and drinks, great playa for guys night oht and dinner with the wife. Food is great , I ordered the blackened salmon and loved every bite , shrimp app - also amazing prices are cheap for what it is !!! Only thing we did not like was the fact that we had to wait for almost a hour to be seated both times that we went there. Other than that, all and all we would recommend and def will be going back again!

Really liked this place. Not the best sushi I've ever had but definitely good for this area. The service and atmosphere are pleasant. Sat at the bar for a meal by myself and enjoyed it. Places in Princeton are preferable, like Tomo Sushi, but if you're looking for tasty sushi at a clean local spot, definitely come here.

This place is a self-congratulating joke. I have so much to say, mostly negative. Let me walk you through the lowlights of the meal we had this past Thursday. While reviewing the menu, my wife mentioned to the very chipper waiter that she was torn between the duck and something else for her main course. The following exchange ensued: Waiter: Have you ever had duck? Wife: Uh, yes. Waiter: Then this will be the best duck you've ever had. This moronic response from the waiter was our first significant clue that it was going to be a rough night. Why would the waiter assume that we were so inexperienced as to have never had duck (we're both in our late 30s, not, say, Yale kids)? And on what basis could the waiter possibly assess how this duck would compare to other renditions of duck we've had, having no idea where else we've eaten? To me, this exchange epitomized the condescending yet incompetent meal that was to follow. After orders were taken, about 40 minutes passed before the appetizers appeared. During that time, no bread basket was brought, and no amuse bouche was served. It was not unreasonable to expect those items because we eventually got them during other parts of the meal. Indeed, the amuse bouche was served while we were in the middle of eating our (hot) appetizers. So, that was a major screwup. But it was exacerbated by the comedy of errors that ensued. As the waiter was serving my amuse bouche, he spilled it, and the glass fell into and knocked over my water glass. We didn't care about the spill. What galled us was that the waiter never apologized and made no attempt to clean anything up. So, we ate our hot appetizers and cold amuse bouche simultaneously while looking at a wet Jackson Pollock-esque tablecloth. By the way, the chilled spicy corn soup was actually very good; the squash blossom "beignet" was decent, but frankly not as good as the similar dish at ULC's casual sister restaurant, Bar Bouchee. The amuse bouche was dull and wouldn't have been enjoyed even if served at the appropriate moment and without spillage. Anyway, by the time we'd finished our amuse bouche/appetizer course, the water+amuse bouche had started streaming onto my wife's dress. I called the waiter over to point this out. He said something like, "Oh, I guess I should clean this up." I responded, "No, you need to move us to another table." He complied. Miraculously, upon being seated at the new table, we were given a bread basket. I can't possibly understand why we didn't get this immediately after placing our order. Nor can I understand why the restaurant decided to give it to us upon moving us to the new table. If intended as a gesture of apology, it was ill-conceived: the waiter still hadn't apologized; it's just bread - indeed, everyone else seemed to get bread after ordering; and it was terrible. The multi-grain bread was stale; it had presumably been cut hours earlier. The white flour bread was wan and flaccid. Eventually, our main courses arrived but did not brighten our mood at all. The duck was trimmed very badly. The skin had not been rendered properly and therefore was so thick still that we could not even cut it with a knife, let alone chew it. There was a big flap of duck on the side, as if the chef had started cutting and then changed his mind, stopped mid-cut, and started over 1/8 of an inch over. And  some parts of the duck had 2 thick tendons running through it, rendering that part inedible as well. The chicken was edible only if eaten with the tomato compote because otherwise the sauce on it was too bitter. This was the bitterness not of, say, greens, but of overcooking, that is, I'm pretty sure they burned their sauce. The potato macaire that accompanied the chicken was unfortunately  overpowered by all the garlic in it. On the bright side, we'd had the foresight to order a side of pommes frites, which were pretty good and got us through to dessert. (Let me also say that nothing we saw on the menu was remotely inventive, so it all comes down to execution.) We'd planned to order two desserts, but given how things were going, we chickened out and stuck only with our earlier-ordered souffle, which was perhaps slightly eggy but otherwise quite good. After then seeing some of the other desserts making the rounds, we had a twinge of regret that we hadn't ordered another dessert. It occurred to us that the pastry chef may be playing at a different level from his or her colleagues in the front and back of the house. Alas, we'll never know because we're never going to return to ULC. The waiter never let on that he had any concern about how the meal went. He didn't inquire as to why my wife had barely touched her duck. As soon as I signed the check, we bolted for the door. If anyone on the staff had asked how the meal was, they would have gotten an earful, but no one was anywhere in sight.

Amazing place ! I had a chicken dish Mediterranean style amazing seasoning ! Food and service was really great people were very friendly I am going back! But I wish the have more food ?? lol amazing sports bar spot got to keep it in mind for an event!!! Ps get the free range chicken it was amazing!!!!!!!!

We had a group of six and we were seated for drinks at a hightop in no time, although the place was packed (we went on a Friday night around 11). We had amazing service and enjoyed our time. Good music, great atmosphere, and plenty of bathrooms so no wait! Overall we had an excellent time and will be back to try the food next time.

I can only comment on the donuts ( didn't have any chicken) and they were AMAZING!!! We came at around 4 pm, so the specialty donuts were sold out, but we got a dozen regular donuts and split those between lemon, vanilla, and brown sugar cinnamon. All were still warm, fresh made, and glorious! The only reason for FOUR stars is these donuts don't keep well. Once they have cooled their texture becomes very dry.

I went here on a recent business visit with a colleague from China and suggested that  he order from the menu. The food was  authentic and the flavors were very deep and satisfying. We ate spicy cold noodles for appetizers, which was quite good. The tofu and fish special was spicy and fabulous. The deep fried shrimps were large and cooked with lots of red chilies, again outstanding. The dry cooked beef was also delicious. Even though we ordered smaller dishes, we had lots of leftovers so plan accordingly. They were out of the red sangria so we hesitantly ordered the white sangria instead. It was sweeter than expected but we liked it so much we ordered seconds . This is a must go to place especially if you are a fan of authentic schezwan food.
EVERYTIME I visit Newark, I gotta stop at HOBBY's. Combo # 5 is the only thing i get. the size of the sandwich is AWSOME and I ABSOLUTELY LOVE the coleslaw

Beer selection was alright but the staff was terrible. Despite my best efforts I couldnt get a drink at the bar to save my life, the bartender walked by us and our empty glasses on multiple occasions. When it came time to pay our tab, just flagging down anyone who worked there proved difficult, we finally got the attention of one of the bartenders who asked my name and promptly left. She came back 15 minutes later only to ask my name again. The bar was not packed, I dont understand why everything was so difficult. The final nail in the coffin came as we were leaving, the bartender spilled an entire beer on my helmet and cell phone. I didnt get an apology, she just tossed me a dirty bar towel. I had to ride home with a helmet that reeked of beer, I dont know if I'll be able to get the smell out. There are too many other bars to waste your time at this one.
A great hidden gem! The food is daring, but not so adventurous to scare off the less courageous eater. The food is delectable, the service is friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and inviting.

It was my first time being in Philly and I had a cheesesteak with Provolone cheese and it was just average. The meat wasn't too juicy. I've had better cheesesteaks in Richmond VA. The fries were really really good though. But this isn't a place I need to come back to, it was good to try.
Good chicken and waffles

It was good when I went but I think I was expecting to much. All my friends and family said it was a really nice and really fancy restaurant. The fancy part was pretty much accurate but I wasn't a big fan of the food. We ordered an appetizer which was a simple Mexican dish, chips and guac. The chips were hard and cold and the guacamole was pretty good the I got this taco sampler which looked very appetizing when the server brought it out. But I didn't like it all for some reason the tastes didn't go together. I was a little  disappointed but they seem to be doing good with the line of customers out the door.
$22 for 5 tiny scallops, don't waste your time. Those scallops should have been on the appetizer menu. Very nice bartender and okay vibe too bad the overpriced food ruined the experience.

Went on a Monday, atmosphere was what I expected, quiet but really enjoyable. It's a bar, dark. It was my first time there and was made to feel at home like a regular. The staff was awesome. Their Long Island ice tea was NICE. I had veggie dumplings, so good I had to get more. Place was spacious I would definitely go again.

Food is extremely tasty and this comes from a native New Yorker who loves local Dominican and Spanish food. My favorite dish is their pernil. Free delivery over $10. One star was docked bc their weekday delivery time during lunch is way too long. Average wait time is 1hr. Usually it's well over an hour, max being 1hr 30 mins. Order well in advance!

I finally went to the lobster pound in Red Hook. I'm sorry but nothing special there. Way to far to go for a Lobster roll that's O.K. The reason why I say it's just O.K. is because they skimp on the amount of lobster you get. They put the lobster on a bed of lettuce in the roll. Really..... Why? You say I should ask? To save on the amount of lobster you get. It's like an Illusion, that works. It looks and feels like your getting a nice size lobster roll. The lettuce is nothing more than a filler. That's why I gave it two stars. I felt cheated out of my money. If you have to have a lobster roll fix, Luke's is way better. You get a generous portion of lobster. No lettuce there. IF YOU WANT THE BEST AND TASTIEST LOBSTER ROLL  IN NYC  go to Lobster House in City Island.  NOW THAT'S WORTH THE TRIP! It cost a little more but you get fresh fried potato chips with the roll. So good. Oh did I mentioned the view? I don't mind sharing my secrets with the world when I have a great experience. Red Hook is off the beaten path, but certainly worth a visit for a day. They have good restaurants and bars. I suggest to do some research and plan ahead of time. I will return to red hook but it won't be to the lobster pound.  I happen to stumble across a wonderful art gallery called Brooklyn WaterFront Artist Coalition. A must go to place to visit and buy art if you have the extra cash. You don't have to take my word for it, go and find out for yourself.

This cafe just opened up in my building and it's great. The owners are really nice and eager to adapt the menu to what customers want. They have sandwiches, pastries, breakfast omelettes and of course coffee. I really like the brisket sandwich. It's on a nice little corner here around Steinway and has a pretty cool vibe going on.

Wanted to find a good place to dine on my birthday and a random google search landed me here. Assumed it will be a small place but was blown away from entrance to the dining to the after effect of the amazing ambience with string lights, al fresco dining, live drum beat music revving up the feel, and energy packed summery place! Felt right on the Cuban planet and didn't feel like I was in jersey for those few hours. Great service, delicious tapas, amazing place! Best in montclair!

In our short trip to NYC we visited this place twice. Excellent rolls at very reasonable prices. The chai is great as well. Very well managed and their Manager Scott is very friendly and runs a good operation.

Excellent food, poor service! Had made reservations 3 weeks prior to going. My party and I arrive a little late and we were taken to the back of the restaurant and was told to stand there while the young lady went to check on something. After of five minutes of waiting, we were finally seated. Our server comes over, never introducing herself, carrying 4 water glasses, there were 5 of us. She then comes over and asks us if we would like to hear the specials. Another person rolls over this huge black board, behind my mother's back and walks away.  Finally our server comes and takes our orders. We all were finished eating and 3 of us needed things to be boxed. She asked only one person and before anyone could say anything, she was gone. That's how our entire visit was like. Then I find out that she wasn't happy with our tip, well I'm a hairdresser, the better the service, the better the tip!!

We love Patsy Grimaldi!  Favorite pizza in Brooklyn, and Patsy is such a nice guy.  Don't bother standing in line at Grimaldi's (no longer owned by Patsy) for the pale imitation when this is the real thing!
The tom yam fried rice is just takes you to a whole different level. It is juicy, fresh and spicy. The staffs are so nice and the they bring the best service.

I wanted to like this place, I really did. I read all the reviews and it sounded great, so maybe expectations were high, but I don't think I'll go back. our first issue was not being served immediately, even though there were people who came after we did who gave their orders before we even got menus.  We had to flag a waitress to finally get a menu. But that isn't the reason for the low rating, as you never know what staffing is like on a particular day, and our waitress was lovely once we got her attention.  It was the lackluster food.   I ordered a breakfast burrito, which was almost inedible. It consisted of watery, unseasoned and crumbly scambled eggs with some token veggies in a fairly dry tortilla., and a smattering of cheese somewhere, but very bland. The only seasoning consisted of side sauces, and I have to say there was a chipotle sauce that was delicious and nicely spicy, but they should have integrated spices  or even a little salt or pepper or herbs into the base product.  If you douse the crumbly mess with the sauce, it's a little tasty, but just not integrated.   Call me old fashioned, but food should be seasoned properly and not require heavy dousing with condiments to make it edible. I only ate about a third of it that was it. My friend ordered the one thing that might be a specialty, the lemon ricotta pancakes. I shared bites of that, and it was indeed nice, if not as awesome as reviews would lead you to believe. If I were to go again, I'd order that and skip any kind of egg dish. The other issue is the comfort factor. Yes, the industrial thing looks nice but the small, hard metal chairs that squeek on the floor were simply uncomfortable.
Had their chicken pot pie and it was great.

Very consistent. We order take out and every time the food arrives hot and delicious. The ribs fall off the bone. French fries are hot and crispy. Gravy is thick and good. Flounder filet was deelish too. All good things. Definitely try the ribs.
We had Villa Salad and Ravioli with meat balls both were Delicious and YUMM .. I totally loved it.

They say "you can't make a meal out of side dishes."  It's true. The service and fig salad were both phenomenal, but that's about it. Upon entry we were courteously greeted and made our way to the packed bar to get a drink until our table was ready. We were promptly seated and greeted by our friendly server. We started our meal with e delightful fig salad. It was light and refreshing and the vanilla bean vinaigrette was amazing. After that we had the "ricotta." I understand the limitations of ricotta with vegan meals, but they had used way too much lemon in the tofu mixture. The texture was there, but it honestly tasted like Trix cereal. Sorry, vegans, Trix are for kids. From there we an order of the chickpea fries. We were warned ahead of time that the portions would be tapas style meant to share ("to gain the full experience"). The fries came out on a plate that looked like someone just smeared aioli with their finger across it. The fries were stacked perfectly like a little chickpea log cabin... All ten of them. They had the taste, texture, and appearance of Lincoln logs. There was barely enough aioli to cut down the dryness of what I can only assume was reclaimed fried hummus. To cap off our meal we had baby leeks with romesco (Which admittedly I was excited to read as romanesco... Not the same thing) and the heirloom beans. Both tasted wonderful but were laughably small, even as tapas. Throughout this experience we sampled many of the drinks, all of which were served in glasses barely half full, is there a liquor shortage we're unaware of? Is this place supposed to be prohibition themed? No, they actually don't seem to have a theme. From their crystal chandeliers to the green lamps above the bar to the LED lights on the bar and book shelves, from the teal painted walls to the curtained wall with classic black and white films projected on loop, there's a whole lot going on without much to say. Charlie was a sinner, but he also probably had the appetite of a small bird. Guys, I think Charlie was a bird. It is their logo after all.
GREAT FOOD!  recommend making a reservation

The Real Deal:  great 'cue, friendly vibe, no pretense, happy times. Drinks:  nicely curated selection of beers, ciders, wines and sodas. Wines by the glass looked appealing, but I always go for beer or soda with BBQ.  This time it was Abita's Jockamo IPA for me and (if I remember well) Ace Apple Honey Cider for the Missus.  Great choices both. Appies:  Love the Mac 'n' Cheese!  A sandwich-plate-sized cast iron skillet, baked to runny perfection and miles past al dente.  Everyone (except the well-loved gluten-free among us) must try! Meats:  Nothing bad in our bunch:  A+ ribs, Solid A brisket, A- turkey and pulled pork.  And we are tough graders!  Those who said "meh" to the eponymous brisket may have come late at night, encountering dryness or other cause for a culinary joy deficit.  Our brisket was tender, juicy, well-rubbed and plain delectable.  The turkey was truly a pleasant surprise:  moist, with just-right smokiness, a red meat antidote worthy of its plate-mates.  But the ribs were declared king of the mountain, and we ordered another half-pound to take home.  Woo hoo indeed! Sides:  We stuck to the greens (no beans) and had no regrets. Collards maybe a little strong on the vinegar, but cooked to a succulent, no-crunch firmness.  Potato salad was dressed in a peppery, savory secret sauce. Pies:  Stuffed to the brim by all of the above, we ordered a Chess Pie to go.  Can't wait to tuck in! Service:  Chatty, but not too; prompt (on a busy Saturday evening); helpful in navigating the shoals of portion sizes.  Much appreciated.   Waiting Time:  5 - 10 minutes for a table for four at about 8pm on a summer Saturday WHEN CAN WE GO BACK AND BRING A CROWD OF FRIENDS????
Great ambience, great pizza (big enough to share for 2  if you are ordering other things). Try their avocodo sandwich. SO GOOD!

Have been dining at this location for 20 years, been enjoying the food under the new name and diamonds management. We have been going about once a week, food is fantastic. Recently celebrated my wife's birthday, about 8 of us. Again, food was great. But the moment we sat down we were very rushed. Server kept interrupting conversation and practically took my food off table before I finished. Too bad, would have ordered more cocktails.

You can chew their seafood forever, and swallow the whole piece still. Pork chops were dry. The staik ordered as rare came well-done, with at least quater of it being pure fat. The service was good, as were side items such as bread.
I went here with 3 of my co-workers and we all loved it!  The food is so so good! The rice balls, chicken, you name it, it was delicious!
I had the Ishka steak (provolone, spinach, roasted peppers) - delicious.  Had some juice to it.  Nice roll, good mix of meat and topping.  Need a few more peppers to get a 5 star.

Finally I have a minute to review one of my absolutely favorite spots in Bay Ridge.  Every time me and my boyfriend visiting Campania, we have such a pleasing time. Efficient service, delicious food, cozy atmosphere, and last but not least, is the music. LOVE IT! They play soul music and oldies...Al Green, Frank Sinatra.. not too loud, not too quiet, very tasteful like the place itself:-) And just a few words about  Jimmy- Professionalism, Charisma, Smile:-) With Love, Ammon and Liliya.
Really really good food. Service was great and it's not what you imagine when you think of a diner..more upscale. lots of options to choose from. Will definitely make this a regular spot.

Delicious at 2pm or 2am after a night of dollar beers at 13 step! Accepts cards with no minimum. A regular will fill up 2 people. Sauces to try: Sweet Mango Chutney, Vietnamese Pineapple, Sweet Chili, Dill Pesto

I really, really like this place. Banging ambiance. Fast and friendly service. Lotion in the bathroom. All they're missing is french fries. Kudos for the delicious, fresh, very well seasoned crab roll...with 2 types of creamy aioli. But I could have really used some french fries. The potatoes were probably organic and the broccoli was not over cooked. For $2 I could have really used an entire ear of corn instead of half an ear, but because y'all looked out for the parents with a baby high chair I forgive. All in all, a great restaurant, but come y'all...add some fries to the menu. Peace.

Consistently great. I just moved from San Francisco, and I used to eat at the one downtown. The West Hartford location is just as good. My favorites orders are the Chinese Chicken Chop Salad (480 cal), and the Japanese Pan Noodles with Steak (790 cal). Each are about $9 and great for lunch or dinner. Service has always been excellent, and polite. They offer takeout, so save yourself time if you want to pick something up. I'm pretty good at complaining, but this place is definitely an exception :)

I got the buffalo chicken salad it was really yummy! The chicken pieces were small it wasnt big chicken fillets so the flavor meshed really well with the lightness of the lettuce and feta cheese. The service was really good overall great experience. My friend got the pasta she loved it and my sister loves their mac and cheese!

First time here. Had a coupon. Good martini's. Nice salads. My salmon alla senape was very good. Wife's salmon granchio was too salty. Service was above average with friendly staff. We will return at some point. Nicer atmosphere inside than you would expect when viewing place from the outside.
This is definitely over-rated. The hot and sour soap is particularly disappointing. It is so watery and tasteless. It is $7:00 for a bowl per person. Most of the dishes are small portions.

I used to eat here fairly regularly.  Last time I found out the entree I like went from $18 up to $24 -- that's a 33% increase! and the appetizer I get went up 25%.  I know prices increase but this seems extremely high.
Get here right when they open (or before).  Great breakfast and lunch foods Different types of bloody marys

Interesting unique food which I enjoyed.   Clearly heavy on cheese which is what you should expect.  The ingredients were of quality and fresh but I didn't love my dinner.  This was my second venture to Caseus and I would try again because clearly they have a reputation for something.  Perhaps my expectations were too high for what I actually got.  I love the cheese truck, I would rate the truck with 5 stars.  The grilled cheese is different, but then again it's a food truck and not a restaurant.  Service was great and well informed staff helped my table order several items.

food was delicious i have nothing but great things to say - drinks were even better - i had this watermelon mojito and it just hit the spot.  i had the server surprise me since I couldn't decide on what to get (it all just sounded so good!), anyhow he picked the dish with the poached eggs, chips and i think it came on a griddle - whatever it was, it was amazing and blew my taste buds out of the water... top notch place here.

Terrific little neighborhood place! Came in Saturday night and really enjoyed dinner & wine. In truth, my smoked chicken with red beans & rice was a little on the cool side, but tasted so good, I happily ate it anyway. My friend loved the fried chicken and the biscuits and turkey smoked collard greens were the best I've ever tried. Wait staff are charming, energetic and fun, and the chef, who is from Natchez, Mississippi came by to ask how we were enjoying our food. I normally squirm when that happens, but this guy is courteous and charismatic. My one gripe would be that the price of a bottle of wine runs high -$38 and up, whilst the food is in generous portions and very reasonably priced. It would be nice if they had a couple of cheaper wine options. However, that is the only complaint, because this is good quality food, cooked with care and pride, which is the main thing really, right?
Simple good burgers.  A New Haven staple.

My husband and I went in for lunch yesterday and were pleasantly surprised. We were fans of the previous restaurant on this site, Asian bistro, so we were disappointed when it closed. We wanted to give its successor a shot and I'm certainly glad we did! The first thing we noticed was the gorgeous decor. It's very tastefully decorated with two dining rooms--we were surprised at how large the second one was! The waitstaff was attentive for the most part--it took a while to get our check, but we weren't in any rush, so it wasn't a huge issue. I attribute the slowness to the fact that we were the only table in the restaurant (understandable at 2pm on a Sunday afternoon) and they wanted to give us our space. Our waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu and gave recommendations, even going so far as to pull out the special "secret" menu with the more authentic dishes on it (usually reserved for customers who are more familiar with authentic Chinese food) when my husband mentioned that he was hoping to try Szechuan hot pot. We started with the Peking Duck roll appetizer and I also had a bowl of wonton-egg drop soup ($2ish). The soup was average; no better or worse than any other restaurant I've been to. The scallions in it were very fresh and gave it a nice pop of flavor. The Peking Duck roll was outstanding. I've never had duck before in any form, let alone Peking style, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that the duck had a delicate, non-gamey flavor. I was expecting small, spring-roll sized rolls, but we received two large rolls, well worth the $8.95 price tag. My husband had the Szechuan hot pot with chicken ($15). Now, I'm not a fan of spicy stuff, and as you can see from the picture, the broth in this dish is hellfire red, so I was wary of it (and rightfully so--it's hot!!). However, beneath the heat there is an outstanding flavor. It was definitely too spicy for me to do more than taste, but my husband said that while it was indeed hot, it wasn't painfully so (as long as you have a tolerance for spicy food). He pointed out that while he was sweating, he wasn't crying, and while his tongue was numb, he wasn't hurting. There were tons of veggies and chicken in the soup and it was way too big a portion to finish at lunch--he brought it home and shared the leftover with a friend that evening. I had the beef Pad Thai ($13). It was average, as far as Pad Thai goes, which was expected Fusion House is primarily a Chinese/Japanese restaurant, not a Thai restaurant. It was certainly not the worst Pad Thai I've ever had, and it had an interesting flavor, different from any Pad Thai I've had elsewhere. Our check came to $40, which is a bit much for lunch, but we did order an expensive appetizer, so it was not unexpected. We will definitely be going back to Fusion House for their all-you-can-eat sushi deal and to try a few other dishes on the menu (I saw at least 4 that piqued my interest and we're in their delivery radius, which is a big plus in my book).
A good place with 8 different stations from soup and salads to sandwiches, sushi, pizza, and grilled items. Located in the corporate headquarters of Urban Outfitters.

This place appeared to have great reviews but was really so-so.  I wasn't greeted for about 5 minutes while standing there. Food was good, but really just average Drinks were better than the food - unique combinations
One of the best burgers downtown. Worth all 18 bucks
The scallop n marrow tacos are amazing...

Not up to the standard... food taste varies.. and it is becoming pathetic day by day.. and the cost gosh its expensive... the only food I find to taste better is crab masala.. the rest everything is waste of money.. I would not go here again.. Everyone comes for the authentic chettinad biryani, hope they know this.. It would be great if they can do something to improve the quality.....

I have always had a good meal to begin with here, but in an hour or two I always feel sick. It can't be just a coincidence.  Service is okay, it's overly crowded and always a long wait which I never feel is worth it.

Amazing salad!  Winter salad with romaine and blue cheese dressing with a side order of chicken breast!  I dont like salad!  Yet, this salad arrived looking so appetizing and fresh, mandarins oranges, cranberries, nuts and feta cheese. I barely touched the dressing, each ingredient exploding with freshness and flavor!   Yes, I could probably make this at home....but I dont think I could match the balance of flavors, especially the moist, perfectly seasoned, freshly prepared chicken breast.   If I didn't live a bridge toll and an hour away... I would be here every day!   Oh, and I was given dessert on the house as a first time customer....sigh, homemade butterscotch pudding is worth starting the diet over tomorrow!
LOVED our huge pizza slices at this amazing and oh so neat little pizza museum. I could have spent hours just checking everything out on the walls! Sucha  fun and delicous little stop in Philly.
Pho was good. However it was not better than sao Mai. Peking duck banh mi was a good idea but didn't taste that great to me. This place was a good place to try but I doubt I'll be coming back again.

I was initially waiting for a table @ Toast yesterday morning (sunday) which is next door. The wait for Toast was 30-35 mins & being a pregnant woman I was hungry & noticed that there were alot of empty tables @ this place. I convinced my husband to just have brunch here. We walked in & the tall blondish older man behind the counter looked @ us then continued doing whatever he was doing. No greeting, no Good morning, hi.. Nothing. Another guy came & sat us @ a small table in the corner, we have a 16 mo. Old & needed high chair. We kind of felt like we were being put in a tiny corner bc  we had a toddler with us. After sitting down of course, we get a text from Toast saying our table was ready :(  but it was too late we had already sat down. We got our glasses of water & menus. We were ready to order but no one even looked our way for another 15-20 mins. We were getting annoyed & impatient. Finally the blondish grumpy man asked us if we were ready. He took our order very quickly. I got the tunisian eggs & my husband got 2 eggs scrambled. I think my dish sounded better than it tasted. The dish wasnt spicy at all which is why I had ordered it. The eggs were runny & it was pretty bland.The home fries were reallly good though. I think the best Ive ever had. Sorry for the rant but in conclusion I probably wouldnt go here again. Although their menu sounds really good, their service is horrible. I shouldve just been patient & waited for my table @ Toast. I get why this place was half empty now.

If there were more stars, I will never hesitate to rate as many as I can! If anyone is a super fan of spicy food, this must be the great place for you! Some of my my friends didn't like spicy food so they ordered different kinds of XLB but we still enjoyed a lot Dandan noddles and special fish. I think it could be the ever best place to enjoy Chinese food for most people~~~ :-)

My husband & I Just had dinner here and it was fantastic. You can taste  the authenticity in the food. You can tell in every dish we had that it was made fresh on the spot. I love that it is a BYOB too. The owner and staff are very friendly! We will def be back! Must try the guacamole!!!

Excellent Services!!! Elvis is the most professional waiter I have ever met. He helped us to make some very tasty BBQ beef, shrimps. And not to metion he also put his secert ingredients sources on mussels and eggplants. Wow!! It was just Yummy!!! How can you tell a waiter is professional or not? Even he had work for 9 hours by the time he served us and was tired, he still had a very friendly smiling face throughout the night.

love love love this place!!! the BCT roll is amazing- who would think that bacon and sushi would be so amazing together? awesome ambiance, reasonably priced, friendly staff and delicious food! my favorite sushi place in the city :)

We went for dinner here in our last night in NYC. The overall experience was fantastic. We had mussels with gigantes as starter, which was very good. And as main we went for sole filet and branzino filet both very good. The food is fresh well prepared and creative combination of veggies an spices. We had a great night.

Had the Seared Tuna Tataki and it did not disappoint. The tuna was perfect, and along with the avocado and tomato, the salad made for a light and refreshing meal. Just a small warning: my friend ordered a bowl of ramen and complained that it was only sub-par. However, I recommend the salad for those who want a lighter dinner.
I almost don't want to write a review as I don't want it to get crowded..however I also don't want it to ever close.  AMAZING!!!

El Vez is a great place for drinks w friends, but I wouldn't recommended for dinner. I came here on a tuesday night. I sat by bar, the service was lame. This isn't a place for authentic Mexican food. If you like quality food and good drinks go to Barbuzzo, which is a block away from EL Vez.

Great new French spot in the UES. The food was absolutely fantastic. Tried the Roasted Fig & Prosciutto and the Roasted Dijon Salmon. The drinks were amazing and you can't go wrong with the tartines. The owners of the restaurants are also great people! Don't be deceived by the location. It's definitely worth a trek if you are not in the area. I highly recommend this place. Can't wait to try their brunch menu.
the food was surprisingly good. Very good, in fact. After dinner, check out the Press Lounge on their roof top.
They always seem to get my order wrong. Some of the staff is nice but always feel like the management is suspicious of all customers. I'm done trying this place.

Me and my husband were looking for the places in our area that served a chocolate soufflé for dessert. Then we found this place on yelp. We had a reservation for 2 people. They gave us a nice booth table with lots of space; it was wonderful . The restaurant looks modern, luxurious and romantic. We had a lobster bisque and stuffed jumbo shrimp for appetizers. Then my husband had ribs and I had a salmon. The good portion size was great and satisfying. The service was very accommodating and friendly. The highlight was the chocolate soufflé . It was incredible. Actually, we didn't want to share a dessert, but the server told us the soufflé is big so you can share. Yes, she was right. It was a huge soufflé . It's soft and melted inside was a chocolate sauce. It made my mouth water! It was fantastic.

Food was great, service was really good too. Everyone was very courteous. Fantastic vegetarian options, just the right amount of spice. While the portions looked small we had the 3 course meals, and the entres were very filling with the appetizers.

Farm to table flatbread. A favorite dinner spot in Burlington using (all?) mostly local ingredients made over a wood fire stove. They also have a great in house brewery. The most delicious pizza in b-town!
A very cozy and romantic wine bar, just a step off broadway, with an interesting and tasty menu. The host is very welcoming,  and will good care of you

There are so many choices in Little Italy, it can be somewhat overwhelming.  I have been to several of the restaurants and Pelligrino's is a standout.  The service was impeccable.  I had the lasagna and it was simply the best that I have ever had, it was so flavorful and the portion size was just right.  I tried my sister's fettuccine Alfredo and it too was awesome.  I had ordered that dish last week at a competing restaurant and this was definitely better.  The sauce was creamier and thicker, it really clung to the noodles.   Another thing that really made this restaurant stand out from the pack was their tomato bread.  Unique and delicious is the best way to describe it. One if my friends who generally doesn't like bread with her meal scarfed down several pieces.   A total of eight thumbs up from all of us!!

I think 2 stars is a lot . I like the rustic feel of the place. The service was average. When we were given the utensils the cloth napkins were  dishcloths which/ was cute but they smelled like grease . Yuk . Th  fire roasted peppers were awful. The pizza was mediocre.  The best part was I had my grandma with me and the host was smart enough to seat us close to the front door. Best exit strategy.  The server was slow and jumped in and out of restaurant either to take a smoke or to go to the other side of restaurant to get drinks . I had sat in my car for 30 mins when I got there to wait for the rest of  the party and sorta to stake out the place. The server had about 4_5 CIG breaks .  I like the place but not sure I be spending 68$ on pizza  ..I would prefer to spend twice that and be satisfied

Awesome staff & manager made our big group of out-of-towners very comfortable and welcome!  The food was wonderful; everyone seemed very happy with their meals. Salads were delicious, also loved the scampi and gnocchi.The portions are not huge, but with this kind of upscale Italian cuisine, I don't think they should be. We were quite content. Atmosphere is nice, old-world Italian flair. Cute place, right near Princeton but not too college-student-y. Highly recommend!!

Took my sister out for a birthday dinner here and it was definitely one of the best dining experiences I've had in NYC. If you enjoy wine then this is the place to go! The ambience is perfect for a fancy-ish wine and tapas dinner, the service is courteous and prompt, and the food was AMAZING. The owner was around and suggesting wine pairings as well which made the experience even better. Definitely going back next time I'm in the city!
That first time at Obao. OMG!!! Nice place Excellent food. I order Rib sugar cane so yummy Calamari love it Pad thai so good Grill pork & shrimp I would like to come back here with my friend again.

I've never had a bad meal at Geronimo.  First of all, they have the best tequila menu in town, and make tremendous drinks.  We often order tapas and appetizers and share - and we've brought everyone from carnivors to vegetarians - no complaints. Some very clever options, too!  Go. Drink. Eat.  A very handsome restaurant, with whimsical, tasteful decor and lighting. The only drawback is that it can get quite noisy - but I'd overlook that for the food.  Just reserve early!
Great place to be introduced to Filipino food if you've never tried. You won't be disappointed. Staff is knowledgeable and friendly. And holy smokes, gotta get that garlic fried rice!

Visited today again, this time for dinner and drinks - amazing experience of excellent food and great service. Candied bacon was a surprise of taste and creativity; skin and bones... let me not spoil it by describing - it will be another interesting dish to try. Tuna sashimi were too salty for my taste, but were loved by my companions and their presentation was amazing.

Visiting NYC and wanted to explore Greenwich Village. Picked this place based on Yelp reviews and it didn't disappoint. I had the french toast and my friend had the biscuits and gravy. Each was absolutely amazing! I will definitely go back next time I'm in town.

This place should be 5 stars. The xiao long bao here is as good as the street vendors in shanghai. Lots of soup inside the dumpling, which is the authentic way to do it. The pork is the best but the shrimp is also ok. I've been here every time I'm in NYC, which is about 7-8 times in the past couple of years. There might be a line outside since the place is really popular. I haven't been to any of their other locations but this one is enough to satisfy my cravings. One more thing, the seating is combined tables, so you'll probably be seated with strangers unless you are in a big group of 7-8 people. Check this place out!

Best restaurant in Philadelphia! I moved to Philly from Italy around 4 years ago and it's hard to find a great italian restaurant that is authentic and innovative at the same time! The server was attentive, remembered us from previous dinners and the kitchen was able to perfectly accomodate my mom's dietary restrictions. Our appetizers were the squid, the pork terrine and the fried cauliflower. The paccheri with eggplant fries and swordfish is just perfect and tastes just like something I would get in Sicily. My mom's scallops were cooked to perfection, very juicy. The cacio e pepe is creamy and perfectly al dente! The kitchen staff was really nice and sent us a corn and heirloom tomato salad to try and a rice pudding. I hate rice pudding but I just devoured this one! It had cherries and pistachios on it! The staff went above and beyond to accomodate us and just made my birthday dinner really lovely!
Of you are looking for good seafood portuguese style you are the right place. We been coming to Newark for the past 20 years. This is so far the best portuguese restaurant. You won't be disappointed.
Every now and then I eat somewhere that reminds me why Anthony Bourdain has the best job in the world.  This is one of those places.

My review is completely based on food since I haven't dined there, I had takeout. I tried chicken corn soup and chengdu chicken. The soup was good but chengdu chicken seemed like an americanized version (sweet and saucy). Maybe, I'll try dining here sometime soon and update my review soon.
Had the omakase and extra orders of uni. Yumm. Was hungry later on in the night and ended up in ktown for dinner #2.

Don't let the deli-looking, plastic neon fool you-- Ltauha is a full on restaurant (minus liquor license). All I have had so far was a delicious burger with great french fries. Tasted just like Dumont burger!!! They do need to serve alcohol or at least be BYOB before they get the permit, but it is very promising and I will absolutely be back!

Hands down best Australian place in New York. Amazing coffee. Brunch is wonderful. Cocktails are fantastic. Best neighborhood. Staff are lovely. I truly felt like I was back in Melbourne. Don't come here if you are expecting American portions of greasy food. This is genuine fresh Australian with Asian-fusion styled food....and its great.
Simply delicious. I was in the area and I the mood for sushi. Stopped in and had a tuna roll and salmon roll... Both were very good. The service was great, too.

I love Hispanic food, but the portions of their "Tacos" and "Tortas that should be call TortiTAS" are not enough to satisfy the hunger of a Hispanic male. The ambiance of the place is really cozy. In overall this place is a nice spot if you wanna just grab something small to eat.

I wasn't disappointed, nor overjoyed.  I ordered Lamb Byrani - medium spiced. Rice could have been more al dente and I was expecting more spice.  They threw  in two peppers which I used to up the temperature.  They should provide 2x the amount of raita (sauce) - so ask for extra on take-out.

This place is legit. Don't be fooled by the hoity-toity setting. The cooks crank out real Sichuan food. We had the "dry pot style" beef, the "crispy rice style" pork, and the "double cooked style" chicken.  Each tasted how it would in Chengdu, Sichuan (the world's best culinary city), and those three together made for a nice combination of flavors. Also tried the "Won tons in chili oil." Yes, again. Price is reasonable, especially in light of the large portions.
Service is incredible . Stephen couldn't do enough for us . You will not walk away hungry. Definitely a must.

One of the best places to get Italian cuisine in NYC! When I went, they were offering a promotion to try three different types of pasta and the one you liked best was all you can eat. This also included a salad and bread. All three choices were fantastic! Even their plain spaghetti was great! What is also great is that though the food is amazing, they're relatively reasonable on price! I will definitely go back!!!
Tried Tick Tock for the first time a couple of weekends ago when my parents visited. Huge portions, great hashbrowns and our server was super friendly!

We were looking for a place that used fresh ingredients and we found it. I ordered the Palermo, which was a salad with baby kale, figs, almonds, sauteed veggies. My boyfriend ordered the New Orleans (smoked ham, sliced apples,fig jam, on baguette). He ordered his because it was listed on the menu board that it won 'Best of Philly 2014'.. and it most definitely lived up to that rating. Both items actually exceeded expectations. I am a vegetarian and I still thought his smoked Tasso ham sandwich smelled delicious. My salad had fresh, crisp greens and I loved the figs that came on it, they were truly the highlight of the plate. We plan on coming back in to try more of the items available and I think it is great that they had a pretty wide variety of vegan and vegetarian options and even offered substitutes of hummus or tapenade on a sandwich or two to make it vegan. They also have a full espresso bar along with an assortment of teas, cold or hot brewed from what I could tell. The atmosphere was artsy and hipster, it was very clean and pristine inside, and it was pretty cool that they offered juices made at a local juice bar in south Philly for sale in bottles along with hummus and other takeout items to grab if you are looking for a quick, healthy option. The only thing I didn't like was that the counter employee was also making the food and drinks, so he was running around hectically when we ordered. He did an amazing job multitasking but I felt bad for the guy running around. I'm sure it's hard on a weekday to have enough people on hand without overstaffing though. Overall, Plenty is a great, healthy location to stop by and try something new!

"I wonder if these napkins are edible" is what I said to my friend after 45 min of waiting for our appetizer. We were already starving when we walked in. It was strange to see our waiter running around trying to cover too many tables while the other staff with in our eye line were hanging around. When I worked in food service if someone was in the weeds, you jumped in and helped. Our actual meal was ANOTHER 45 min after our appetizer.  The waiter, who did seem apologetic, told us that it was my sandwich that was holding everything up. A. Sandwich. Bread. With meat on it. The height of complicated cuisine. I'm a former upstate girl. My friends and I tour dinosaur bbqs like its a pilgrimage. Second time at the park slope location and hands down the worst service out of all the other ones I ve been to. Good enough food...if you ever get it. Maybe try Harlem if you're in the nyc area and really want to give the chain a try.
Very well prepared. Love it. I'll be there on next visit in mew york city. You must go!!'

Overall, the pizza was delicious and filling. The crust was not too thin and not too thick, and perfectly cooked. The sauce tasted unique although I prefer a bit more spice in my sauce. Good and efficient service too

Was visiting a friend in Monmouth Junction and the restaurant was a fairly close walk since I did not have a car.   Was very delighted to find that the food was great and the servers very friendly.  Once more during my stay I called and had my order delivered to the condo for they do deliver.  Once again the service was fast, the food delicious, and very good service.  Slightly on the pricey side but a nice place to get some great Asian food.

A wonderful warm place with a great staff and charming chef/owner. Best Negronis in New York. A variety of fantastic homemade pastas. The vegetable lasagna is terrific. One of my favorite restaurants in the city.
Had the sweet Afton burger which was really good. Dimly lit so it's great for dates and hanging out. Pretty small.

Recently I finally had a chance to sit and eat here. I had a amazing time!  My boyfriend and I order the Mac attack for a appetizer. That was delish !!  For dinner I had the pull pork taco and he had the meat loft. Both were great.  Drinks were good too. Cafeteria gets four stars for me. Great atmosphere. Waitress was sweet. Just hated where they had us seated. By the kitchen smh. But besides that. Great date night.
The pinwheels are possibly the best thing you'll eat this year.  Or next.  Highly recommended.  A lot.
Too pricey for what you get. I had the chicken bowl with rice. chicken was overcooked and chewy over seasoned. stuff grape leaves were 4/10. Probably will not reorder here.

Looked forward to dining at Le Virtu having heard wonderful things about the restaurant.  Was disappointed on every level.  Waiter was incredibly aloof and inattentive.  A 20% service charge for our party of 6 was added automatically but not mentioned by the waiter - we did not realize, so we added another 20% which the waiter accepted without a word.  Glass of Sauvingnon Blanc was stale.  A good number of the mussels in one dish were unopened and therefore inedible. Roast chicken was undercooked and very fleshy. Salad overdressed.  Will not return despite all the positive buzz about this restaurant.

This is a great cafe right by Columbus Park with delicious coffee, baked goods, pastries, and sandwiches. Also, they take card which is less than most places besides the large chains can say. Everything I've had so far is super delicious and the baked goods are hot and fresh out of the oven whenever I walk in. I'd recommend this place to anyone and will never be going back to Dunkin Donuts or Starbucks.
