I really enjoyed Oaxaca the first two times I went, back when they first opened. (And I"m a big fan of the owner-chef's two Thalis.) But my lunch yesterday was terribly disappointing. I ordered two chicken tacos. They were definitely worse than what I would have gotten at Chipotle. Bland cheddarish cheese, entirely unmelted. Bland grilled chicken. Pretty lukewarm, for that matter. To be clear about this: I am not that fond of Chipotle. I had tacos at one of the fantastic taco trucks on Long Wharf the other day. I know my tacos, at least to some degree. And yet I still think my taco experience would have been better at Taco Bell. I would add that the waitress told my gluten-free (celiac, not the trendy kind) friend that the general manager had told her that the restaurant has no gluten-free food. Now, I can understand saying something like, "There's always the possibility of cross-contamination in the kitchen." But to make this statement when the menu is bursting with gluten-free food, including the corn tortillas that I had, seems very odd. Again, not the waitress's fault; it's what she's been told to say.

Well I guess it's all about competition, or the lack thereof---there is maybe only one other Vietnamese restaurant in the Hartford area that I've found online, which would explain the lackluster quality and outrageous prices---$10-12 for a lousy bowl of pho (rice noodle soup) or some meat/veggies/rice plate???  Even in downtown Boston, the same can be had for around $7-8, and of far better quality.   The only plus here is that the food arrived really fast, like maybe 5 minutes fast---which suggests that it was pre-cooked and simply heated up in a microwave.  At least that's what my wife thought of her grilled pork and rice plate.  My beef and snowpeas rice plate was better, although what they called "fried rice" (the older female server offered me a choice of white vs "fried" for some reason) turned out to be nothing more than normal rice with some kind of orange coloring which made it resemble Mexican rice more than anything---there was nothing "fried" about it, zero onions, scallions, bits of egg or pork in it, just plain ORANGE rice! The best thing about our visit was that a lovely young female server came as we were finishing and gave us each two pieces of cake on paper plates, gratis.  The cake was probably from a cake mix box, but it wasn't bad, and it was a nice thought.  Perhaps she knew we weren't thrilled with the food, even though we weren't exactly scowling or complaining at them.  So generally speaking, nice service, just mediocre food and crazy pricing.
Best chicken and rice platter I've ever had. The free hot falafel while waiting in line is definitely a plus. The cart guys are super friendly too.
It's the kind of place where you actually have to stop yourself from closing your eyes and uttering "yummmm...." Because the food is so good!

Awesome Galician Tapas bar situated in a very authentic and vibrant part of Newark.  My girlfriend and I came here and were delighted with the overall decor and vibe of the place.   They had a great guitar player one Thurs. night named Matty D I believe who played really cool music that enriched the atmopshere.   Highly recommend this place to anyone coming looking for a classy and elegant dining establishment in the Ironbound district.  :)

Amazing food! The 3 for 5 appetizers were particularly good (empanadas) Highly recommend it, lots of food for a low price and a very friendly environment with great service. The recomendations were spot on!
Disappointingly one dimensional flavors. I wasn't expecting much, but was expecting more than this.

Small, European-style shop, friendly staff. More of a to-go atmosphere than a sit-and-sip (no other consumers in the small shop on a Monday late afternoon). High quality coffee (small latte, tailored to my taste with extra steamed milk), well worth the price tag.
The food is awesome I just didn't like the service maybe because we went at a time there was to many people but I'll come back

My friend and I went to the LES location. We were seated right away without a reservation. The place is quite small so I don't see it working for big parties. However, the arepas are just amazing. This is my second time here and I will be returning. The two people I've been with have enjoyed their arepas as well. The menu is not extensive but is a powerhouse. I've had two arepas and tried two others, and every single one has been delicious. Thus far, "La de pernil" is my favorite one. If you enjoy drinking beer, the cold "Michelada" is a great combo with the arepas. The flan the coco is just right, light, not too sweet with tons of flavor. I can't wait to visit the Brooklyn location and try their rum bar!
Great happy hour menu!

Great atmosphere and the foods are amazing its authentic as you can get without leaving Queens. NY worth the travel . Parking is definitely not a problem just right in front of a municipal parking. Dont skip the desert or you will lose out

We were waiting for our son to get out of work to have dinner.  We checked Yelp and Salute came up as #1.  We found the restaurant and went in to check out the menu and ambiance.  We were greeted warmly and shown the outside terrace.  Everything was spotless and entrees looked fantastic.  We had some time to kill so we went across the street to the park.  When we returned the staff told us they had saved us a table on the terrace if we liked.  We sat down at the bar while waiting for our son.  Bartender was friendly and knowledgeable about their selection of single malt Scotch. It was Happy hour so we had a drink at the bar while waiting and talked with the staff.  It was a little slow when we first arrived but by the time our son showed up the place was packed for a Monday night with a line out the door.  My wife was extremely impressed that, as packed as it was, the owner remembered our names.  The cheesy garlic bread was fantastic.  We had the Shrimp Fra Diablo and one of the specials for the night - sea bass.  Everything was cooked perfectly and the wait staff didn't make us wait for a thing even though the place was hopping.  We didn't have room for desert but the owner sent us off with a bag of biscotti for our 2 hour drive home.  All in all this meal and the entire experience was fantastic.  The next time we are in Hartford we will definitely be back.  Highly recommended!

First time I ate here I did not know that it was vegetarian food. YES IT TASTED THAT GOOD. I was absolutely impressed, as a meat eater the food here is full of flavor and nothing like the typical  flavorless chewy gross tofu that I've had. The food is great, and you will not be disappointed. Also there is a 6 dollar lunch special up until four.

Great little spot for good quality Mexican cuisine. Tasty food, great service, and a positively fun ambience! So far I've had the taco de pescado, pollo sandwich, and a few of the salads. All tasty. The carne asada salad is especially good! Will be going back for more... :)

A good sushi place nestled away in Lower East Side. The lunch specials are reasonably priced, good portions, and exists on weekends! The grilled teriyaki salmon bento box lunch special was $9 excluding tax/tip.
My wife and I went to Tashan for dinner. The food and service were fantastic. The boar chops were exceptionally delicious.

Went for restaurant week. The food was very good and the service was exceptional. If you're looking for a solid Mexican meal this is a very good value at a very nice location. Cocktails were a little pricey and not very strong but I understand they have some specials a lot during the week.
It was good I just dont like how they chop the meat so fine

Went with my brother, his fiancée, a friend, and my wife during Restaurant Week. There were 10 mezza on the prix fixe menu, so we had one of each. They were all fantastic. I had the lamb makloubeh and thoroughly enjoyed it. Both the ashta and strawberry rhubarb cheesecake were perfect desserts.
I just had my second prosciutto and (organic) tomato  sandwich here, and it was great! I loved it, fresh and tasty! Go for it...

Carnitas taco... amazing. Rajas taco... mouthwatering deliciousness. Queso nachos... heck yes. It's got limited stool-only seating. BYOB. Probably my favorite new place in East Village and worth the walk from Union Square.

I've been here for brunch many times. The drinks are so fresh and yummy. I keep ordering the  moletes with a fried egg. It's the most amazing brunch ever. I need to go for dinner bc I'm sure it will be amazing! Go here now!

Eh.  Going to give it another try for brunch, but right now not feeling super enthusiastic.  Maybe it was an off night?   Decor is AWESOME, and I love the courtyard.  So relaxing and pretty.   So. My drink was pretty good.  Definitely strong, but a little unremarkable.   The guacamole was the big downer.  It had a super smooth (too smooth) texture that seemed off - maybe they added sour cream? - with chunks of unripe/chewy avocado throughout.  Too much lime juice, not enough salt - just my preference.  The chips were nothing special. The braised short rib tacos were tasty, but a little lukewarm-ish.  Corn tortillas were great! All in all - I felt cruddy spending $51 for a "meh" meal for the two of us.  Heard they have a good brunch, so I might try it again.  If the guacamole were better, I would go back for chips and guacamole and drinks. Service was GREAT.  Maybe a little bit too attentive.
Lovely spicy food. Can definitely recommend the koreansk BBQ need short rib with kimchi fried rice!

You feel like you are in a small Italian town eating squash blossom fritters which resemble the clouds floating by and eating heirloom tomatoes with burrata (which is also remarkably light). Excellent pork terrine links you to the earth. Cocktails are inventive and fun and delicious.  Who thinks to mix tequila with a grapefruit wheat beer?  Nice wine list as well.   This is a great place for a pre-Sunshine Cinema bite or a place to absorb local color.

My favorite place to get soup dumplings! This place is worth the trip. Always a little packed and it feels like I'm being rushed to finish my food but the dumplings are incredible. Their other dishes are pretty good but no different than any other Chinese restaurant. The dumplings, on the other hand, are the best I've had. I love the crab and pork ones.

Great place with a very lovely atmosphere. Besides the food, delivered fancy and tasting great, the place offers a very nice hangout to grab a bite and enjoy some local IPA's. If you're looking for an inspiring place to lighten up you're evening, this might just be the deal.
Got the shwarma it was delicious and I don't even like tomatoes!! The line was pretty long but the wait wasn't service was very fast. Nice and cheap too, pretty awesome
We had a lunch there in May, we took the Brussels sprouts without the honey dijon, cauliflower, sweet potato fries, chilled quinoa: amazing food. Service was great too! will come back

So obsessed with the pizza and chicken wings!!! Great prices here.. It's definitely worth the trip coming here. This place is great for families and families with little children. The meatballs are also wonderful!

Went here for what I hoped was going to be the best seafood experience I have had in a while, and it started that way with a great menu, great server, and delicious food, but then the large black hair in my crabcake. very disappointing. they were very courteous and professional taking it away and replacing the meal with a fresh hairless version, but never an apology, offer, or gesture to make up for it. the food was delicious but sadly disappointing as my meal had to be consumed 15 minutes after the rest of my party and felt let down by management as they made no attempt to extend any sympathy

This place is very romantic.  Brought my wife and some friends that were newly dating and it was so awesome and so intimate Service - A+ : so attentive throughout the entire dinner Food and drink - A+ Just an amazing evening - the service really separates this place...you will enjoy it, guaranteed!!

I really liked this place when it first opened. The food was good, the service was good, and it was just a nice place to go. The last two times we were there, "last" being the operative word, the food was average, the menu choices were cut in half, and the service just wasn't good. In the last instance the server was all tattooed up, with short sleeves on, and sagging pants as if he was part of a gang. On top of that the service was slow. The hostess was seemingly bored, and the whole atmosphere had just gone in to the dumper. 100%, we are never going back.

I came here with my wife and after not eating here since August 2013 we were both extremely disappointed. I remember this place being so much better. Tonight, the service was poor, the margaritas were blah and the good was below average. We will probably look elsewhere the next time we're in the mood for Mexican food. Two stars is generous.
This is an awesome beer bar in the Fairmount/Spring Garden area. Close to the Art Museum and Logan Square. The food is good and the wait staff friendly.

The two stars is not because of the wait. In fact, we didn't wait at all because we went for dinner. This was strategic. I called 15 minutes ahead to ask if there was a wait for two, of which there was not. The ambiance at night at Clinton St. Baking is great. It's candlelit and intimate and the two-top tables that make up a majority of the floor are occupied by couples. We were sat immediately, but it was steadily busy. All but one table was occupied, however that sentiment carries less weight when there are 12 tables in a restaurant. I love the biscuits they serve in place of the expected bread basket. Our food came out quickly. I suggested since it was my dining companion's first time that she get the blueberry pancakes. She absolutely loved and devoured them. I should have taken my own advice and stuck with the breakfast for dinner agenda. I ordered the burger with bleu cheese. It was mediocre at best. I requested it be cooked Medium-Rare and it came out Medium-Well/Well. This is always completely demoralizing for me. This goes hand-in-hand with the awful service we had. Had our waitress come over ONCE after the very attentive back-waiter dropped our food this situation could have been rectified. Alecia H. was our waitress on Tuesday, August 19 and she was inattentive, disinterested, and most importantly, not present! For a restaurant as small as this one I should not have to actively look for my waitress. Both me and the person I was dining with work in the food industry and we were actually laughing at how awfully we were being treated. Because we know what it is like to work in service we tried to be understanding, constantly rationalizing our server's blasé attitude, but when we realized that she was not busy serving other tables, a fact of which we could have dealt with, we started to get angry. Completely inexcusable and intolerable. Will not return.
What a gem!  Quaint, fun and sexy all in one. Great food, service and enjoyable experience!

Everyone here is so nice. The burritos are inexpensive and a million times better than Chipotle; the burritos are slightly smaller than Chipotle, but quality over quantity! The chicken burritos are fantastic.

This place has excellent tacos and plantains, and the service always is great. The tacos are reasonably small and the food is pretty simple for the cost, but the quality keeps bringing me back. I go for lunch, I'm sure it would add up quickly for dinner. I would give it 1 dollar sign based off of lunch, but if I went for dinner I'm sure it would be 2.

Great comfort food with a little bit more flare than how your grandma made it, excellent, fast service, comfy atmosphere, strong drinks, great location... What more could you ask for? We had the pierogies for an appetizer (growing up in my big Polish family, I can tell you these are some real deal pierogies, not your Mrs.T variety!), the chicken and waffles (waffles were slightly sweet and nice and crispy on the outside but soft on the inside, chicken was perfectly crispy and not greasy), the potato pancakes (love the applesauce!) and the buttered peas. I could have done without the chicken gravy and would have preferred to have some honey, and the buttered peas were a little too close to frozen peas out of a bag for me, but these are minor complaints in an overall fantastic, delicious meal. Oh and for dessert I highly recommend the key lime pie with caramel sauce and passion fruit salsa. You won't be disappointed! And in case you were wondering, they have a Bellini of the day (served all day!), a margarita of the day and a sangria of the day on top of a nice speciality cocktail, local brew and wine list. Do yourself a favor and come here- you won't be disappointed!
simple fast sushi.  not the freshest but sufficient. simple decor. friendly service.  a little overpriced

Good place, always full, seating outside and inside. Unique mexian food. Tried fish tacos, seafood todtadas (hard shell tacos) unique pork tacos. All great. Poetions are a bit small, so 3 for 2 people is minimum. Very fun place. Desert: avocado and lime icecream, not to be missed!
Great atmosphere, good service, quality ingredients. The items just didn't justify the cost. Poor value.
If you want authentic Italian this is the place. The meatballs and gravy are the best I've ever had!  The same family has run the place since 1963, and couldn't be nicer and treat you like family.

Really overpriced for what you get. Not awful food, but not great either. The service is about what you can expect in Burlington - slow and impersonal, its more like dealing with government bureaucracy than getting served at a restaurant.
Degustation is really great.  It's great food and preparation spectacle.  I love the banter with the chefs and each preparation is extraordinary.  Get the Tasting menu and ENJOY!

Sheep's Milk Ricotta/Truffle Honey/Burnt Orange Toast. Poached Organic Farm Eggs. Garlic Potatoes. Smoked Bacon. Hazelnut Crusted French Toast/Sour Cherries/Mint. Whole Grain Waffle/Roasted Apples/Walnuts/Marsala Cream. OMG!!! Absolutely Delicious! Beautiful Restaurant! Love the location as well.

Good food, terrible service. I order takeout from here about every other week or so. Whenever I order wraps, they come out completely wrong! I've had to drive back to the restaurant at least 4 or 5 times to correct the order. The wraps were not even comped when I returned. I keep coming back because the food is very good, but if the service stays consistently bad, they will lose a customer. Always check your order before you leave the restaurant when ordering takeout!
Love this place to brunch! ++ for the deco

My son and I have been coming here for years and love it!  The food is consistently good.  Tonight we had Szechuan dumplings, chicken pad thai and curry thai with tofu-all very good.  The veggies are always fresh.  Also, it's a nice looking restaurant-copper top tables, homey wooden flooring.  Try it!  You'll like it!
Chopped steak, way better than Geno's, good portion
I had my first true Philly cheesesteak and decided to buy one from Pat's and Geno's and I have to say that Pat's was better- sorry Geno's.
Menu is overwhelming, confusing. Price seems high to me. $13 for salad and iced tea. Small portions but that's probably for your health. Food was excellent tasting though.
This place is Fantastic!!!!! The wings are amazing, solid ribs and the brisket is to die for. Great atmosphere!

I've lived in the area for about a year and recently I've been enjoying my few during the day pit stops here. There's a lot of light from the large windows and plenty of seating. Beautiful place really. Every time I get a coffee it's lukewarm and watery, the music is usually way to loud but I can deal. Breakfast is pretty good, they have amazing bread for their toast! A good place to sit and write or use your laptop. Eh... if only the staff would just please loose their pretentious all knowing of everything grand attitude this place would be stellar.

Three words: Oh my God. Ambrosia of thinly sliced roast pork steaming in its own au jus, on a crusty roll with sharp provolone cheese and sauteed broccoli rabe. I died and went to heaven. Just make sure you arrive early and snag one of the counter seats. Service is quick and pleasant. I would suggest to share a sandwich, that way you can sample all the food  the Reading Terminal Market has to offer.

Good flatbread pizzas, nice people, and good atmosphere! But I'm actually not a flatbread person. I can say their flatbread pizzas are very good, but I would be happy if they have more thicker pizzas! It's a nice and affordable place to get good pizzas :)

Typical of what a LOT of Williamsburg restaurants are. Overhyped, overpriced, decor-oriented, and very sub-par food. I'm going to cut to the chase. The Scotch egg was a good starter at a good price. The artichoke appy was a tiny serving for an entree price, and not worth it. The entrees that my girlfriend and I had were the Halibut and Lamb Kebab. Halibut...expensive and dry. Lamb...DID NOT TASTE LIKE LAMB. I couldn't identify what taste it was, so I sent it back and ordered the pork belly instead. Pork belly is supposed to be somewhat fatty...yes, but it's not supposed to be 95% fat and a smidgen of meat. Tried the desserts....MEH. If you have money to burn, and just want nice ambience, then this is your place. If you want good food, to go with nice ambience, there are PLENTY of better places than RYE.
Bravo!
Great food, staff and atmosphere. Get the mash potato flantas. Tacos are awesome and the Quesadilla's were great too!!!

The white pizza is awesome. The atmosphere is casual and the staff / service is excellent. Pretty good beers on draft and theres an outside patio area to eat (weather permitting). Generally speaking, the pizza is good if you like well done pies that are relatively thin crusted. I don't get all the hype over their famous chicken wings - I think they're dry. Nothing will blow your mind on the menu but it's a fun place and the prices are fair.

While the food is okay, they seem to be working as hard as possible to make it feel inauthentic. The restaurant smells of cigarettes, the teas are all cheap Lipton American teas, the candies are Chinese and they don't give or offer you chopsticks unless you specifically ask. The menu is very hit or miss, certain items are quite good while the less popular dishes are only okay.

I was sitting in heaven. Peach sangria, caramel bread pudding, live music and a sense of community. Vibrant artwork all over. Delicious, varied menu. I already reserved three seats for a live show + dinner next week.

Excellent food, some middle eastern reminiscent flavors(lamb appetizers) service lagging behind, our waiter was too busy to serve us, runners are good though hostess greeting us nice but quite visibly missing front teeth! Altogether great food that's enough for me to go back, yet more attention to details is needed.
Delicious and friendly!
This place was an incredible brunch spot to go to if you're interested in an affordable eatery in the cutesy side of Brooklyn. I loved it!

The menu here is simple and had a lot of southern variety. The Fried green tomatoes were fried perfectly. The mac and cheese was super creamy and cheesy. The main highlight is definitely the chicken and waffles. The chicken was fried just right and the waffles were hearty (buckwheat waffles). The blueberry toppings on the waffles along with the cinnamon butter was just enough sweetn3ss to balance out the meal. For drinks I would get the jollyrancher a watermelon and white wine agua fresca mix that was super refreshing. I will be back to try the desserts, the food was so filling to have them the same day!
Hands down my favorite pizza place! Be prepared, they do not accept credit cards. Cash only. The pizza is extra greasy. Just the way I like it lol
Great food, nice atmosphere. Love this place.
Amazing Ramen! Awesome service! Just had their short rib special Ramen and I am beyond satisfied or content. Leaving with a happy belly! They also gave us an app on the house to try!

This is one of our favorite brunch places. They don't take reservations but its definitely worth the wait. My husband loves the Bloody Mary- it comes with a slice of bacon and a hard boiled egg. The service is friendly and the the food is very good.
By far my favorite Chinese restaurant ever. Their food is delicious and  inexpensive. Every one is so friendly here. You want good Chinese food you seriously need to check this place out!

Food is AWSOME! My family and I have been coming here for many years. Everyone is so nice and welcoming. Tea is always on the table ready for you and your order comes so fast! Food is so delicious and fresh. The roti cannai is obviously everyone's favorite but the pad tai OMG out of this world!!! Also they always let you know how spicy (or not) you want the food. Love love love this place !
Best Breakfast Ever--- from my 15 y/o daughter after having her first Tosilog and I second that. Will definitely be back again on our next visit to NY.

It's not as good as it used to be. My basil chili salmon was burned and rubbery and did not taste fresh. It's not as clean as it should be. The menus are falling apart and need to be replaced. Bathrooms were extremely dirty. Great location with outdoor cafe tables.

This place is amazing! The Gluten free food taste awesome and you don't have to worry if there is cross contamination! My fiancé and I went there a few days ago and the lady who owns the business was fantastic. She explained the steps of keeping everything gluten free and regular separated since I was worried about ordering gf pasta. She also told me about certain apps and places that are all GF! The staff is super friendly and helpful. Overall fantastic experience can't wait to go back again soon! If you have tried it out you should!

Small but so worth the wait for a table. The breakfast is outstanding. The Challa French toast come with extra cinnamon. The hashbrowns are full of flavor. The eggs are perfect. Can't wait to come back and try some of their other menu items!

the braised beef was delicious, i almost licked the plate once we were finished just to get another final taste. the interior is adorable. my one issue is that the "pizza bianca" is not pizza!!!!! it's bread and some kind of dipping sauce. really good, but not pizza.
Ezra, when are we getting married? Your food is orgasmic. Love, Jenny

This was our 2nd time at Applewood and once again it was delicious and memorable. The menu changed to complement the season and the cocktails were fun and creative (even though they make all their alcohol infusions in-house, I think Tanteo Jalapeno-Infused Tequila would have tasted better in their Jalapeno Tequila cocktail of the day). My wife and I are new to the neighborhood and just delighted to have a restaurant of this caliber around the corner. Not only was the food amazing and inventive, their hospitality was second to none. If you haven't tried Applewood, go tonight, not tomorrow, not next week, go now.

3 stars only because I was disappointed with half my brunch.  Deep fried french toast was a good attempt but at the point at which you can taste the oil,  it's a deep fried dish gone wrong.  I'd warn people about that either on the menu or by the server.  Bread basket was amazing though and would get that again. Want to try the place for brunch.  Have tried Battersby before and expect no less

Been coming to Libretti's since the mid 1960s. I've never had a had a bad meal and, mostly had great meals. Last night was no exception to the norm. An added benefit was the fun time in the bar after dinner. Karaoke us not my thing. However, there was some amazing talent singing last night ranging from Whitney and Motown to Sinatra and Martin. Loved Miss Mia! Can't wait to go back for a "complete" evening of food AND fun!
everything is good.  please get on GrubHub asap thanks!

You take bad raw materials, poor cooking, snobby service, and... *miracle* you get 4 stars and almost 2,000 reviews.  Balthazar is one of the best financial success stories of New York, living proof that good marketing is worth more than anything else.
The fresh bread was REALLY FRESH! Excellent sandwiches. Liked their homemade Turkey a lot.

Don't let the appearance fool you; the food is better than you'd expect. Good soups and sandwiches, especially breakfast sandwiches (which you can still order in the afternoon). The woman behind the register may seem brusque, but she'll give you good recommendations and will check to make sure you're happy.

I am surprised by the low reviews. I had this pizza yesterday for the first time and it was absolutely the best I've had in a long time. The sauce had delicious flavor and the cheese was gooey. It was a perfect combo of sauce and cheesiness!!! I will definitely be going back there!!!

Indian Kerala style food at its best! Very authentic reminding of eating in kerala itself. The fish moilee with Tilapia and Kozhi varutharachatu..was just great! Great place with attentive staff that we will keep going back to..keep it up Kochi!

Great little BYO Thai restaurant in Fairmount. We have eaten both in the restaurant as a couple and with friends, and have equally done take-out. Easy to make a reservation, nice outdoor seating and great food, and fast delivery for take out. Our favorites are the Pad Thai and the Drunken noodles, along with the Beggar's pouches for an app.

I came here for lunch with my family, and well it served the purpose. The food was ok and everyone left with full bellies.  But the service was terrible, once the food was served we were completely forgotten about. I had to get up and ask for the check and my wife was unable to get a bottle of hot sauce for her bland couscous.

Went for dinner yesterday with three others. Meal was excellent. Had the bone marrow, veal and beans and filet mignon along with the Minetta steak and mash. DIVINE all around. The bone marrow was excellent, better than most places. Our waiter Henry was excellent. Lastly the chocolate soufflé was soooo creamy and just the right thing to top off a great meal.
Four pork dumplings, one huge stuffed pancake, and a bottle of water, all for less than $5. Fast, cheap, delicious!
Brooklyn Classic, go here for square pizza and spumoni!
Regular customer, their food is delicious! Very friendly staff
Yummy, such a delicious pizza !! Enjoyed it much, thanks :)
Good Food and service

I visited for my first trip to New York ever and took a lovely lady on our first real date here and everything was flawless. The food was class A and the drinks were delicious. The atmosphere was great and the service was exemplary. I would recommend this to anyone and everyone in the financial district In Manhattan. I had flank steak with yuca croquettes and I was incredibly impressed. Everything was perfect and it was such a good deal. I will return here on my next trip.
An excellent brunch place, the egg benedict tasted really good. I didn't enjoy smelling secondhand smoke from another customer sitting at the table next to me though

Last week was there for light dinner. Ordered baked stuffed shrimp; this wasn't bad at all; I rather enjoyed it. Also ordered NE clam chower. This was terrible. Very few clams, potato was puried but worse of all a very harsh hot after taste like way too much white pepper. This was very poor. Nothing about it to recall clams, new england or chowder. Waitress didn't seem to notice I left 95% in the bowl at the end of the meal. Stay away from this item.
its great price in the huge amount(espeically in NYC!) but it actually taste the same just like other halal food not really stunning
Go for pat's! but i think they're both over-rated to be honest...

CASH ONLY. BUT- Great turnaround, the wait isn't long, the service is fantasitc, and the food was perfect. Nothing fancy, but just well-done pancakes (Danish), home fries  (get the hot sauce to put on 'em), and french toast which pair wonderfully with the home-made flavored butter. Sometimes all it takes for 5 stars is to deliver perfectly on a simple premise. Good food, served quickly with good service, at a great price. Done.

A bit overpriced but honestly so very delicious. They have coupons in Valpak so look out for them. I'm a New Yorker so I've had many of bagels. It's no H and H but it's good. They could have better hours.

This place is awesome!!!!   Five stars if you ask me.  Chrissy is awesome as well and always greats me with a smile on her face.  Whether it's the Bacon Blue Burger, or a Cheese Steak, there is nothing that does not taste fabulous here at Sonny's. The atmosphere is always pleasant and the shop is always clean. As far as I am concern, Sonny's has the best food made in Philly.

The place is actually amazing but the food I think was ok. I tried the fried chicken with honey sauce. I guess the sweet sauce made it taste weird for me.  My fried ordered the eggs Benedict with mushroom sauce and she said it was ok too.

Tunxis Grill - Newington, CT 08/25/14 Monday - I just left the restaurant and arrived home. Disappointing - S...L...O...W  Service after ordering our Entrée.  Monday night reservations for a party of 6 at 6:30pm.  Four of us were seated and we waited for 2 more.  Ordered drinks and a couple of appetizers while waiting for everyone to arrive.  Placed our meal orders and our salads were served.  Then we waited and waited and .............. waited.  Our order consisted of three salads, one wrap with fries, one dinner special (pasta with chicken) and one baked sole dinner.  At least 30 minutes went by when I had to ask if everything was ok in the kitchen.  The waitress look puzzled that I was asking where our meals were.  So I explained - It's Monday night and the dining room was empty.  Two parties - One with 2 patrons and a family of 4.  And finally our meals arrive 40 minutes later. While we are eating a woman asks the table if everything was ok and I replied that our meals took a long time.  I'm assuming she was the manager but never identified herself and didn't notice a name tag.  She claims there was another large party of 6 or 8 and would check with the kitchen.  She never returned to tell us what the problem was and why we had to wait so long for our meals. Paid the check and the waitress tells me one appetizer was comp for the delay with our meals.  Shame on the manager for not returning face to face and letting us know what the delay was all about.  And shame on the manager for comping the least expensive item on the menu.  Oh ......  the drinks were cheaper.  It will be quite a while before I return and when I do I won't plan on being served my entrée for an hour.

Celebrated my anniversary here with my wife, and had a wonderful evening. 6-course prix fixe for $120 a plate took 3+ hours, and the staff made every moment a breeze. Our selections (August '14) included arctic char, scallops, halibut, squid ink pasta, duck, and an apricot-based dessert. The food was delicious and interesting, wine selections for any budget, tasteful and interesting amuse-bouches as one would expect at a restaurant of this caliber. All in all it was a great experience. Not precisely a value pick, but for the whole package of fine dining of this type, you can't go wrong.

I didn't know how great this restaurant is but my aunt suggested going to it and a free meal won't ever be turned down. Taverna Kyclades has a great location, only a couple of blocks from the train. We sat on the patio on a nice day and it was definitely crowded and bustling. We ordered as appetizers their trio of dips and their greek salad. The dips are absolutely delicious with their oiled bread. My favorite is still the cucumber dip but their red dip that's a little bit sweeter is also very delicious. The greek salad literally comes with slabs of feta. The dresses for their salad is also refreshing and balances out the richness of the bread. I ordered the grilled calamari and my aunt ordered the fried whiting. The grilled calamari was cooked perfectly and not chewy at all. My only complaint is that there were a lot of black crusts from the grilling that wasn't so tasty. The fried whiting was definitely better than the calamari. It had a great breading that was crispy but not too thick. It came off the bones easily and had the perfect level of salt to it. I would definitely come again and try all of the different dishes. There's a reason why so many people come and the reviews are so great. I can't wait to try the rest of their menu.

We had the calamari and the spinach pizza, and it was amazing. There was a long line ahead of us, and we were still seated in no time. The food came out really quickly, and the servers were delightful. The calamari was really light and delicious, and the pizza was thin crust and perfect authentic New York. So glad we discovered it.

When we walked in, there were two children watching Netflix on a computer in one of the booths. As we approached the counter, the older one rolled his eyes and huffed as he got up and walked behind the counter. He took our order and we took a seat at a booth. The pizza took about twenty minutes to come out, and it looked as though he was the only one working there at the moment. When our pizza came out and we had just started eating, what looked to be the owners, and most likely this child's parents, came in with goods for restocking. They quickly glanced at us and continued into the store. The pizza was quite good. So no complaints there. Maybe order out? The weirdest thing was this man who kept walking in with his hands in his pockets, and obviously handing things to the male owner behind a half wall across from us. I made eye contact and he glared at me. Drug dealings? Incognito laundering? I don't know, but it was clear something was going down since the unknown man walked out and back in two times after that. So maybe... Order out, pick it up, and do it as soon as possible because there may be some shady dealings here?
Another amazing meal at HQ... tonite with my mom & a German colleague, visiting from Raleigh, NC

i usually like hipster food but hipster pho is gross - should have listened to my instincts but i had recently had white ramen that i actually liked (i'm usually not into fusion food) so i thought i'd try hipster pho. when you walk in you can tell instantly that it doesn't smell like regular pho - it smells really shroomy.  The broth in the beef pho is kind of bland and really salty at the same time.  the beef pieces in the pho (which is the one thing i thought would probably be better quality than the usually cheaper authentic places) was pretty tough and the flank was fatty (but not a melt in your mouth kind of fatty), the tofu bahn mi was really salty but the french roll it was on was very good. Also - the vietnamese iced coffee had like cardamom in it - they should tell you that on the menu as I would have gotten another drink instead.

I don't know what to say other than I hope the lunch is as fabulous as they say it is...dinner on the other hand was ridiculously expensive for average Korean fare. "Eundae" fish entre literally had 2 pieces of monk fish costing $36!!!!! Whoa.....
Really nice place, really good food, amazing deserts.   Specifically I really liked the octopus appetizer.   I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

A colleague, a member of our top brass and I decided to lunch at Antinori. We were seated by the owner who, after offering us a table, came back and reeled of a list of specials with panache, far too many for us to keep track of. All I remembered was something with clams and steaks. Anyway, after speaking about the choices amongst ourselves, when he came back to take our order and saw us dithering he suggested that we have a seafood starter with a bit of everything and steak and veal as our main course. Of course, the bread arrived and was good. What I particularly liked was the fact that unlike most restaurants they had butter knives, which to me epitomizes a great restaurant. Some miscellaneous accompaniments for drinks arrived and were good. They changed our forks and knives after we had had these starters. (I, particularly, hate it when servers put the used forks and knives down on the tablecloth). Then the main seafood starter arrived. There were two clams, each in a different sauce, a giant shrimp in it's own sauce and a calamari. I wish I had taken a photograph because the plate presentation was exquisite. Each item on the starter had been cooked perfectly and was excellent. I thought that I should have made it my main course too. Just as well I didn't. Then they changed our forks and knives again! The veal and a giant T-Bone arrived. The veal was good and might have been great on it's own. However, it paled in comparison to the T-Bone which was fantastic.The server put the T-Bone plate facing away from us and the owner came and corrected the positioning. He proceeded to serve us from the main plate. The steak was cooked to perfection and easily ranked amongst the best steaks I have eaten. Nobody had space for dessert but we decided to have some coffee. By this time the table cloth had lost it's initial pristine look despite the fact that the server had continued to pick up crumbs and debris created during our meal. Rather than letting us drink our coffee on the now grungy tablecloth, they brought a fresh one, rolled it up and then unrolled it onto the old tablecloth making the table look great again! Everything was done with great style and panache and the food was wonderful. Do I plan on going back? Definitely. In fact, I plan to take my family there for my son's birthday next month. Do I recommend this restaurant? Absolutely!

Came as a group of 6 on a Tuesday evening. Portions ranged from small to just enough. Wine comes in tumblr glasses. Pre-meal bread looked like leftover pieces for crostini--- a bit dry, and some were already ripped apart (!?) --- and came with plain olive oil. Oxtail pappardelle was good, but nothing exciting. Found some bones in the sauce, and surprise pieces of gnocchi. Pasta was fresh, and had a good pasta to sauce ratio. My dining-mate's spicy sausage gnocchi and gorgonzola was very tasty! She thought it was too creamy though. Seemed understaffed, as it'd take awhile before we could get service. Romantic atmosphere.

I am SO happy to have a BBQ place in Fort Greene that's better than the mediocre Smoke Joint. While this place might not be the most consistent every time, when it's good (which is most of the time) it hits it out of the park. The pork ribs are excellent, the chicken is great... sides are delicious too. There a cute patio out in back as well. I hope it sticks around because the location's a bit off the beaten track of Myrtle. Please support this place!!!!

everything is so delish here... Great service.... do get their blt,  their yellowtail tartar,  yuzu and lychee panacotta, fried chicken-so juicy and the most tender chicken in the world... everything is so darn good!!
Great Chinese food and great for take out! Always quick and never disappoint. This is where I always go for Chinese food.

The cocktails were good and the staff was friendly. But in terms of atmosphere/ decor this place needs a little spicing up. Just too gimmicky And the happy hour crowd was semi disappointing... the plus is there is a roof deck for the warmer months.

Amazing. The food here as divine and the service was spectacular. Try the Pork Belly and the Noodles and you will be so pleasantly surprised. The watermelon spiced cocktail was delicious as well. Can't go wrong here!

Superb. A classic cavern of Irish pub authenticity. Being an Ireland native who came to the states 17 years ago, Liffeys has been here as long as I have. This place is the real bloody deal. The staff is surly irish guys, and young, attractive hipster waitresses without the pretentiousness you can expect from dive gem craft brew haunts. The prices are what youd expect- and the aura is 1000% true to emerald form. the city's other pubs feel more like a Buffalo Wild Wings with an irish theme than "real". not so here. The food is exceptional. Best fish and chips in the states. sport events are amazing here, esp. soccer as the yanks call it. world cup is an event, and the premier league saturday am is something u must witness in all its jersey wearing, chanting, bangers and rashers eating glory. liverpool fans will feel at home here, as the owner is a LFC die hard and Liffeys is the biggest LFC fan pub in CT. overall liffeys is a gem that feels like your own discovery.

True Italian deli!!! 5 stars is for food only. The gentleman didn't know much English.... But, WHO CARES. Their food is amazing!!!! Arancini is a must. The only thing I'm sad about, is that I'm going back to Cali. Sigh. Enjoy....

In town on a combination work/vacation visit, found this gem on Yelp. Gotta love the $1 slice and opportunity to make a difference locally, and ordering right from the owner. I actually picked up a couple of pies, also a steal, and brought them back to feed the family. The pizza was a universal hit with my crew, especially the extra pepperoni!
Great place to have a fun evening and nice conversation. Great non-traditional pizzas, for those bored with just sausage and cheese. Great selection. We go there to celebrate.

One of the best diners I've been to. (That means a little something in the fact that I travel a lot by road.) Organic eggs option for the omelette, perfectly cooked hash browns, a fantastic bowl chili with corn chips on the side, and a perfect cup of coffee all made us love this spot. Great service also!

Tasty, cheap and fast. Just what we wanted after a day at the Frick Museum. The gyros are not huge but just the right size for my wife and I for a late lunch. The beef/lamb meat was good. The tzatziki was light on the garlic to my taste. They put French fries on the gyro, which it didn't need. The pita was very fresh and good. Price was good at $9.50. We also had a kale and butternut squash salad that was good and also well-priced at $5.50. All in all, a good lunch spot.

Let me tell you a story.... My softball team was sponsored by the angel that heaven let run a dive bar, Jeff. Last weekend we lost in the championship game 7-5. Hearts broken, 12 men and women (and a few fans) traveled from the upper east side to come break the news to our beloved sponsor that we had come up short on delivering a promised trophy for behind the homely bar. Within seconds of walking into the bar, down-trodden, Jeff exclaimed "Next season I'll make it $1,000!" Second place was about to feel a heck of a lot better than first. From that point on there were non stop buckets of delicious, ice cold Amstel Light, and shots of fireball and Jameson every 15 minutes like clockwork. Free range to fill the Jukebox with Billy Joel, Garth Brooks, Mark Morrison and every thing needed to re-lift spirits. Right about the time when we were starting to feel the effects of the 4th or 5th shot, dear, sweet, little Mama delivered basket upon basket of home cooked heaven. Buffalo wings? Sure mama batters and deep fries them herself. Oh you're a vegetarian? How would you like some mozzarella sticks? Wait, whats that? We're out of mozzarella sticks? Well Mama has some provolone and a whole lotta time. Are deep fried provolone sticks a thing? Yes Please! Oh so you ordered a burger huh? Did you appreciate the onions inside the meat? Cause I sure did. Food was on point and had the special touch that only Mama could bring. Now that dinner had been served, and a magical white castle crave case was somehow pulled from behind the bar, the normal 15 minute shots were back in play. After the "Friends In Low Places" sing-a-long wrapped up it was time to celebrate our second place finish in style. 2 ice cold bottles of Andre's finest champagne were promptly opened and sprayed all over the bar as if we were the New York Yankees celebrating our 27th World Series Championship. (Disclaimer: they wear goggles because champagne stings the eyes, a lot!) We came into that bar that night losers, and we left champions. Enough nice things cannot be said about Jeff and his Mama. They absolutely treat you like family. I think when people think of a world without racism and people who don't see colors or ethnicities they must be talking about Jeff, he'll get anyone drunk no matter their race and he'll be right there with you shot for shot. God Bless Fish Market

I like Amy Ruth's food as I've been frequenting this restaurant for many years. I find that the food over all is good but has changed over the past few years and continues to change not necessarily bad but original styles or recipes tastes better. I love their salmon croquettes and cheesy grits! It's one of my favorite go to meals and I order it ALl time. I realize that the recipe has changed and it doesn't taste as good as it did about six months ago. I don't know either they have a new cook or a new recipe but they should go back to the old recipe, it tastes better! And the biscuits are too thick sometimes. Doesn't taste flaky like a biscuit, not completely bad but can be better! The mac n cheese is always amazing and the chicken and waffles are to die for. The sweet tea will give you diabetes but it's worth it. It always packed in the afternoon and for dinner so breakfast is your best bet for seating without waiting on the long line. Overall, good food but can always be better.
Best banana pancakes, ever. Everyone who works there is extremely nice and the food is awesome. It's definitely a treasure.
Delicious. Delicious. Delicious. Get the seafood pancake and thank me later.

Absolutely horrid, there are no words as to how terrible service was tonight. As soon as my boyfriend and I walked in, the snobby brunette hostess snickered and sat us down. After waiting over 10 minutes, she came back to take our order (because my boyfriend said something loudly). She was busy talking to the other waitress making casual conversation and looking at her phone. Granted the food came quickly, but it was definitely not as great as I believed it to be according to Yelp reviews. The tomato sauce was watery and bland, I understand it's "neapolitan pizza" though for almost $20 I didn't find it to be worth it. I ordered the ravioli, and the sauce was also watery, and not very appetizing. I was served maybe eight to nine pieces for around $17.50 for that price you would expect the meal to be at least semi-filling. Two stars is for the atmosphere, it's beautiful at night and incredibly romantic. Also, I give them props for the Apple Zu martini, that was delightful. Other than for drinks, I don't think I would ever go back.

Again strolling around with my cousin. I ate here for a quick breakfast! We ordered cinnamon raisin bagels, my favorite! They seemed fresh and cooked well. The eggs could be better thought. It was a little less tastey. It's weed everyone knew about this place. The little town of north Arlington goes to this place to get some toasted bagels!
My other half loves their pizza. I like it, too, but its not as fabulous as the flavors the top pizza places in NH manage to produce. Their clam pizza is not as good as PP's.

I went to this place on a Tuesday night, and the hostess didn't even let me through to dine. I was in a group of five people, but it wasn't busy and I could see empty tables around the restaurant. She made us wait twenty minutes, which I would have  understood if the place would have been packed. We waited, and waited and finally forty minutes later she said oh just twenty minutes please. So we waited and finally left. After an hour I don't think I would come here to eat.I hope this place changed their staff because with service like that I don't know who would want to go.

i had the avocado salad and a side of 5 pieces of falafel. it was absolutely delicious. the falafel was perfectly crunchy/fried on the outside and soft but not soggy on the inside. the seasonings/spices were wonderful. the salad was a lot bigger than i expected and the meal could have definitely been split between 2 people. i will definitely be going back - it is light and fresh and the price is on point! looking forward to trying other options on the menu.

Custard cups !!! The greatest thing since sliced bread. Sure , they have other pastries,  rolls,  bagels,  cakes,  coffee,  sandwiches,  drinks. Just about everything any other deli has. But did I mention Custard Cups !!! Sure ... you or I could make them any time of the day. But that takes time and effort. Buy them here and put the time and effort into eating them. Enjoy !!! ...

This is the best sushi restaurant I've ever been to. The Irene's Paradise Roll and the Angry Dragon Roll are my two favorites and I always get their Leechee martini when I go. When I worked in Hartford and out of town auditors would come and wanted sushi I always brought them here. The only complaints I have are that they are slightly over priced and once I accidentally walked into the women's bathroom because they only have Masks on the door. Thankfully, nobody was in the rest room at the time.
Never had the food but the bubble tea is fantastic.

The food was incredible, reminded me of places in much larger cities. The service was impeccable- the waiter put the cloth napkin in my lap and has excellent recommendations about wine and food. The atmosphere was great as well. Our new favorite spot!

I frequented Terakawa this past summer many, many times (about once a week) and unfortunately I think that's coming to an end. The ramen is very good which is a plus because it's hard to find good ramen places in Philly. The restaurant itself is nice and service is fairly quick as well. Sadly the service, particularly the waitresses, could be a little friendlier. There seems to only be three waitresses here and I've had rude and off putting experiences with two out of three of them. It's really just a shame but I won't be going back.

This is a cool bar but I had the rudest female bar tender there. I ordered a drink, she asked for my ID and checked it, and then I stood at the bar (it was quiet) for 15 minutes waiting for the glass of wine I'd ordered. I tried to get her attention several times but she literally ignored me. This was a while ago, she was petite with short hair. Maybe I came on a bad night but I haven't been back.
I went here for my friends birthday. It was pretty good. I got a chicken Cesar salad and it was tasty :) my friends got the chicken marsala and she liked it as well. The waitress was very sweet :)
Really, really loved this place. The food is delicious and the service is good and fast. I just wish they had some low carb options or could substitute the rice for more veggies.

This restaurant is AMAZING. I had a vegan philly cheese steak - the bread was so light so the sandwich didn't feel too heavy.. and the soy steak/ nutritional yeast cheese were perfect! For dessert I had coconut cake - moist, DERRICIOUS. If I go back to Philly, I will go out of my way to come back here.

The service was excellent! The executive chef treated us to a sample dish while we were waiting for our appetizer, we had 4 dishes and dessert and it was all excellent! The octopus tacos were my personal favorite but I also really enjoyed the Lobster dumplings. For dessert we split the peach donuts and they were heavenly (picture posted). I will definitely be going back to this place!

If you are looking for authentic Japanese food and romantic ambiance, this is the place to go!  My boyfriend and I ordered several different types of sushi roles, and found the fish to be extremely fresh and delicious. The presentation of  each dish especially the seaweed salad, sushi boat, and creme brulee was truly remarkable and artistic.

This place absolutely lives up to its reputation. It is hands-down my favorite restaurant in Astoria. I could never have imagined myself waiting in freezing weather for two hours for a meal, but I've done it multiple times for Taverna Kyclades. As I write this review, I am 9 months pregnant, past my due date, and I am secretly hoping the little bugger hangs in there long enough for me to wait a couple hours for a table and indulge in the delicious calamari, octopus, sea bass, and lemon potato feast that awaits me this weekend. When you're more excited about seafood than meeting your first child, I'd say Taverna Kyclades is doing something right. This will be our last date night pre-baby (I hope), and I am willing to bet it will be our first date night sans baby!

Being here in US, you may never be able to exceed the said limit as you get some tasty sea food. Furthermore, Upstate owns this prestige to have city's well honored elite here and taste the food served. I came to Upstate back in July with some of my mates from office. It was an incredible experience which made me feel highly satisfied. Both; in terms of taste and liking of place, they excelled so beautifully that they are second to none and I really got impressed to them in such an excessive way out. I would recommend all my mates and other yelpers to come to this place whenever they get a chance to come to New York. This place will always retain its memories in your mind to which forgetting won't be enough easy.

What can I say? This place is amazing! The food was great! I ordered the kebabs and they were seasoned and not chewy. The wait staff was very nice. It took some time to get seated but hey it was well worth the wait.
Eh - this place is ok in my books. Not very authentic, a little over-priced, but a more gourmet take. I went for dinner, however, and heard that the brunch is better.
Perfect meal.  Will dream about the lasagna.  Great wine list.  Can't wait to return.

This place is pretty darn inconsistent. The restaurant itself looks gorgeous, but once you sit down, your experience will be a bit rocky here and there. Food: Be careful about what you order. The bread that they bring in? NOT complimentary like other restaurants. They don't tell you a thing, they just bring it over, and set it on the table for you, and will bring more if you finish a loaf. But it's four bucks per loaf. The food itself is -- like I said earlier -- inconsistent. Some dishes are good(such as the calamari, and the snapper), but other dishes are way too salty or glaringly a rip-off( the duck, and the market cobbler, which tastes like canned fruit). Simply put, it ranges from delicious to disgusting. Service: Sure, the waiters are attentive, but anyone else that is a part of management will REFUSE to do anything for you other than give you refills and take away your plates. They will not help you place an additional order, they will not help you order a refill of coffee, and will even give you an incredulous look or rude glare if you attempt to request anything. I'm not quite sure why my experience was so wildly different from these other reviews, but I definitely will not come back again after that disappointing(and pricey) meal. Hopefully improvements will be made and others will have a better time.

The thing that first drew me to this cafe was its look on the outside.  It has such a quaint feeling to it and so I had to check it out.   The espresso I got was good!  Dark roast, not bitter, and full of flavor.  No complaints about this.  I also got some food. I got a turkey panini.  I wasn't too happy with the fact that the panini wasn't toasted nor was the cheese melted, which is what I expect a panini to be.  It was more so just a sandwich.  It was good though!  Nothing special, but it was cheap and worth getting.  I would most likely get food from them again as a snack.   Overall, this seems like a wonderful place to hang out with friends or do some homework if you're in school, etc.  The lady working here was pleasant and told my friend and me about the open mic night they have.  I would have stayed to check it out, but I had to head back home to do laundry.  Perhaps worth checking out?   I recommend this place as a better alternative to the Starbucks down the street for sure.

Well the Sushi House has new owners and they have spent quite a bit of money updating the restaurant decor, which is lovely.  However, up went the prices, down went the quality of the rolls.  Less tuna in the Tsunami Tuna and less eel in the Dragon Roll, just to name a few.  Plus the stopped giving pineapple at the end of the meal.  Now even though it was canned pineapple, it was a nice touch and a palate cleanser.  We have been coming here for years and I would choose this over many other sushi restaurants in the area.  So, you can imagine our disappointment.  Not looking forward to finding a new place outside of my town.  :(

I was truly disappointed tonight. Walking my dog and looking for a place to have a burger for dinner, I came across Mile's Table and there was a sign saying half priced burgers, what really actually caught my eye first was one of the burgers on that board. As I am walking up and noticing the sign I see a couple leaving one of there outdoor tables. things are coming together! I have eaten their breakfast sandwiches before and they were ok, figured it was time to try a burger, especially with the half off incentive. Right inside the door is a sign explaining the order process: go to the counter to order and pay, grab a number and a table, food will be brought to you and they will clean up after you're done. Since I had my dog with me I couldn't go in; but, since it was a week night and they weren't really that busy, maybe five or six tables in the whole place, and the staff had to come out to clean off the table I was going to sit at and care for the other customers outside, I sat down and waited. After the first five minutes and witnessing one of the employees attend the front most tables three times without ever glancing to check on the outside, I stood up and walked toward the front door, waiving my hands trying to gain some attention. no luck. Ten minutes goes by and while I am standing in the door way still trying to catch some ones eye, another customer walks out to grab an outside table with no luck, but sees me trying to get an employee and offers to inform them I am here. The seeming overwhelmed "busser"(?) comes out. Right from the start I explain that I am aware of their ordering method but I have my dog with me and ask if it would be alright to essentially have some one "wait" on me since I cannot go inside. Not sure he was listening to everything I was saying, looking at me but not listening; because before I was even finished talking, he began to passive aggressively inform me that I Must go inside and order and then grab a seat and that is why no one noticed you, "We don't have servers". I replied that I do understand and asked again if I could sit out side and have him take my order since I had my dog and couldn't go inside. He said yes, and then quickly reminded me again that they don't have servers and that's why I wasn't noticed and the normal procedure is to go to the counter inside (regardless if Miles Table doesn't have servers, shouldn't he have come to the table to clean it after the last guest left?? No exaggeration, they weren't that busy. In the span of what is by now  over 15 minutes, shouldn't he have gotten to the table, just to clean it??). Fine. He asked if I knew what I wanted, I asked to see a menu (Just to check it out but I was pretty sure I was going to get a burger). before he left to get the menu I also ordered an ice tea which he informed me was unsweetened. He came back with the menu and I then asked if they were going to clean my table, it had aioli and other sauces all over it. He came back a minute later with utensils for the next table and then bolted back inside. Finally, he gets to me, I order the burger from the board, the one that caught my eye. He says that burger doesn't count for the half off. I explain that the board says half priced burgers, and that's a burger listed directly under that sentence. He says, "Yes it is, I'm sure it's confusing, but those specials don't count". Now I'm getting aggravated. Fine. I ask for another minute to look back at the menu. This is out of principle at this point. I decide on the Miles Burger. It looks delicious and I'm still hoping for a positive spin to this experience. The, lets call him 'employee' because he adamantly professed that he is NOT a server, because they don't have them (He felt it necessary to remind me this several more times). He came out again after I had to stand up and try and get his attention, again. Table is still messy, and I still don't have my ice tea. He comes out and I order the Miles Burger. He then asks me if its to go or for here. That may be a reflex from when they are at the counter; however, I have made it abundantly clear that I intended on eating in. He seemed so shocked that I wanted to eat there. Proof again that he just wasn't paying attention which made me assume he didn't give a S#!7. I breathe and again hope to put all this behind me, sit down on this great night, and enjoy a burger. Lastly, the snarky employee tells me that the Miles Burger on half priced night doesn't come with the bacon it is so clearly described on the menu as having, and the bacon, if I wanted it, would cost extra. Yeah, that was too much, I left and got a burger somewhere else. Three strikes and that was it. I won't be giving this restaurant another try.

Went with a group of friends in July for brunch and had a great experience.   My Lamb Burger was flavorful and perfectly cooked.  The sides were tasty, thinking about it makes me want to have more of the lamb sausage.    Our server, Angel, was very helpful and friendly.  Will definitely go here again.

I am dazzled by the crepe soufflé + peach compote dessert. The crepe soufflé bites were as fluffy as they were light as they were perfectly delectable. The addition of the roasted peach compote was  more heavenly than any dessert I have ever tasted. All of my five stars go to this dessert. The ambiance, staff, and dining experience were great but nothing compares to this delectable treat.

Our family meets here on Sunday mornings for a great breakfast, yes I said breakfast we love the Mi Ga. Be sure to ask for boneless if you are new and it's great to spice it up it you like hot just ask for the homemade Sate. Don't forget the ice coffee!

Lively east village spot with nice ambiance and good food. The sangria is deadly (in a good way!) tapas were delicious- 4 and an appetizer was more than enough for 2 people. Service was a bit slow and we didn't get any table bread or chips, but it's a fun hangout spot with good unique food
Pretty cool little place to grab a bite. Friendly staff too. Food was great.

Stopped in here one day to grab some food as I did not feel like cooking that day. Got the Storachi wings and enjoyed them quite a bit. Ended up going back there another day and tried the Yum-Yum Wings which I would recommend to people to try. Much better than the Storachi. This place would get 5 stars, but the consistency of the wings can be a bit off in the way they cook them. One chef seems to put a ton of sauce on them while the other is stingy.
Mmmm

I came here with my boyfriend on a Tuesday night. We had tickets to a show at 7 and we got to Juniors at around 6:15, so we were in a hurry. We only waited for a little while before being seated. The waitress was really nice and was able to help me find a item on the menu that accommodated my wheat allergy. She was also understanding about us being in a hurry and gave us our check right when our dinner came.  Overall our experience was great and the food was good.

Went here last night for the first time. There was nothing "bad" about it, but I was disappointed with my General Tso Chicken. Everyone has different cooking methods and different spins on a particular recipe and I understand that. The sauce was excellent. But, the chunks of chicken were so large and strangely shaped that it was awkward to eat even with a fork. And with no knife to cut these extra long pieces, it was a test of wills. However, the wonton soup and the shrimp egg rolls were fantastic! Great flavor. I usually prefer spring rolls to egg rolls, but I'd come back for these eggrolls any day. The other disappointment was that white rice did not come with the entree. It was a separate purchase. Still, I would return in order to try another entree.

Great lunch specials: $12 for a big burger (or fish sandwich or whatever) with your choice of side (salad or fries) and a drink (coffee, wine, or beer) Beautiful space, too. Great for a quiet meal alone or an evening with friends!

I've had brunch as well as dinner here. For brunch, I usually get grits and blackened catfish with spicy tomato salsa. Once I tasted my friend's shrimp and grits and wanted her plate in addition to mine.  For dinner I've had the pan roasted salmon which was delicious. Nice place to go on a date. Mixed crowd, nice atmosphere and on a nice day/night dining in the backyard on the patio is really nice.

THeir black label burger is the best burger I've ever had! Reservations are a must, but there is often bar space + that's good enough for me! Wonderful, helpful staff. The bartenders are the best, the hosts are so lovely! I miss Amandi - she was my favorite!

Bar Tano is my favorite restaurant in Brooklyn. The prices are reasonable, the food is UNREAL, and the drinks are strong and very delicious. The wait staff is always friendly and helpful. Never have to wait too long for a seat. It's also a great spot to bring a date. Bar Tano RULES!

I was there for a midday brunch with a few of my friends and had a really good time. The ambiance was great although I feel the food could use more creativity and flavor. There were unlimited sangria which we were very happy about. Will definitely go back.

We have been there several times, and each time is as good if not better than the time before!  Delicious food, amazing vegan soup, friendly staff.  Not a fancy restaurant, but truly wonderful food.  I highly recommend it!

Came here for dinner twice and both times were really good. The food here is pretty good but it really depends on what you order. The two times I was here, I ordered 2lbs of the shrimp, cajun style and lemon and pepper. They tasted the same to me. DELICIOUS.

Very good! Chips and salsa served first. Authentic offerings. We had the lunch enchiladas, chicken quesadillas, and shredded steak burrito. Burrito had the rice and beans inside. FYI, if you aren't into that.
great pizza if you're in the mood for fancy pizza. restaurant is good enough to go on a date. classic italian

Absolutely delicious and although I have never ate in, the service is always very courteous and quick when I go to pick up my food.  I'm so happy to have such a delicious Indian option close by.  Both, my vegetarian husband and I give it rave reviews.  My personal favorite is the Ispice chicken curry.  My husband has tried a variety of the Vegetarian options and has loved them all.  5 stars all around

What can I say that everyone else hasn't already? This is my favorite (note, not best) restaurant in Philadelphia. The soup dumplings, pork noodles, pan fried napa and pork dumplings, and scallion pancakes comprise the perfect meal to cap off a rough week. I was concerned that the quality or prices would change in moving to the new digs, but to my pleasant surprise, it's still great.

Highly recommend the Mango Sangria and Mikes Dragon Fire! Louise, our fabulous waitress, definitely made our happy hour much more enjoyable! She guided us through the menu and was absolutely right about the Flour-less chocolate cake.

I was looking for a place to have lunch for a few minutes and luckily stumbled upon Northfield Bagels and Deli. There is a big selection of sandwiches for you to order from plus various baked goods such as bagels, muffins, brownies, and different pastries. "Smokey Joe" Triple Decker: Delicious! It's hard for me not to order a sandwich without meat in it, but this was enjoyable. The sandwich is essentially nova, cream cheese, Swiss cheese, whitefish spread, lettuce, and tomatoes on rye; think of a lox bagel but without any onions or capers. While it isn't as thick as the sandwiches with meat in them, this is a tasty, filling, and relatively healthier option. It's served with two pickle halves. You pick your own drink from their fridge. Corned Beef and Salami "Sloppy Joe": This is the type of sandwich that non-New Jerseyans (what do I call people from this state?) like myself expect when we visit or move to the NJ/NY area. This sandwich has thick layer of shaved corned beef on top and a thick layer of shaved salami below the middle slice of bread. Russian dressing and cole slaw is also added to the sandwich, the reasoning behind it being called the "Sloppy Joe." Like the other sandwich, this is also served with two pickle halves. There's enough parking spaces next to the restaurant. There was only one couple who ordered before me, but my order still took about 15 minutes. Still, the wait was worth it to me. The lady working the cashier is nice. Note that you order first, grab your drinks or whatever else, then pay after you're finished eating. Don't leave your plates on the table; either throw them away or throw the trash then stack them on top of the trash if you're given real plates. Food is reasonably priced and tastes great. It's all the way down Northfield Avenue, but the location is on the corner; keep your eyes peeled so you don't miss it.
Just good!!
Best halal cart in the world! Love their spicy red sauce. There is almost always a long line, so be prepared to wait, but it's well worth it!
Amazing brunch menu. Def plan on going back if I'm around the area.

I went to Nixs for a lunch meeting today.  I love tapas style restaurants, which I didn't realize Nixs was, until arriving. The three of us ordered a couple dishes each, for the table to share. Everything was out of this world! I think my favorite would have to be the lobster rolls. The way the chiefs present the plates  is really classy and upscale. The place still had a laid back atmosphere though. It's a really unique spot . Our server Michael was on top of his game, very attentive, very informative. All the ingredients they use are as local as possible. Even the beers are from local craft breweries. If I remember correctly, they had at least ten on tap, which I found impressive. I was recommended to try the Hooker Irish Stout. I'm so glad I did. I read in a previous review that this restaurant blast techno music. In our experience, they had nice, slow, jazzy, bluesy tunes playing in the background. I thought it was nice. I can't say enough good things about Nixs. When you're taking clients out to lunch often, you don't always want to spend an arm and a leg. I thought the check at the end was certainly reasonable. I think this might just be my new favorite Hartford spot.

I really want to give this 2.5 stars.  On a good day it would get 3.5 stars but one of the problems is that it's inconsistent.   On a bad day - this place seems a little dirty, the staff seems a little miserable, and the prices can be a little high for what you get.  It can be slow too.   I've had amazing cold teas here, and I've also had weak coffees. Typically the soups are good, however.  I have a ton of friends in the neighborhood who are regulars at this place but some of that might to do with the fact that there's nothing else around.   Also - I am strictly commenting on breakfast and lunch, not dinner.
Love this place never fails me the food is the same every time I get the mock chicken wrap with spinach wrap Mayo, cheese, pickles and sweet peppers delicious
Incredibly good. I tried the brisket platter and the bahn mi burger which were both perfect. This was the best meal I've had in Astoria in a long time.

let me start off with MARIO CART!!! and I was sold. also biggest TVs in Old city to watch all the games, and videos to every song that comes on. pretty cool place, great pitcher deals.. hot bartenders and awesome food! i happened to come in when it was taco tuesday, 2$ tacos that were gormet as fuck i will most definatly go back.

One of the best Thai places in the city! This is my fifth visit and I keep coming back for these reasons: 1) Great food (the housemade curries!!) 2) Good sized portions 3) Excellent prices 4) Cool atmosphere
It was OK - not great - not bad. Got charged for Guac I did not order. Rather unfriendly.
I really liked both the food and the ambience!  Must haves include the edamame dumplings, Brussel sprouts, and housemade churros!

I agree with everything S.Y. said in her review, its my fave restaurant in the whole city. It's like getting big, high end french restaurant food with slight Korean flourishes in a tiny intimate setting with everything done perfectly! I can imagine this is the kind of food chefs prepare for each other or experiment with. Even the kobe burger knocks my socks off. but love the kimchi bouillebaisse, bourgongion, mushroom appetizer thing that comes in a tiny cast iron pot, and just get any of the specials. Chef Park is a badass chef guy with lots of stories and opinions. This place / Chef Park has a lot of character. Also, it's BYOB, counter seater, and has a casual vibe. Don't expect a full service regular restaurant-- this is like dining in a special little house.
I have never been disappointed here. Chili cheese fries, quesadilla, mozzarella sticks. Just a few to get you started ;)

Lunch with hubby and father in law. Enjoyed the tapas: Crab stuffed peppers (really good!), Grilled wild mushrooms (sooo delicious!) and revuelto (awesome!!!). For soup, had the gazpacho (really good, refreshing!) and chicken plancha sandwich. Would definitely come back for dinner...Great service and fantastic dishes!!!
I love the dosa here! I'm a New Yorker but I only eat dosa here. It's deeeelicioussss!

This is one of those hole-in-the-wall places that usually turn out to be a nice surprise.  Ani is no exception.  We tried the Mazeman, Ani Ramen and the Shoyu.  All were a bit salty but generally very tasty.  We also ordered the pork bun which turned out to be the star of the meal.  Service was very good and the wait was reasonable for a Friday night.

My wife and I just tried this place for the first time. It was absolutely incredible. The food was made fresh to order and was amazing. They have an awesome craft beer draft list!. My wife is not able to have gluten and they were able to do almost their entire menu gluten free, including having excellent gluten free pasta. I would absolutely recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a great date night meal!!!
crunchy. Good.

Remembering Paisano's as a pizzeria with a juke box in the back as a kid growing up in Rutherford back in a day, I wanted to like it when they transitioned into a more upscale, bistro-type eatery and the downtown became a restaurant destination of sorts. Having not been in town for several years when I first visited the new Paisano's, they did not disappoint. Visiting them numerous times the past several years, Paisano's never disappoints, including our last visit a couple weeks ago. Consider it a reliable, go-to dining choice.
