There are five different food court style restaurants in this place.  Each one actually should be rated differently.  After you go there a few times, you can figure out which ones are the better ones.  The people who have gone here only once probably are the ones which give the poor ratings.  The bhel puri, pau bahji, sabudana khichadi are wonderful.  I did not have a good experience with the dosas.  The Indian Chai is also very good here. This place is cheap, so I eat here first, then I also do take out.  Seating is usually a problem, so it is not good for large groups.

After hearing that this was one of Connecticut's best Italian restaurants my companion and I were deeply disappointed. My pasta was undercooked and his veal over salted. Quite frankly we have had better Italian meals at Bertucci's.

Incompetent service: we made a reservation, they lost it but told us to head over in 10 minutes regardless, we came in, and then they told us they found our reservation but it would be another 30 minutes. Quite frustrating. To cap it off, we asked them as dinner ended if we had to rush to order dessert. Half an hour after a firm 'no', they came to us apologizing for having run out of all but one dessert. Oh, and the coffee was tepid. Folks get your act together.
It was still a half hour before their closing time and they were turning people away on Halloween night...
Great place! Good food! Great atmosphere. Heart of the city. The service is awesome, the people are great! This is just the best place in philly to grab some food and a beer.
Chicken And Waffles is a Must the Mac N Cheese is Good also the Ask about the Specials also Open Late
blue orchid is a diamond hidden in sunny side queens... the whole selection of taste food is worth trying out!!!!

Have been here twice for dinner.  Never crowded when I've been here. Heard it gets better later in the evening when the DJ comes.  Plenty of room and a couple of pool tables.  The food is delicious.  I had the tacos with meat and they were out of this world.  Priced like any other place.

I made a reservation on a Wednesday night. The place was pretty much empty, only a couple of tables taken. Once we were seated, we've waited 20 minutes for someone to come up to us which I could understand if it was on a busy Saturday night but that wasn't the case here.   For dinner I had the chicken with spinach (very bland) and my other guest had the gnocchi which she describes as nothing special. We decided not to have dessert and go elsewhere for a more pleasant environment. Overall, the food was not the best and the staff seemed miserable. Very disappointed, I will not be returning.

Short: Food deserves better service. The first time I came here was awesome; great beer, cheese, specials, etc.  The service was good too...the first time I went.  I went again with some friends and family for my birthday recently, and I had been looking forward to eating there all week.  But I definitely left very disappointed.  Our waitress was pleasant enough, I'm not sure if she was new or just having an off night, because the service was the worst I've had.  Brought out 35 dollars worth of appetizers 10 minutes after our meals had been served.  It was also clear that the fault was not on the kitchen staff, but that our food was simply not brought over to us.  My meal was served cold.  Glasses were left empty for long spans of time.  One person at our table left with a stained shirt because a waitress dropped the contents of a plate on him.   All of those things are no big deal at the end of the night and people make mistakes, and they did comp the appetizers.  It was certainly disappointing though.  I'm sure I'll be back eventually because the food is amazing, but I'll probably be bringing my money somewhere else for the foreseeable future.

This place is a staple in Burlington, VT.  The spaghetti and meatballs are so scrumptious I lack the ability to express the yummyness.  My brother get the veal parm every times and loves it.  If you order to go, they give you a loaf of bread and fresh grated parm.  I love, love, love this place.

fJust look at the line! THere's no way people will stand in the cold and rain if it ain't worth it! Don't be fooled! The 3 carts within the same 100 yards are the same Halal Guys! Street meat at its finest, I had the Mix and chicken over rice and -- with recommendation from my friend -- drowned the whole thing in white sauce.  The white sauce is not as cucumber-y or refreshing as other Greek restaurants, but it did the trick.  The "mix" part of my plate was the best part (I'm thinking beef and lamb mix?).  For $6 (inclusive of tax) the portion was HUGE! Ask for To-Go so they give you a lid because you WILL be taking almost half home! Street cart = no seating, but it was so good that we ate in the rain on the sidewalk. Whatever you're doing guys, keep it up! Will be back here every time I visit!
Came back again and had another great burger.  This time I also had the double chocolate peanutbutter sandwich.  Save room for one!

Such a cozy environment where we sat  down and relaxed waiting for food with the football game playing. We ordered a breakfast burger each and was amazed how delicious and filling this burger was. The fries are yummy as well. It's was filling even for a big stomach I have so its worth every penny!!

We came here for a birthday brunch on a blustery NY Sunday. We had a reservation, yet the obnoxious hipster host made us wait outside. When we asked if our 3 freezing kids could wait inside, we were told no. We finally did get our table, after about 10 minutes. Not a bad wait, except we were standing in the cold. Our table was too small for our party, yet they didn't correct it for us. We sat squished. It's better to have them tell you what they do have here, because they are missing a lot of basics. No Diet Coke. The smug waitress informed me they only carry regular. For the kids- no apple juice, no chocolate milk, no lemonade. And despite this being a brunch place, no hot cocoa or Bloody Mary. Food was ok. Not spectacular. My husband's order was wrong and they didn't bring him his correct meal for another 20 minutes. The kid's mac & cheese was very good. We split the order between 2 kids. Overall, the food wasn't good enough to make the obnoxious and horrible service worth it. I will not return.
One of my favorite restaurants of all time. Great food, great people, great atmosphere.

As a Japanese person growing up in America, one of the few things my parents insisted on was proper fish.  We'd drive 1 hour (it seemed longer when we were kids) to go to a fish store they liked, rather than buy the dubious fish that was offered at the local super markets. Well, Nassau Street Seafood reminds me exactly of the place we went to.  They are clearly (a) more expensive, and (b) fresher and more experienced than the grocery store seafood department.  Your own tastes and budget will have to dictate whether it's worth it (both time and money) for you.  For me, it's worth it.  I will buy their tuna for sashimi, but only if we mutually agree it's "sashimi grade", which usually they do, but not always. Here's two tips: (1) you can learn to see freshness in fish.  (2) ask them: "what's really fresh that you like." All good fish mongers will answer (2) honestly.  If you just march in and order what you came in to buy, at Nassau Street Seafood it will be fine, but you might miss a special catch/buy they sourced in the AM. I only get my fish there, I don't try their restaurant/takeout business. Jack Morrison, the owner, also owns the deservedly well-liked seafood dinner-only Blue Point Grill next door. Disclaimer: over the years I've made friends with Jeremy, one of their managers.  I don't think this influences my review, but want to mention it.
Great service, Delicious food, and I can't wait to eat there again.

Excellent food, excellent service. Kim, the bartender, made the best margarita I've had in I don't know how long. Erin, our waitress, was easily the best server I've had in Philly. The food was complex, rich, and delicious. I think V Street might be the best vegan restaurant in Philly.

Went to the Montville Inn last night.  Its a nice enough atmosphere but that's where it ends.  Service is mediocre at best.  Ordered an appetizer that was full of salt.  Service people there are friendly but incompetent.  Never received our dinner because the server forgot to place the order.  After an hour of waiting we paid our check and left.  It seems like there are far too many people working there but nothing is getting done.  Unfortunate because it is a nice venue. Just needs a good manager.  The wait staff stands around talking to each other and not attending to their customers.  I've been there before and had the same experience.  Won't be going back.

My partner and I paid a visit to Claire's Corner Copia yesterday evening while we were in New Haven for the day.  I had heard a lot about this place for some time, and we stumbled upon it while walking 'round in the rain post-concert and decided to give the place a spontaneous last-minute go instead of the more pricier options in the 'hood. The one thing I immediately noticed was, there were so many options to choose from; it was quite overwhelming admittedly! [but in a good way]  It should be noted that Claire's is a vegetarian place, but they can and will accommodate vegan substitutions, if you ask them. I wound up ordering the Enchiladas de la Casa [gluten-free] sans the organic fried egg as my main dish for dinner.  I found it quite appetizing and the serving was generous and ample. They supply you with complimentary bread with your meal, and it should be noted that the rolls are HUGE!  They gave us two, which was plenty for my partner's lentil soup and for my enchilada.  I also ordered a Kale-a-bunga smoothie and it was to my palate and liking; not too tart, not too sweet. Before leaving, we brown-bagged a slice of their Lithuanian coffee cake, which is one of their dessert specialities which was good, also. Last aside:  if you need to use the restroom, you will have to flag a waiter/waitress down so they can open it up for you because they keep the facilities under strict lock and key. The folks who worked behind the counter seemed to be warm, patient and helpful also. If and when I return to New Haven, I'll most certainly give Claire's another go!  Enjoy folks and happy eating! :]

I'm now leaving the actual restaurant and I just ate and paid the bill and was literally asked to leave. By a young man who is in the pictures I just posted. Food was great, drinks were OKAY, service was horrible, we got here at 3:30 and waited to to eat actual dinner that wasn't serve red until 5 we ate ordered a few more drinks, and were told that a reservation was coming and that we basically had to leave. I've never in my life experienced service that way, the man told us "no rush but we have a reservation with tables we have to fill soon". Of course after we paid our bill were asked to leave. HORRIBLE SERVICE with this man in the photo.

Such a great and amazing place!  Phil Gilmore, Chef Isamel Alvarez are the coolest people to hang with! Chef Isamel Alvarez way of cooking is extremely passionate, beautiful and like him handsome!  Master Sushi Chef William is a Sushi Veteran, like the guys knife skill looks like It's coming outta a samurai flick fighting giant tuna making their way to Bushwick and he's there to protect the civilians. Their veriety of beer, sake and fresh sushi is unbeatable. My favorite of course the Momo Salad, Agedashi Eggplant, Fried Chicken,  Shrimp Tempura, with a nice Pork Chop and washing all that down with Orions, Marlboro Lights and a nice vibe. . Sometimes don't want to leave because the veriety of music, people and its always a party... Even on a Tuesday

Food was very good. Service was a bit slow. But my  one star rating was because of what I saw today. The owner/manager was annoyed at one of his employees for whatever reason and was ridiculing him asking if he's hard of hearing and if something was wrong with his hearing. It made me uncomfortable - and i don't get uncomfortable easily - and got me mad someone was talking so down to someone - especially in front of the customers. I told them my complaint and left. Needless to say, even though the food was good, I won't be coming back and giving business to such a guy.  He needs to watch an episode of restaurant impossible and learn better.

I love tapas. I love that my taste bud can go through so many experiences in one sitting. Amada is a great place to go for tapas because they are so accommodating. My bf and I got a free dish on the house. We also got out plate of olives for free because it came out late. Lots of complimentary dishes. Go and have an adventure with your palate.

Love the menu. Love the atmosphere. Quality of both food and drink is great. Service is good as well. All in all this place is one of my favorites in Brooklyn and totally worth the trek into Greenpoint.
I love this place!! Perfect Italian options with wine pairings! The food was delish and atmosphere so cute. Loved our waiter as well. Will absolutely recommend for a cute date night spot.
Great food at amazing prices. The Panang Curry is the best I have ever had. The drunken noodles were really good but the curry is the reason to go back.
Wonderful food and service!! Great filet mignon and duck confit!! The escargots were also amazing! Best wine bar! Wonderful staff as well :)

I would eat here every day, unfortunately it's located by the super touristy time sq. The food was absolutely amazing. The over friendly service made us a little uncomfortable (I'm not complaining)! Loved the free olives!! I had two plates myself!
I've had some great meals and drinks at Garces Trading Co! I'm still drooling over their homemade mozzarella. Their price point however leaves a less than desired taste in my mouth.

Although food is pretty good, I was very disappointed by the rudeness of their waitress Emma. When you forget your customers' order (which is ok, it happens) I don't think you should call them off in front of the whole restaurant, blame them for your mistake and say things like "oh so you think you're perfect, really?". I understand her job can be difficult and frustrating, but she should keep in mind that it is not appropriate to treat customers that way, and her attitude was insulting and totally uncalled for. However, I would like to add that I didn't have to pay for what I ordered, which I appreciated. Nevertheless, I hope the restaurant management will do something to prevent their customers to be treated that way in the future.
Food is okay. Waiters look like homeless people. Their appearance kind of kills your appetite when they bring you your food.

First off, it's not called Harris Millis dining, it's the f*****g Grundle. I grundle at least 3 times a day, it produces the worst bowel movements known to man. But Mary is an angel and I love her. On good nights, I make 3-4 appearances at late night between the times of 12 and 1:30 am. It's the perfect destination for non-sober nights even though you'll completely regret it the next day while you make roughly 8 trips in the bathroom to "drop the kids off at the pool" except the "kids" you'll be delivering won't be solid to say the least and are louder than the fresh dank you lit up that night. This review is more impressive than any assignment that I have completed at this school mainly true because I spend hours of everyday in this fine establishment instead of opening a book and doing homework. Many epic and preposterous moments have taken place here and there is absolutely no regrets. I'm done. Rogue out.

There's a reason that this place has been in business for so long ! We had crab meltaways, New England Clam Chowder and sliders. Food was AWESOME !   Very reasonably priced - two of had a great lunch with two beers each for around $60.00. Way too much to choose from on the menu, I plan to get back here more often.

I do think this is the best sushi place in Burlington, and especially love the sushi pizza. However, I have never had good service. Always slow. One waitress seemed to feel that waiting on tables was quite the burden to her day. It never seems to be busy, so it confuses me as to why service is always slow. And often times they are out of things that are on the menu. I will go back because it is delicious, and I like the location, out of the way of church street, and easy parking. I try to leave my past judgements of bad service behind each time I go, but so far, service hasn't improved. But...yay for sushi pizza!!

Quaint French restaurant of which everything breathes French except that it was built not that long ago. Even the stairs going down to the restroom was 'typical'. The oysters were excellent and the mould frites too. The crenelated brûlée was ok, too sweet for my taste and too custardie. The place was hopping that was for sure

Great Sports Bar in heart of south Philly...Lots of screens One of best place to watch an Eagles game... Family friendly too...so bring your kids to celebrate the Eagles win...Every time I'm in philly ...I hit this spot ... Crab fries to die for... Friendly servers and good eats and great screens

Such an awesome place in NYC - the New Yorkers are spoiled to have this gem in their midst! We got in and the place was mobbed - people everywhere - shopping, scouting for a seat at one of the mini restaurants or bars, drinking...just people everywhere. The market areas - they have a large cheese and charcuterie section, produce, fresh pasta, bread, dessert...everything and it is just like Mario Batali - legit! We managed to get a seat at one of the bars and ordered the cheese and charcuterie plate (and wine if course) and it was amazing. The fresh made ricotta was outstanding - so outstanding that I looked up the recipe and plan to make it and pair it with honey and almonds - just how it was there. Stop in and check this place out - it makes you want to move to Italy...or Eataly. :-)

If I didn't find little warm- like thing on my son's plate, I would give 5 starts to this little casual restaurant., because food was delicious. We ordered Octopus Salad and after my son was almost done with it, he found this yakee warm-like thing as shown on enclosed picture.  Thing was not moving, i don't think it was alive., but we were scared and disgusted.    When we showed to our waiter, she offered not to charge for the salad and insisted that it was part of the octopus. She said that it was normal to find things like this in meals with octopus.   We believed her and paid for our meal, but more I think about, more bothers me. I just can't imagine people have no problem eating something like this, even if it was harmless.   Is that normal? Or I am too picky?
I go for the lunch buffet. Its right by work. The food is very good and the guys are nice.
Been here several times, and the food is very good. The only downside is the crowded weekend. Otherwise really good..

Not a fan. Yelp is usually very useful but in this case I was disappointed. The atmosphere was nice but the menu was short and misleading. I had the sunny egg with greens which was fine. My friend had the biscuit which was huge and they brought two mini mini jams on the side. The portions are strange as well as the prices (the biscuit only 5 dollars and a small glass of orange juice 5 dollars???!). Would need a longer menu with attractive options to go back.

West Haven's best kept secret. You may not think much about this bar while just doing a drive by, but I strongly suggest popping in. Whether you're a local or not, you will sit down feeling right at home. Excellent service and by far the cheapest drinks in town. They have a large backyard area where they host numerous charity events, as well as outdoor grilling and delicious homemade food. They also offer video bowling games and have a jukebox. Do yourself a favor and take a chance on this place. You will not be disappointed.
Amazing burnt ends, best slab  bacon I ever had in my life, great service and great good. I'm glad they expanded this is an awesome restaurant!!  They provide catering also.

Here with a group of six, wife and adult children with friends. Shared everything. Everything was awesome. No disappointments. Good spanish wines. Great atmosphere. Came here years ago when our son was attending UPenn, so fun to be back and glad to see it is still so good. Highly recommend.

Hands down the freshest, healthiest and tastiest chinese food i have ever had in my life. Their dishes aren't weighed down with grease like most chinese places. Everything is clearly made to order with the freshest ingredients. ***BYOB

This is perhaps an epitaph or nearly one. This restaurant was a regular monthly feature for my wife and I. The food reminded us of our Turkish holiday and the deserts were amazing too. Something has happened , either management had changed philosophy or they have opened another restaurant somewhere or the chef has left. We recently took our guests from London to this place after much praise only to be  completely let down. The Iskander Kebab was flat, the Kuzu Tandir was not as soft and cooked over slow charcoal fire and tasty as we have had before before and worst of all the lower portion of the Baclava were burnt to blackness and tasted of the burn. We perhaps will give this once-really-good restaurant , one more shot and then if the experience persists, will remove this place permanently from our list.

I've been here numerous time as I live in the area. My favorite is the ceviche, but ask them to add other seafood to it, costs a little more but so worth it with the hot sauce they have! The home made tortillas with duck comfit, slow cooked in the basement prep room, is fantastic.

We stopped by after dropping off my niece a few towns over. Not knowing the area ,we took a chance. I'm so glad we did. The bangers and mash were off the chain good, and I had the steak pie. Everything was super fresh, and I was delighted to wash it down with a Belhaven Ale - my absolute favorite beer, and they have a full line of bellhaven on tap. Rustic charm, friendly staff, and a game of futbol on the Tele. Do not miss out on this stop that is sure to be a new favorite.

I love the Shannon rose! Tons of space and short wait times on busy nights. The wrap around bar is great and the seating upstairs and down lets you choose what kind of atmosphere you want. Their boneless wings are great-I usually order a box to go with every meal and they package it up with tons of extra condiments and celery. Their service is ok. The main negative I have is it isn't very Irish. They do have an Irish section of their menu and a great decor, but there should be Irish music playing more often and more of an Irish theme inside.

Oh man!  After eating at Ramen Misoya this past Friday night, I was itching to eat ramen, again, today, so my boyfriend and I headed out to this place. This place is the bomb diggity, yo'!  It's a very small, hole-in-the-wall place.  Nice and cozy decor and a sense of "Japanese-Americanism" in the air.  I was already judging the place according to the ambiance, thinking it may not be good, but oh hell!  Was I wrong!  The appetizers and ramen, here, is bomb.com! I ordered Spicy Shio Ramen (comes with black garlic oil, chashu, green onion, and thin noodles).  I also ordered extra corn and extra bamboo shoots (Menma).  It was so deliciously good!  The broth was great, not too thick, yet not too thin, and very flavorful.  The chashu was excellent, fatty and juicy, just the way I like it, marinated to perfection.  Green onion was crisp and fresh.  The corn and bamboo shoots were alright, but added in together with everything else, it tasted good! I also ordered Spicy Gyoza.  This was your typical Japanese "gyoza," pan-fried, just the way that I like it (not that fried shit at inauthentic Japanese places that are Americanized...they have a lot of that stuff back home in Cali), and it was drizzled with Japanese spice.  On the side, there was gyoza dipping sauce.  Each Spicy Gyoza plate only came with about 7 pieces, but those 7 pieces were so delicious and went perfectly with my ramen! Lastly, I also ordered the "Curry Rice Set," so my ramen came with a side of curry over rice, in a bowl (with pickled ginger on the side).  This, my friends, was delicioso as well!  I ate it heartily and happily (lol, can't you tell that I simply LOVE food?!). The portions of these dishes were the perfect size, too; there wasn't so much that made you feel sickly, yet there wasn't too little that you were left craving for more.  The service here is also good, they have more manners and class here than at Ramen Misoya (where at Ramen Misoya, they kept asking us if we were done, 'cause I know they wanted to go home - the jerks!). A bit on the pricey side, but it's worth it, if you really want great ramen in NYC. They also opened another branch on 11/1 on 3rd Street.  I'll probably try that place later on, as well. Overall, I would highly recommend this place to family and friends who want some good ramen in NYC!  All hail, RAMEN-YA!  YATA!!!!!!!  Hai, oishii desu!!!!!!!!! Keep doin' yo' thang, you guys rock!

This joint used to be the ish...but alas times have changed. Sigh...my wife and I used to look forward to coming here on my off days for the chicken afghani biryani and the mix grill rice but the chicken isn't the same. Don't get me wrong, the rice is still outstanding but the last two times we went the chicken felt like tuna out of a can instead of the grilled feel. When we told them about it, the looked at us like a deer in headlights and put more "canned tuna chicken" on our plates...yeah thanks. Oh yeah they raised the price on the malai ice cream by 50 cents so now they're two bucks. You can get it for 50 cents on Newark Ave.

We had a fabulous meal at Han Dynasty tonight.  I know,I know, don't go out on a Monday night, but this place was great.  Our server, Josh, was great.  He walked us through the menu and explained the heat levels.  We ordered the two apps he suggested--Dan Dan Noodles and Dumplings in Spicy Oil.  Both were delicious and reflected the heat and portion that Josh described.  The Dumplings were spicy, but not over the top.  We had the Dry Pot Chicken to share for an entree.  HOT, but delicious.  Anybody can make something too hot to eat, but this dish had a satisfying,  whole mouth heat that wasn't painful but enjoyable. Definitely returning.  Hope Josh is working.
Good food, very fresh, and well prepared at reasonable prices by people who really try to please. Not a fancy place, just good.

Terrible. Very Bad service. Started a tab with them and they lost my credit card. After talking to the manager about this, he simply told me "These things happen" and continued to ignore. After trying to ask questions about where my credit card was I was kicked out. When i called my credit card they said that it was used that night at the tavern and I had all these charges from there. A bartender used my credit card for other customers purchases and tried to tell me they "lost" it. I do not recommend the tavern, service is very shady and they are not trustworthy.
Overpriced, outside, cheap ingredients...add to that one of the trashiest collections of patrons in the city, and you've got a real loser.

Came here on a Thursday night and the place was bumping. The vibe perfectly walks the line between a trendy place to meet up for drinks, a spot to watch a game or somewhere to take clients out for work. Solid crowd and sound system, too. Had the house burger and truffle fries. Will def come back.

I love this place!! food comes out fast, and its really delicious. Best of all. its so cheap!!! Here's my recommendation: Each time im coming in I order as follow: starter - Guacamole + Main- barbacoa taco and cactus taco. = yummy !!!!!

My boyfriend and I randomly came here one monday evening looking for a late lunch. He got the grilled chicken with cheese sandwhich with a side of fries, and I ordered the turkey burger on brioche with sautéed spinach and american cheese. ... Let me tell you, these were the BEST burgers/sandwiches we have ever had. The brioche buns were soft, the meat on both sandwhiches were juicy and tender, the spinach was lightly seasoned and the fries were handcut. As if that doesnt reel you in, the warm cozy luxurious decor and the impeccable wine selection add to the overall experience, making it a perfect reasonably priced but wonderful quality brunch, lunch, or dinner spot.

Just had lunch here and it was perfect. Me and my friend got the lunch for two. It was amazingly delicious, super filling and a steal at only 15 bucks. Jasmine was an excellent server. Funny, friendly and accommodating. Currently telling all my boos to come here!
Overrated... Really not that good.   Best thing was the kimchi.  Not worth waiting for.  Service was good. Gets crowded.  It's pretty much fusion, which means not good.

By far one of the best Halal Food Carts New York has to offer. I would have midnight munchies with friends and we would drive down to the city to grab us a platter of either a lamb, chicken, or combo. What makes it so tasty is the free pouring of sauce. When given our food we get to put the right amount of sauce in our platter before sitting on the side to eat or sealing it for later. The white sauce is delicious and a little hot sauce. There's also BBQ sauce if you want that sweetness flavor. They have been a popular choice towards new yorkers as well as foreigners who wants to see what the fuss is about. Best to go after drinking or when having the munchies for halal food. Enjoy your visit.

My boyfriend and I walked in because he was set on getting a steak dinner on our night out in Burlington. The food was good and the price was right. We loved everything but the fried calamari. The service was good and they have cheap wine! Would come back for sure!

Ok, maybe the food they carry is impressively abundant and true-to-the-core Italian but the place is so confusing. The fact that you have to get different food items in different sections just reminded me of old Soviet food stores. Also, the lines were kind of similiar: too much hype. I wish everyone would just go to smaller, much nicer historical places in Little Italy to get their Italian cravings fixed.

This is one of those great little finds in the middle of Little Italy/Chinatown.  I'm a local and love a good breakfast place that I can eat at once or twice a week. The food is excellent and reasonably priced for the area. The reason why am not giving it five stars is that the service was so painful this morning that it nearly ruined my appetite.   I walked up to the counter to order and the gentleman standing there, a blonde Australian guy,  said to me "can you hold on a second."  I said "sure." ...And then to my surprise right in front of me on the counter he was pulling his one dollar tips from the jar.   Five one dollar bills at a time and replacing it with a five dollar bill.  Then he did it again and again till there was 4 five dollar bills at the top of the tip jar.  I found it a bit strange or shall say I poor taste, but I thought okay.... maybe finally has a chance to do that.   I sat down and waited for my breakfast and notice three or four tables were piled high with dirty empty plates. One of them even had a tip on the table.  I did see the sign "bus your own table" but not everybody follows that and the sign is ONLY in the back.  Meanwhile the entire restaurant has dirty tables all over the place.  Customers we're coming in and wanting to sit down but there was dirty tables everywhere.  Even the table I was at was super sticky.   Then when my amazing food showed up and the same blonde Ozzie said "do you need anything else"?  I looked in the little silver bucket on the table and said "there's no fork here" and he said "oh you can get it over there."   I cannot believe how lazy this person is!   Half the tables are missing them.   It's a service business and he works for tips!  What a joke! It put a bad taste in my mouth.  Then I asked the guy across the table from me "is it just me or is the service here really bad."   He said, "I had the same experience with silverware."   I walked up to the counter and said "the knife table in the bucket is dirty."  Response he got was "you can get a new knife over there."  I've waitress for 10 years.  My response would've been "oh my gosh I'm so sorry " and walked 3 feet to hand a new knife. Now I'm willing to come back here because I'm a local and love Two Hands food.  Maybe the manager or the owner had a talk with the staff or got a new staff.  I hate to blame one or two bad experiences cause of one or two poorly hired choices.  One more time Two Hands And if I have another bad experience service I'll bring my breakfast appetite elsewhere.

The food here was Amazing!!! The menu is so unique and everything is so tasteful. Loved the ambiance and service. We had the kale salad, ricotta and fig spread, Brussels Sprouts Pizza and Fried Chicken. Its hard to get reservations here, so try to book a table in advance!

This restaurant has good reviews but for us was disappointing. Very crowded, we were sited at the center communal table. When the couple seated to our left side left the water glasses were not taken off the table and table not cleaned properly. The appetizers and main course tasted ok (nothing to remember) and were pricy (only cash accepted) for what is being offered. We ordered desert (I love sweets and I never miss deserts). Two puddings that were worse we ever tasted: thick bread with syrup.
Definite 5 stars! Service- great, food amazing. Very authentic and pretty impressive. Coming back soon. Also BYOB FYI that did not affect my judgement :)

Beer was ok, food was not so great. Would not go back unless it was for just beer. Service was good but it was slow and they had plenty of servers. Getting two stars cause they are not worth a return trip to me and food presentation was nothing like pictures. Cheese steak was small, no cheese, chips were crumbs and coleslaw cup looked like it was dropped on the floor then placed into basket. Hummus was not good as well.

I love the food here, and it is easily the best in plainsboro and West Windsor.....but they rarely get my order right. I am a frequent visitor, usually twice a week, and this makes the 4th time in a row where my order was incorrect. It is never a complicated order, always just one item, but usually something is wrong. These are simple mistake such as not giving any sauce on an order of buffalo wings, adding onions when I asked for none, forgetting to add mayo, or not heating up the sandwich. I really do like this place, but I think I need to start going elsewhere until I can have any amount of consistency in this delicious food.
Oh man, all the nomz your belly can handle. The portions are as big as the flavors. Get in on this deliciousness now you fools!

If you were a fan of Thai food, you must make a stop at this place. Newly decorated and expanded, offering one of the widest range of authentic food selections. If you can think of one dish that you would love to try, most likely the place serve it. Weak point is, slow service at times.

Amazing arroz con pollo. I came because i saw the restaurant on the foodnetwork and i was so excited. Seriously the arroz con pollo is great and HUGE. i took my dad here for his birthday and i love the way the waiters celebrate birthdays here :)

This bar is a favorite of mine and many of my friends. Definitely drop by for a pickleback and a some great eats. The only caveat I have about this place is that it's pretty packed around happy hour (but that describes most bars in that area). Late night, I've never had a bad experience here.

Never really had anything to say about this place but oh man, last night changed it all. Halloween 2k14 and the place is dead empty. Seated immediately by a cheery gal, skip on drinks and give several attempts at showing interest in placing food order. When it finally happens we are relieved, as we are near starving and had ordered an appetizer to take the edge off. Flash forward 25 mins to just the entrees and one being totally wrong after at least 2 reassurances of correctness. We mention the lack of it, where in the girl goes to the computer and enters it in. I said oh no thank you never mind. No "how is it?".  Nothing. Another person even delivered and picked up the empty plates. You need to be a bit more decisive on your choices of servers, because just being "alt cool"And playing biggie Smalls isn't always sufficient knowhaimean?

This place is so good. I went on Saturday around 8 and the wait time was around 10mins which is convenient because you can figure out what your going to order in that time. There drinks are really really good and strong but so tasty. I ordered the steak and collard greens which were so delicious like the fact I ate collard greens means it was amazing. The customer service was excellent and very quick. The lighting is pretty dim. They had sinks outside the bathroom which were really cute and they used natural soap which I appreciated. Overall this place is fantastic! Perfect date restaurant.
Great food, great service. The highlights are the Bacon Wrapped Apricots & The Smith Bar Steak.

I bought a sandwich platter for my daughter's birthday.  My sister-in-law is a vegan and I wanted to make sure she had something to eat other than fruit.  Lisa came to me and told me there had been a mistake; that the sandwiches were not vegan.  I ran to the table thinking someone had screwed up labeling the food on the table.  They had not.  I assured Lisa the sandwiches were vegan.  On three separate occasions during the party, she repeated that the sandwiches were delicious and couldn't believe they were vegan.  She removed the "Vegan" sign from the table so other people would eat them.  No one knew.  I tried them too and they were yummy. The next day, Lisa called to ask me where I had gotten them.  Thanks, HipCityVeg, for making me a hero!

We had French toast plus sausage and a Baby Mo which is one egg, potatoes and toast. We weren't impressed The French toast was undercooked and arrived long after the baby mo. The potatoes were burned and had an "off" flavor. Service was indifferent. Would not go back.

I have been going here for darn close to 40 years. They closed for a little bit , but now they are reopen. Since the reopening their food is even better then it was before. The have many varieties of burgers and it's quality beef. They also have various seafood & subs and things to tickle the kids fancy too. The help is and has always been friendly and you couldn't ask for better ownership.
This place was filthy. Dust all over the place including their coffee tables. The food wasn't tasty. I didn't even finish what I had b/c I was so disgusted with everything. Don't go.
Flies all over this place. Rude owner or guy making pizza. Pizza sits out for the whole day, you can tell by looking at it. Don't bother with this place. You will not be pleased.
Every time we hit up NYC, my wife has to get a slice from here. Great pizza, fresh ingredients, can't get any better than this.
I literally will drive an hour just for their curry chicken , Mac and cheese and collard greens. My favorite Jamaican restaurant in NJ hands down!!!

I always go through the negative reviews before eating any where. When i did i was surprised. once i actually tried one of their sandwiches i was when more surprised, the quality of the meat was good. the Price is GREAT The taste is GREAT the Iced coffee is GREAT Who can go wrong with an amazing sandwich for $5.50 - $6
Great  food in a upscale setting! Hearty food in large portions make this a winner! Close to Convention Center, Infinity Hall and across from movie theatre make this a great weekend spot.

So according to a lot of reviews here they say that Geno's is a rude and can be a racist establishment. I didn't experience that . I went at about 9pm with my Indian pal and there was zero rudeness or racism toward my friends accent. So very pleasant experience.  Keep in mind that it was late and nearly empty so the level of stress wasn't displayed amongst the employees which can happen in fast paced hours. Anyhow, the Steak Sandwiches were OK. Not out of this world. Average. But I suppose my curiosity got the best of me. So if your in tourist mode and you just need to go. Fine.   But it's not the best. Sorry to disappoint. And neither is Pat's right across the street. Just helping you not waste time.

This place is awesome! It's a bit of a chameleon in terms of the vibe - during Eagles games can feel like a sports bar, Tuesday night supper can feel romantic and hushed. The food is always amazing. Great mussels! They rotate a lot of dishes so you can't expect your favorite to always be available...if they ever get rid of the veggie wings I will be crushed! Cocktails are a bit pricey but I usually switch to beer after one and I'm still happy. I actually prefer this place to Loco Pez across the street.

We came there yesterday and were agreably surprised. The place is very nice and the food and the wene were just perfect for us, french! If you want to have a clear overview of french cuisine, you should totally go there. The brie with black truffle and the foie gras were delicious! Good chat with the chief-cook/owner who took time at the end of our dinner to tell us the history of his restaurant!

Very nice atmosphere, and the food was very good. Pizzas are nicely sized and Cannelloni was small but good, my date loved it. We are giving 4 stars mainly because the staff seemed a little spaced out. But that's okay because they were very nice when they were there. Wood fire oven and delicious pizza and atmosphere. We will be back maybe enjoy a drink. Thank you
Great pizza. Love the Baci gelato! Almond cookies are delicious :).  Great service.

Discovered this restaurant driving down Bedford Avenue one Saturday afternoon. Was a little skeptical going in. As I looked at the menu, I asked if certain items were available, to my surprise, everything I asked for was available. There were four of us, we sat down inside the restaurant. I order turkey wings, sweet potatoes and macaroni and cheese, others in my party had tilapia, with rice/beans and potato salad, smothered chicken with macaroni and cheese and collard greens, red velvet chicken and waffles. For dessert we had banana pudding and red velvet cheese cake. I must say, I was very impressed. Everything was seasoned and tasted great! Will be ordering for lunch today! A great place to eat and very generous portions!

We loved every minute of our experience at David Burke fabrick. We were seated right away, at a nice corner booth; the hostesses were friendly and smiling. Our server, Mark, was charming and attentive without being overbearing. The ambiance was interesting to look at (but not distracting) and it was quiet enough to have a conversation without straining to be heard while still feeling vibrant and exciting. Everything we ate was delicious. The drinks were wonderful (I had the Manhattan while my friend tried a couple of yummy lemony vodka concoctions), and we devoured the Avacado Panna Cotta, which was incredibly delicious and flavorful. We almost ordered a second one. :-) Every bite of our entrees (the burger and the mushroom pasta) was wonderful, and we had the incredible Burke-in bag hazelnut dessert... wow. (And clever name.) I don't usually eat sweets, but I tend to make exceptions at restaurants like this because they're usually exceptional... this proved me very, very right. After dessert we paid and headed upstairs to Spyglass, which was a true gem! Tiny but solid, with an exceptional view. It was the bartender's last night working there, so I'll opt not to judge this place by his less-than-stellar service; I would definitely come back for a future night of cocktails before or after dinner, as the view of the Empire State Building was stunningly great, even on a cold and rainy night. (Sunset there would probably be gorgeous, as the patio faces south and would give you great contrast in the sky.) Overall I was extremely happy with this recommendation and will absolutely come back the next time I'm in the city.
This is my first time here. I had M.I.G. wings. It was one of the best wings I had. Good place. Owner is very polite and really nice guy. Place is very inviting.
The place is really simple, old style, I think a new decor would be really inviting, but I still go there when I'm near by for a slice.  They really do make great pizza!

Found this cute little spot near Williamsburg and it is one of the best places I've eatin at. I took my girl friend on our anniversary and we both loved the food and the decor of this place. I got the Hungarian pie which was delicious and tender . My girl friend got the polish platter which had a wide variety of foods from dumplings to mashed potatoes. I definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a cheap meal with great food and large portions.
great food!

I went to Tuome as part of a self-guided tour of "what's new and up-and-coming" in NYC this fall. I wasn't disappointed, but nor was I really amazed. (Note - I just read the NY Times Review today and I'm a little surprised by the enthusiasm for things that I've seen a lot of before, but my complaints are the same, so maybe there's something there) Service - just fine, attentive but not overly so and quite friendly and enthusiastic about what they are serving Ambiance - spare and industrial/cabin hybrid. Not overly fussy but clearly on trend. Restaurant designers just can't seem to get enough of all those Edison bulbs these days... Wine - short but interesting by-the-glass list. Props for diversity. Food - we had a few small plates, sides and one main between two people... Deviled Egg: If there's one thing I'm absolutely going back for, it's this! LOVED IT Scallops: Perfectly cooked, like butter, but the veggie puree with it is too sweet and really distracts Octopus: I came specifically for this dish and found it was neither here nor there. Really well cooked, but both my dining partner agreed that the bacon distracted from the octopus and was too salty to compete with the delicate flavor of the foam Corn: Too sweet, a bit too liquidy, and nothing particularly special Sticky rice: Yummy comfort food, but nothing I haven't had before Conclusion: I'd go back to have those Deviled Eggs, and maybe try some of the other things the Times raved about... always worth a second shot, if it's even possibly to get in!
I love everything!
Wow, authentic Thai food that leaves you wanting more. Definitely love the staff and the quick take out time. Stop in for sure.

5 FING STARS BABY! Its so rare to find such a place these days. Very pleasant didning experience. We got a chefs menu. Got stuffed wall to wall. Very nice execution of veriety of different dishes that make you pallet come alive. And at a right price.
Loved this place.   Great food, atmosphere, and wine too!

Absolutely amazing, a splurge that was totally worth it! Came here on a rainy Saturday with the boyfriend. The ambiance is nice - the restaurant is lit well enough to see the food, the music is just the right volume where you can hear your date talk but not necessarily every other word being said at the other tables, and the décor is charming. This is not a party atmosphere, nor is it super overtly romantic, but the room has a definite warm glow-y buzz as the clientele seemed to be all couples and everyone seemed really into the food. The food is unbelievable - some dishes are mindblowing in their flavor combinations, others are for their high level of execution. I have never had better octopus or ice cream in my life, and the butternut squash tea soup with husk cherries blew my mind. The care in which both the chef and front of the house take in explaining the dish to each table shows how much pride they take in their craft. The service toes that perfect line between attentive and unobtrusive. The playlist rocks. The wine list is great as well, plenty of reasonable options. We will be back for another special occasion, if we can even score another reservation. Tip: We got there exactly at 8, but felt like we were a little behind as other tables had drinks and snacks. In the future, I'd try to get there around 7:45. Also, the neighborhood is charming and good for a post-meal walk!
Always amazing - even the leftovers. Go heavy on the white sauce and light on the red. For leftovers, I fry and egg and let the yolk serve as additional sauce. Out of this world amazing.

Hands down best Chinese takeout I've ever had. I used to work in Hartford and pick it up on my way home - now that I'm in Simsbury, I make the drive from Berlin to West Hartford to pick it up and it's STILL hot and delicious when I get home! Sonny is awesome and everyone there is so nice. And there's free green tea while you wait for your order :)

This place is a must if your passing thru. The sandwich takes the cake over having a cheese steak at pat or Gino's. The roast pork With broclirabe is the way to go. Throw some cheese on it and your all set. The flavor of this sandwich explodes in your mouth.
Terrific restaurant.  Good service and Food.  Both the seafood stew and the blackened salmon were the best I have ever tasted.  Try it you will not be disappointed.

Ok somebody has to say it. Those who gave this Thai restaurant anything more than 2 stars apparently has never been to Thailand nor tried authentic Thai food (or were just piss drunk when they ate the food). I am of the opinion that if you never traveled to a foreign country and tasted their food, you really shouldn't share your views on Yelp. You guys are just skewing the ratings system. Really, the food here is at best mediocre. Service, well, they managed to screw up my order every time I go. So at least they are consistent. I know, there are so many garbage Asian "restaurants" in Manhattan it is hard for those who has never been to Asia to tell the good ones from the bad. So I am going to help you guys out a bit since so many of you can't tell the difference between good and bad Asian food. Often, these restaurants' food has the same quality as McDonald's, but these "restaurants" have better furniture and are much more overpriced. I don't know why but you Manhattanites somehow love that combination (ie crappy food, nice decor, and an overpriced menu). As a general rule, you can tell an Asian restaurant has terrible food and is just trying to sell you an image (and not the quality of their food) when you see one or more of the below: 1) Hip, trendy music playing at the restaurant. 2) No (or very few) Asian patrons. Maybe one of two who are just mostly hanging out with their unfortunate non-Asian friends who are about to get ripped off with overpriced and mediocre food, but no groups of Asians (and come on, guys. This is a dead give away. If you haven't figure this one out already then god help you. As a general rule we Asians have a better idea where good Asian food is so you might want to follow us on this one instead of Tom and Dick from Ohio). 3) Food served on over-sized square plates. 4) Over-the-top Buddhism/Hinduism decor. 5) Strong smell of garlic (chef can't cook so he drenched everything in garlic, oil, and MSG and just fried it). For better and authentic Thai food try Jaiya (was there many yrs ago not sure how good they are now) or that little Thai restaurant in Woodside, Queens (right off the 7 train line). Totally forgot the name. Think it starts with an "S". Or befriend someone from Thailand and ask them where they go to get good Thai food. And stop messing up Yelp's rating system.

This place has the best Thai food I have ever had!! It is a must!! The sticky wings are to die for and try anything that has pork belly as the main. Anything on the menu is delicious!! It's a little out of the way but it certainly is well worth the trek. There could also be a ridiculous line but again it is well worth the wait.

If you are looking for a cozy, unique and authentic restaurant that serves delicious top tier food. This is the one. Perfect for a special occasion although I've been coming here with my wife quite often. But the portions are relatively small, even though it's perfect for me and my wife. If you are very hungry and have a big stomach to fill in, you should go somewhere else, otherwise you may end up ordering multiple dishes. And remember, BYOB, even better. I highly recommend this restaurant to every foodie.

The cassava cake is my all time favorite and their coffee taste great! I stop here whenever I am in the neighborhood. The employees are super friendly and it's always a pleasure to stop by their for a quick coffee and cake/muffin on the go.
Delicious foods! The menu was very good, taste was was so good and their prices was very good too. Were enjoyed the moment in this place especially their foods.

Meal: Dinner Type: Vegetarian Price: Around $50 for two Service: Good Recommended Dish: Jaipuri Kofta with plain Naan The food is good, but their dessert was a disappointment. And the restaurant was extremely packed and crowded. I would prefer to get the food delivered rather than eat there.

I have been going here for a few years now and it is my favorite restaurant. The food is amazing and the service is fast. All of the servers are very kind and remember you when you go back. The best Ethiopian food I have ever had!
My compliments to the chef! Flavors just right, food cooked perfectly. Service not so great but food worth the aggravation which I never say.
I love Wedge + Fig. I am always happy with the service I receive as their customer, and my meals are always fresh.

Delicious I order third of chicken beans and rice chicken noodle soup steam broc and fried shrimp dinner  amazing great customer service also. I couldn't believe great service in Jersey normally people are rude. Being we are from the south Im always looking for southern hospitality world wide. Must eAt here

Honestly, outstanding! Beautiful interior, gracious staff that is well-educated on each and every dish, and offers suggestions based on a number of appetites. Admittedly, I'm not well versed in Szechuan cuisine, but the flavor profiles in the appetizer and lunch dish I had were lovely. Started off with the wontons in chili sauce which were plump, and quite filling. Followed up with flounder in a pepper sauce that was delicate and flavorful and was accompanied by garlic sautéed string beans. This is certainly not Americanized Chinese food. For that, head to your local take out. Instead, go with friends to Shu, and enjoy some family-style, brilliantly-prepared Szechuan fare.
Great burgers, good selection of beer and booze.  bar gets crowded but good spot overall.
The scallion pancake, a spicy brisket bao and shoppe fries were excellent! The interior leaves a lot to be desired but they are quick and it's still good once I get it home.

Really nice intimate setting. Friendly staff. Really enjoyed the spaghetti and meatballs. As a fan of California wines I was disappointed that they only had Italian wines. Also had fresh burratawhich was delicious
Good food good service and good prices. The half carafe of red wine at happy hour nearly poured over the top. Great specials.
Better than Geno's

Loved this place! It was so laid back and a perfect atmosphere for a lunch break! I'm from Cali and heard that there was no good Mexican food in NYC- well, someone LIED! This place was great. I recommend the cactus taco- sounds weird, but go for it!
Great place with a very friendly bar! Bartender Ariel rocks!!! Will definitely come back!

If I could give a million stars I would. But unfortunately this piece of shit yelp only allows me to count to five. As for the food: bomb dot com As for the bar service: bomb dot double com As for the bar tenders: Marshall, he's a hunk of baltimore body and you won't regret talking with him. I also can attest to the fact that he is a trivia goddess. His questions will literally blow your mind. Jen, she is probably the sweetest and most genuine person who can tend to you for 1.5 hours while you satiate your innards with sweet liquor. Overall -- all around great people at this bar. So glad it's in my neighborhood.

Had such a great experience here just last week! I went with a group of 5 people and everything was perfect Three of us had the vegetarian wings and loved them so much. Another of us got the spinach salad and the last got the po boys. The atmosphere was great, the music was great, the service was supreme, and I can't wait to go back! I'm super picky about public restrooms, and theirs was mega clean :) Thanks guys
Came for lunch to go, I ordered the original and WOW, the food came quickly and definitely fresh, definite must try! #StuffedGrassFedMovement

What a place with great potential. Big space, but this place needs some soul. Music, or art maybe? A rearranging of the furniture? Not really sure what it is missing, it just felt like it was missing the ambiance or an inviting quality. And my first time eating there, met a friendly new face, but my adult grilled cheese was burnt on one side and soggy on the other and the tomato was as tough as gristle. I left feeling like I had been had. $10 down the drain.

I've had a really hard time finding decent ramen in Brooklyn. Ganso, despite being the hipsterest ramen joint you will ever see, takes the cake so far. Chuko, on the other hand, was not worth the wait. The pork bun was fine, and the veggies on it added a very refreshing brightness to the bun, but the pork itself was very small and just kind of there. Didn't really add to the flavor. I ordered the pork bone broth with roasted pork. (Kind of a fan of pork.) The broth was bland and much thinner than I'd ever expect of pork bone broth to be. Adding some of their really pretty good garlic oil helped a bit, but I'm a firm believer that a ramen dish should come out perfect from the kitchen. If the customer has to add something to give flavor, you're doing it wrong. The noodles, also bland, lacked the toughness I love in my ramen. And the eggs! I didn't even know it was possible for soft boiled eggs to taste like absolutely nothing! Quite surprising. The staff was incredibly friendly and they were a delight to interact with, but that's no substitute for the still-mythical perfect bowl of Brooklyn ramen. Also! I neglected to check yelp before coming here, and it seems that I probably should have tried the kimchee broth instead. I'll come back and try that some time. There's got to be Some reason there's apparently always a long wait to get in here.

Modo Mio is incredible.  I've been going here for years and it gets better and better each time!  I love there turista menu for $35.  What a value for such an amazing meal.  The sweetbreads were one of the best I've ever tried!

Poorly managed. Wait staff is good, but seems overwhelmed. We went for some apps before a concert...the room was less than half full, yet it was several minutes before we even saw a hostess/waitress and then another couple of minutes before we were seated. After 40 minutes the waitress apologized for the delay and said it would be another 10 minutes before our food would be out. Really?! The manager apologized and blamed the cook and too many room service orders. Honestly...room service doesn't trump patrons at tables! We left without getting our apps, without paying for drinks and with two breakfast comps. We actually got food for breakfast, but again they just aren't organized. It's a buffet with bacon and sausage but they have one cook preparing everyone's eggs. He was quick and good, but we heard him say to a coworker that he hadn't had a break in 4 hours and walked out. Suggestions: put plates where the line forms for the buffet (instead of the other side of the room), put out steamers of scrambled eggs and pancakes...save your cook for special orders and most important...hire a new manager who accepts responsibility for the service and doesn't blame the employees!

So I need to start this review with one premise...I've never reviewed anything on Yelp. Frankly...no one is deserving of my time unless they wow me. Well, I've been wow'ed!! Kenko just opened a week ago from what the hostess told me.  It's a darn shame they didn't open sooner. This place has fantastic food, a great decor and amazing service. Thanks to Kenko I've found a regular sushi place.
Once again delighted to be there! Great service. Delicious rolls. Thanks Hendra! See you soon!
Great food; great value. Huge portions and delivery. What's not to like?

Not that this place needs another glowing review, but it really lives up to the hype. Delicious, fresh food and a nice atmosphere. The tasting menu left me perfectly full (with just enough room for dessert), and overall, it was one of the best meals I've ever had in the city.
Cool place....lots of good food!!
Love this place and all the options.  The amish stands are great.  One of the best places in Philly to visit!
yum yum ! great experience at this place . food was very good .drinks were even better . excellent Mexican spot

I was looking forward to this because of the yelp reviews, but was extremely disappointed. The burger we got was extremely burnt and inedible. The chicken parm was pretty awful. The pasta was cold and barely had sauce on it. The chicken was overcooked and could barely be cut with a knife. They ruined our Friday night.

Serviceable asian inspired food. As mentioned by others, the portions are ridiculously small. The crispy tofu consisted of three pieces of tofu served on a small bed of sprouts. The shrimp were two shrimp and a few sprouts swimming in a bowl of coconut milk. Beyond the small size of the portions, neither dish was especially remarkable. Also, the wait between courses was unconscionable. I came close to canceling the last course and asking for the check.

If you are looking for authentic, comforting and yummy Italian food, look no further! I just moved to the city and one of the first things I wanted to do was find my go to Italian restaurant. I come from a family of Italian cooks so I would say I am pretty well versed as to what is quality. My boyfriend and I ordered the Chicken Parmesan as delivery and it was amazing! The portion was HUGE and the sauce was nice and light (the way it always should be), with perfect flavor. I will definitely be back for a dine in experience!

Glasserie is definitely worth the trek to north Greenpoint. I came here with a date last weekend and sat at the bar. The tall, blonde female bartender was so friendly and recommended an excellent glass of wine. I had the griddle bread (delicious) and the lamb in a red sauce. The restaurant has a great atmosphere, friendly and attentive staff. Great spot for a date or if you just want to treat yourself to a delicious middle eastern dinner.

Chez Moi is a fine choice for brunch or dinner. The atmosphere is intimate and relaxing. The menu is simple, however it has enough options to satisfy a wide range of tastes. The service is consistently friendly and professional. A great choice for an evening out or a saturday afternoon cocktail.
Forget the line and don't worry about finding the right one (they're all pretty good).  This is definitely a stop worth visiting if your in the area.
food is great. The best pizzza/flatbread i have ever had.

I'm new to this neighborhood and decided to check this place out. Nothing short of amazing! Very quaint little place that was packed and could only fit the 2 of us at this little counter facing an open kitchen. I loved it because I could watch the Chef's cooking. We ordered the cauliflower which was to die for, the kale salad and spaghetti. Dishes were perfectly portioned so you didn't feel over full. The waitress Katie sent over a complimentary plate of Brussel sprouts since we had such little room (man sitting behind us sat very far out) best Brussel sprouts I have ever eaten!! Whole experience was top notch. Food incredible and ambiance was perfection. I will be coming back here again again and again! Oh and be sure to try the apple brownie, you won't be disappointed!

Stopped in on 11/5 to try the burgers with 2 of my business buddies as I had seen a review in a local restaurant blog earlier that day. The review was spot on.  We ordered the Bacon Jam Burger, Montclair Blue Cheese and Bacon Cheeseburger.  All were freshly prepared and served with fries.  I suggest you kick it up and go for an order of the bacon jam fries as they are outstanding!  While dining we had the opportunity to chat with the owners for a while.  Some really great people with a passion for creating and serving delicious "stuffed" burgers!

I love this place and its food!! I tried many thai places as it is my favorite food, but this one beats them all for price/quality! Delicious food, great ambient and cheap price for lunch (8$ for appetizers and big portion of entree). I am recommending it to everyone and will definitely go back!

Generally have enjoyed our meals at Olea which means everyone else has too, so they've become too busy for a last minute meal. Unfortunately they aren't worth the long wait, and the last time we went charged us extra for seconds on endive leaf to use as a dip which we had substituted for bread with the dips. Come on people, how much is endive leaf!

Rude service. The white blond guy that sits people is a bit weird and not very professional. I ve been there several times and always gives me a difficult time. Even if there are empty places he makes me/us wait without a reason. Last time he told me there was 45 minutes waiting, however the couple behind me was told that the waiting time was only 20 minutes... But the Udon is great, so I keep going :)
Excellent food, atmosphere and service. Highly recommend the minestrone soup, the tuna and tomato panini and the bolognese. If you have space after, get the gelato!

Come early for brunch or else the pickings are slim. They make a mean chocolate chip macadamia cookie (3.50). Spend the money, its worth every penny. The quiche was very nice and the hot chocolate was a steep $4...shldve gotten a cookie! The decor is beautiful, rustic and charming French parisian. Not a lot of space at all. Also it gets very crowded with two people serving. The owners are in the forefront serving, beautiful couple, polite and friendly.
Pancakes: Great Huevos rancheros: Pretty good (but cold every time I order them!) Service: A bit slow given how crowded things get

If you like fresh, homemade food- this is your new favorite restaurant.  Great food! BOYB.  Beautiful space. They have just finished doing a soft open and the place is cranking! Worth the wait.   Give it a try.  You won't be disappointed.
Had the arroz con Apollo and tostones, it was simply amazing! Recommended by a friend and so glad we took the time out to visit. Can't wait til next time!

My boyfriend made a reservation 30 days in advance (Take Root policy) through Amex concierge service. Somehow our information was taken down incorrectly. Apparently, not only do you have to make a reservation 30 days prior and give your complete credit card information in case of no show, you also have to confirm your seat via phone AND email the week of the event. Because they had our phone number down wrong and couldn't get a hold of us, we showed up to eat and were denied seats. The couple who run the restaurant offered no apology for the mishap and when we expressed our disappointment and told them it was my boyfriend's birthday, they could only shrug their shoulders. We were the first guests to arrive 20 minutes early for the dinner. There are a million different ways the owners could have made a bad situation into a comical, happy one. Offer an apology, give a free glass of wine, guarantee a dinner another evening - they need a lesson in customer service. I don't care how amazing the food is - the attitude and atmosphere carry more weight. They are in the business for the wrong reasons if they don't care about the happiness of customers. My boyfriend has an uncommon name. One google search could have led the owners to the correct phone number or email address - we live in a modern world! We've never tried the food, but we already hate the place and will never return. We decided to go to French Louie instead! We told the host about our bad experience with Take Root and they gave us free champaign! Exemplary customer service. Go to French Louie! Good food AND good people.
Omg the cinnamon apple infused rum - you can stop drinking anything else. Nothing will compare to this magical wonderment.

As always great service...only issue we had we were asked if we would like to try the wine of the night...my wife had two drinks... $45.00 for two glass of wine...no one said 22.50  a glass very unprofessional. ...manager said he would take care of us next time for misunderstanding. ..will see!!!! Update On issue...I emailed complaint and got call from manager on that night...he told me next time we were in...he would take care of us...apologized and seemed sincere....went there tonight and spoke with manager justin...he said he would cover our appetizers...a total of $9.00....which mean we still paid 25.00 more then we should have last time.. we had a nice time...when time to pay...the appetizers had not been removed from our bill...we said nothing and paid....so much for making it right!!!!! The saga continues...Justin called me the other night...said he realized he did not credit us the appetizers as promised after seeing my old email. ..felt real bad...said he is sending us gifts cards to make up for the series of mistakes...seems to be trying to make it right We cheers to justin....he made it right with a generous gift certificate as he stated he would proving he is a man of his word. ...cant wait to go back enjoy the great ambiance...drinks...and service...bottom line justin made a couple wrongs and right

Looks like it's a family owned/ran type of place. We went on a Saturday night craving for some kbbq but unfortunately they were not offering the tabletop version. The service was great, the food not so much. For the price the portions were very small and the side dishes were few.

Enjoyed the food.  It was very busy but We had great service.  Make sure u go with a group or you will have lots of food left over!  The only complaint was it was very loud but overall a good experience.
Bleu sushi is the best sushi in Philadelphia! The incredible food combined with the welcoming atmosphere and outstanding owner makes for an awesome experience. Highly highly recommend!

Great tasty food ( I ordered the steak salad, so good) and friendly staff - just a little bit busy and noisy during weekends. I celebrated my bday, so they came with a piece of delicious cake with a candle in it, that's sweet and really good service.

Over-rated.  Not worthy of an appearance on Philly's Best lists. Small portions, pretentious. Honestly, sliced cucumbers with artisan salt doesn't thrill me. 3 pierogies pretending to be ravioli on a plate do not an entree make. Very disappointing.
Love it Here! The food is great and the Little shops have something for everyone! a Must if visiting Philly downtown!

I was visiting my friends in New York and they recommended me this place...I went for it and you know what?? NO REGRETS! Absolutely delicious food and great service! I ordered their Lentil salad with a couple of stix, my friends got their lunch specials...the atmosphere, the music, the food - everything was great! And their COFFEE!!! Their coffee is amazing. I was especially impressed by the service. Don't get to see a good service in LA that much... Anyway, STIX is now one of my favorite places in NY:)

Are here for the first time yesterday and was sooooo PLEASED!!! delicious food, great service, and DELICIOUS food!!! We ordered the pancakes which are the best pancakes I've ever had, the eggs Benedict which were PERFECT and one of their specials for the day. Each dish was mouth watering and I'm already dreaming of having their pancakes again.
Amazing staff,  friendly owners, brunch is delicious,  and the mystery beer and shot are really fun.
This is one of my absolute favorite places to go for lunch the people are friendly and the food is delicious. Also I love the fact that it has the old fashioned glass coke bottles.

Very pleasant dinner for our first time at this rustic spanish eatery. Our party of 4 had 8pm tix to a Saturday night show at NJPAC. Not looking to be rushed we made a 6pm reservation at Spanish Pavilion because it was recommended by a friend for having good food and being less than a mile from the show. And all turned out to be true. We had the pick of our table when we arrived at ten to six, but the place quickly filled up by 7pm. We started with martinis and then shared a bottle of Tempranillo for dinner. Appetizers were the queso manchego frito (excellent!), clams with herbs in butter sauce (a special, not on the reg menu was delicious & great dipping sauce with bread), pork kabobs (juicy & tasty), artichoke dish (in a lemon white wine sauce, also very good) and crab stuffed mushrooms (they were decent but too much stuffing made them not as flavorful). For dinner we ordered two entrées to share which included a house salad for all - house dressing was a sweet & spicy catalina style -- very tasty. Our entrées were the skirt steak cooked rare (very delicious!) and the paella for two (but it easily could feed four. also very delicious, and plenty to take home for lunch the next day). Our service was very attentive, clearing and resetting plates with new utensils and constant refilling of our water glasses. The food was not fast, but we do not like to be rushed so there was always something to eat and drink which was perfect. We told our waiter we were going to a show and he remembered to bring the bill with plenty of time to depart. This allowed us to use the restroom which was also very clean. We did not have time for coffee & dessert but truthfully we were all so full we wouldn't have been able to eat it anyway. Upon leaving, the manager Jerry asked us how everything was. We said great! And got to talking and he wound up letting us leave one car of our cars in his parking lot for the 90 mins we were at the show. Such a bonus to a great evening! Thanks to Jerry and all the staff at Spanish Pavilion, we will tell our friends and definitely be back again real soon!  -H.W.
Drinks better than food most of the time.  Strange location!

Great vibe with a super comfortable atmosphere. Pickles are fresh and served quickly but the Dill pickle wasn't what we expected both times we visited they taste way more sour than fresh and crisp. Pickled Beets and Carrots are excellent. The biscuits are delicious - not what you expect from at traditional biscuit but awesome and served with insanely delicious toppings on the side - I think it's a maple butter that knocked my socks off. Good drinks but the bartender was pretty terrible, which sadly takes off two stars. She chatted with a regular and never once asked us if we'd like another cocktail even though we sat at the bar right near where she was chatting. We ended up getting another drink someplace else. Will definitely go back.

While workshopping this review, my wife asked: "Is it possible that you loved the pho so much because maybe you were extra hungry and maybe hungover?" My response: "That is the whole point of enjoying good pho--you only get out the pho experience what you put into it!" While attending a conference in Burlington, I got to try many different restaurants and bars--this town has a lot going for it from a tourist's perspective! At the end of the ~4 day conference, most of my fellow attendees headed back to their respective homes. (I was stuck in Vermont for one more day because, welp, it's not particularly easy to fly in and out of Burlington *International* if you're not coming from/going to the East Coast.) With my extra night of eating, I was free to travel a bit further out of downtown than possible with conference friends, and I was able to eat whatever cuisine met my fancy. I saw Pho Hong at about 1.2 miles out of downtown--a hike, but not too far. I called to check their beer selection: No beer! But they allow Bring Your Own Beer [this is completely foreign to me, coming from an alcohol-fearing place like Utah.] Luckily, I was standing next to the local organic co-op, which offered a variety of craft brews (I think I got a couple brewed in Vermont and a brewery in Brooklyn NY). With those details worked out, I set out on my walk to Pho Hong. The walk from downtown takes you through some interesting neighborhoods. Not too bad, but I had a few drunken (young?) folks holler at me from their patios. When I got to Pho Hong, I had to wait 30-40 minutes. No big deal, I as I arrived during peak business. I enjoyed my beers, the pho was hot, spicy, delicious. Pretty sure I got the Pho Tai (with strips of beef flank). I ate my soup so quickly, it's hard to remember. But it was satisfying and delicious, and all that much more so because of the aforementioned nights of drinking with friends and colleagues and the walk through Burlington to get to the soup. Yum!
Incredible Pad Thai and ribs!!! Great place with cosy look and friendly staff. No reservations allowed but usually the line moves fast. Don't forget to drink a Singha!

Just threw my husband's surprise 30th at Pier 76 last week. To say that everything was perfect is an understatement! A week later I am still getting phone calls and texts about how good the food is. Guests even begged to take home doggy bags! Between buffalo chicken rolls, Pizzas (Mac and cheese was a fan favorite), pasta, salad, chicken franc, sausage and peppers and zeppoles, the food seemed endless and no one went home hungry!! The staff was excellent, attentive and friendly. Both the bartender and the waitresses made sure everyone was happy and enjoying themselves. The owner Joe made sure everything ran smoothly! I couldn't have been more happy with the outcome of the party. I would definitively recommend going to pier for your next celebration. Whether it be for dinner or for a party, Pier 76 is the place to go for great food and great drinks.
Kudos in every aspect! The staff was friendly,attentive & knowledgeable. The food is on another level. Not what one would expect for an American Restaurant. This a foodies best kept secret!
Fantastic food, cute space, and friendly owners! Definitely worth the visit.

Came here during the first weekend it was open and I had a mysterious 20 dollar up charge on my bank account. I tipped the waiter 17 dollars in cash then they took an additional 20 out. I spoke to the manager and she granted me a 30 dollar credit which I never used. The food is good and I like the look of the place. The meat is tasty with the added sauces or alone, as well as the seafood. The wings are very good too. Our waiters were good the few times we came here and the tipping situation never came about again which is good. Will continue to come here!
Philly breakfast sandwich was disgusting. Bread/bun was way too big with no vegetables (lettuce tomato etc) and scrapple itself was gross. Should have gone to china town
